Retort.note: Artificer to 11 for the third-level slots and Restorative Reagents, then Bard 6, then Paladin 3. It has no Extra Attack and never swings — the routine is cantrips with two levelled casts a fight, and Alchemical Savant adds Intelligence to one roll of anything acid, fire, necrotic, poison or healing. Build-time picks: roughly a third of the pool to damage, the rest to control and outward healing.
Retort.strength: It is the only chassis in the roster that pays for itself in camp supplies: free Lesser Restoration, six elixirs a rest and Restorative Reagents' temporary hit points on the partner directly offset a long rest costing 120+ supplies, which is the resource a two-body party actually runs out of.
Retort.wants: Damage, and a body that can stand in front of it. st never clears 1 and it has no Extra Attack in any act; what it brings instead is the pair's rescue and its own armour.
uncertain: Artificer's level-1 saves are Intelligence and Constitution, which is exactly what Lone Wolf's +4 wants to boost — dedup would leave a proficient set of two. Lone Wolf is therefore placed on Intelligence and Wisdom, and one feat buys Resilient (Dexterity), to reach a disjoint four covering all of Wis/Con/Dex. That trap costs every Artificer in this batch a feat.

Enhanced Weapon's +1/+2 to attack and damage is scored as inert, on the same reading that retired Kensei's Sharpen the Blade: axis-rubrics.md's gear constant k already assumes the act's enchanted kit (+3 by Act III), and crediting an infusion that produces the same number would charge for it twice.
Experimental Elixirs roll a random effect, so no specific benefit is scored from them; only Restorative Reagents' flat 2d6 temporary hit points on the drinker enters the durability pool.

Resistant Armor is credited as a proportional layer at a 0.30 share of incoming damage (x1.18) from Act III. It grants resistance to one chosen type out of ten, so the share is a judgement, not a reading.

Alchemist's Death Ward arrives at Artificer 13 and Greater Restoration at 15; this build stops at 11, which is why rsc holds at the rung-3 ladder line (Revivify at Artificer 5 plus free Lesser Restoration) rather than reaching prevention.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee weapon hit; it adds no roll of its own and has no area form.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Rides one melee weapon hit; no area form.

riders.name: Crimson Rite (1d4)
riders.single_axis_reason: The Rite adds its Hemocraft die to each weapon hit; it has no area delivery.

riders.name: Lightning Bolt
riders.single_axis_reason: One action-slot of Lightning Bolt; the weapon routine on the other seven carries st.

Bulwark.note: Artificer to 11 for Arcane Armor, Extra Attack and Perfected Armor, then Paladin to 7 for Aura of Protection and its oath aura, with a two-level Blood Hunter tail for a Fighting Style and a Crimson Rite. Build-time picks: the Guardian model for its level-9 reaction, a greatsword rather than the Thunder Gauntlets (which need empty hands), and Divine Smite off the combined pool. Only five feats — no class in this split reaches 13, and Blood Hunter 2 collects none at all.
Bulwark.strength: Perfected Armor is a reaction that yanks an attacker off the other body and drags it 6 m toward this one, and Lone Wolf grants a second Reaction so it can be used and still leave one in reserve. In a party of two there is no spare body to soak a focus, so pulling the focus is the closest thing to a taunt the game allows.
Bulwark.wants: Damage and skills. st falls to being outrun by Act II and never recovers, and skl bottoms out at 1 — this body is armour, an aura and a rescue button, and it needs a partner who kills things.
uncertain: Artificer's level-1 saves are Intelligence and Constitution, which is exactly what Lone Wolf's +4 wants to boost — dedup would leave a proficient set of two. Lone Wolf is therefore placed on Intelligence and Wisdom, and one feat buys Resilient (Dexterity), to reach a disjoint four covering all of Wis/Con/Dex. That trap costs every Artificer in this batch a feat.

Enhanced Weapon's +1/+2 to attack and damage is scored as inert, on the same reading that retired Kensei's Sharpen the Blade: axis-rubrics.md's gear constant k already assumes the act's enchanted kit (+3 by Act III), and crediting an infusion that produces the same number would charge for it twice.

The greatsword configuration is chosen over the Guardian model's Thunder Gauntlets, which count as weapons only while the hands are empty. Rule 3 forces the pick; the Arcane Armor is still worn for its heavy-armour proficiency and the level-9 reaction.
`dark-augmentation` is not authored: ledger-schema.md places it at Blood Hunter 2 but bloodhunter.md's level table puts Dark Augmentation at class level 10, and this dip is two levels.

Five feats is the real constraint on this chassis and is easy to miscount — floor(11/3) + floor(7/3) + floor(2/3) = 3 + 2 + 0, with no class reaching 13. Resilient (Dexterity) plus the half-feats for Strength 22 consumes most of it.
Resistant Armor is credited as a proportional layer at a 0.30 share of incoming damage (x1.18) from Act II.

riders.name: Sneak Attack 2d6 x2
riders.single_axis_reason: Sneak Attack rides an existing weapon roll, adds no instance, and has no area form.

riders.name: Sneak Attack 2d6 x2
riders.single_axis_reason: Rides an existing roll; no instance, no area form.

riders.name: Sneak Attack 2d6 x2
riders.single_axis_reason: Rides an existing roll; no instance, no area form.

riders.name: Lightning Bolt
riders.single_axis_reason: One action-slot of Lightning Bolt; the weapon routine on the other seven carries st.

Fieldkit.note: Rogue is the level-1 class — four skills and Expertise on two of them at character 1, where a Rogue dip taken later grants one skill and no Expertise — then Artificer to 11 and Bard 6. Build-time picks: the Infiltrator model, so the Lightning Launcher is the weapon and the hands stay empty, Rogue's Expertise on Perception and Investigation, and Bard's on Persuasion and Deception.
Fieldkit.strength: Five expertised skills on a body that also wears Arcane Armor and has Extra Attack — in a party of two, one character has to carry the whole campaign's check load and this one does it without being the fragile half. The Infiltrator's glimmer also hands the partner a target that is easier to hit.
Fieldkit.wants: Single-target damage. Sneak Attack stops at 2d6 on a three-level Rogue and the Lightning Launcher is one attack per Action, so st falls to being outrun by Act III; it wants the partner to be the one that kills.
uncertain: Enhanced Weapon's +1/+2 to attack and damage is scored as inert, on the same reading that retired Kensei's Sharpen the Blade: axis-rubrics.md's gear constant k already assumes the act's enchanted kit (+3 by Act III), and crediting an infusion that produces the same number would charge for it twice.
Resistant Armor is credited as a proportional layer at a 0.30 share of incoming damage (x1.18); it grants resistance to one chosen type out of ten, so the share is a judgement rather than a reading.
The Infiltrator model requires empty hands, so this body carries no shield and takes no off-hand attack; its instance count comes from Extra Attack plus one reaction attack a round.

Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Constitution and Wisdom here rather than on Intelligence, because Rogue is the level-1 class and already supplies Dexterity and Intelligence — that is the one Artificer split in this batch where the save set costs no feat.
ctrl_a falls from 2 to 1 between Acts II and III with nothing having changed: Hypnotic Pattern is third-tier and the Act III row prices area control at sixth to ninth.

Batterypiece.note: Artificer to 17 for Fortified Position, then a Bladesinging 3 tail for light armour and Bladesong. It never makes a weapon attack: the routine is cantrips with two levelled casts a fight, and Arcane Firearm adds 1d8 to one damage roll of every spell it casts, cantrips included. Build-time pick: half the pool to damage, the Eldritch Cannon kept in Protector mode when the partner is exposed and Force Ballista otherwise.
Batterypiece.strength: From Artificer 15 it fields two Eldritch Cannons off a single action, and the summon is built on the Ranger's Companion template so it resummons without a daily charge. With a Homunculus infusion on top, two characters put four bodies on the field — which is what Listo's added enemy counts are tuned against.
Batterypiece.wants: Single-target damage and a front line. st is 1 in every act; the cannons soak and the Fireballs clear, but nothing here removes a boss.
uncertain: Enhanced Weapon's +1/+2 to attack and damage is scored as inert, on the same reading that retired Kensei's Sharpen the Blade: axis-rubrics.md's gear constant k already assumes the act's enchanted kit (+3 by Act III), and crediting an infusion that produces the same number would charge for it twice.
Resistant Armor is credited as a proportional layer at a 0.30 share of incoming damage (x1.18); it grants resistance to one chosen type out of ten, so the share is a judgement rather than a reading.

Neither the Eldritch Cannon nor the Homunculus contributes damage: axis-rubrics.md rule 2 excludes summons and extra bodies from the damage axes, and they are scored on `act` instead. That is the whole of why a chassis whose headline is two cannons reads st 1 in every act.

The Protector cannon mode granting temporary hit points to allies is what carries rsc to 4 from Act II, on the reading that a summon acting on its own turn is a no-action outward source. It is the rung-4 ladder clause rather than the act row.

`bladesong` is authored from Act III for Bladesinging 2's bonus to Constitution saves. Whether it and `flash-of-genius` combine as two partials into one blanket is the renderer's call, not authored here.
Lone Wolf's +4 is placed on Intelligence and Wisdom to dodge the Artificer int+con overlap, and one feat buys Resilient (Dexterity).

riders.name: Arcane Jolt (2d6 Force)
riders.single_axis_reason: Arcane Jolt fires on one magic weapon hit and is a single roll; its alternative mode is healing, not area damage.

riders.name: Arcane Jolt (2d6 Force)
riders.single_axis_reason: One magic weapon hit, single roll; the alternative mode is healing.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee weapon hit; it adds no roll of its own and has no area form.

riders.name: Fireball off the Wizard pool
riders.single_axis_reason: One action-slot of Fireball; the weapon routine on the other seven carries st.

Ironsmith.note: Artificer to 11 for Arcane Jolt and the Steel Defender's later upgrades, then Wizard 6 for a real spell list, then Paladin 3 for Divine Smite off the combined pool. Battle Ready makes Intelligence roll attack and damage — Enhanced Weapon supplies the magical-weapon prerequisite from the class itself — so this is one of the few genuinely single-stat bodies in the roster. Build-time picks: medium armour and a shield, Enhanced Defense on the armour, and 30% of the pool to Smites.
Ironsmith.strength: One ability does attack, damage, spell DC, saves and the Arcane Jolt allowance, which means the pair fights over one tome and one amulet instead of three; and the Steel Defender's Deflect Attack imposes disadvantage on anything swinging at the *other* body, which is a permanent third-party bodyguard in a party that has no third body.
Ironsmith.wants: Damage that scales. Four attacks with no scaling rider is the rubric's own 'being outrun' row, and this body reads 1 on st from Act II — it wants a partner whose single-target output actually grows.
uncertain: Warding Bond is authored on `redirect` from Act I. ledger-schema.md names Battle Smith 5 as one of only five routes to the spell and says the Listo Master Spells Patch hands it over outright at that level, so this body carries it for the whole run — it is the only chassis in this batch with a bond.

Artificer's level-1 saves are Intelligence and Constitution, exactly what Lone Wolf's +4 wants; Lone Wolf is placed on Intelligence and Wisdom instead and one feat buys Resilient (Dexterity), which is what reaches a disjoint four. That trap costs every Artificer here a feat.

Enhanced Weapon's +1/+2 is scored as inert — the gear constant k already assumes the act's enchanted kit, and crediting the infusion would charge for it twice. Battle Ready still needs it, but only as the magical-weapon prerequisite.
The Steel Defender contributes no damage (rule 2 excludes extra bodies) and is scored on `act`; its Deflect Attack is scored on rsc as prevention aimed at the partner, not on this body's own dur.
Resistant Armor is credited as a proportional layer at a 0.30 share of incoming damage (x1.18) from Act II.

Frenzy.note: Barbarian 1 first for Strength and Constitution saves and the d12, then straight to 14 for Retaliation; Fighter 3 and Rogue 3 are bolted on at 15–20. Configuration scored: greatsword, Great Weapon Fighting from the Fighter dip, Reckless Attack every turn, Frenzy up in every fight. It gave up all armour above medium, every spell list, and any answer at all to a crowd.
Frenzy.strength: Lone Wolf's second Bonus Action is what makes this body: Frenzied Strike fires twice a round for free, and the second Reaction turns Barbarian 14's Retaliation into a second free attack. Six to seven and a half swings a round at permanent Reckless advantage is the highest single-target rate any melee chassis reaches, and the whole engine is at-will — nothing here is spent against a 120-supply long rest.
Frenzy.wants: A partner that answers crowds: this body's AoE is a flat zero in every act, and its control is a single frightened enemy until the Battle Master dice arrive at 17.
uncertain: Frenzied Strike is priced at 2 uses a round on Lone Wolf's two Bonus Actions. The class file records no once-per-turn cap, but I could not confirm from the installed pak that the ability lacks one; at one use a round the Act I ratio falls from 2.18 to 1.65 and the rung from 5 to 4.
Retaliation (Barbarian 14) is priced at 1.5 reaction attacks a round — 2 against a crowd taking three hits, 1 against a boss taking one — blended on the act's MIX weights.

Reckless Attack is scored as routine advantage (×1.35 on the raw) and its cost is carried on `dur` as enemy advantage against this body (p_hit 0.60 → 0.84). Both halves move together; scoring one without the other is worth a rung either way.

Rogue 3 (Thief) is close to dead weight here. Sneak Attack needs a finesse or ranged weapon and this body swings a greatsword, and Fast Hands' third Bonus Action cannot be scored because the format caps bonus actions at 8 (2 a round). The split buys a feat and Cunning Action and little else.
No damage feat is assumed, per §1's par convention. A Great Weapon Master build would read roughly one rung higher on `st` in Act I and II.

Skald.note: Barbarian 1 first for the saves and the d12, Berserker at 3, Barbarian to 11 for Relentless Rage, then Blood Hunter 3 for Crimson Rite and Bard 6 (College of Lore) for Expertise and three free proficiencies. Configuration scored: greatsword, Rite of the Flame, Reckless Attack every turn; no class reaches 13, so this pays only six feats.
Skald.strength: It is the only Berserker that can read a trap and talk to a shopkeeper: Lore's three proficiencies plus two Expertise put a raging Barbarian on Perception and Investigation totals a duo normally has to buy with its other half. Bardic Inspiration is a class feature rather than a spell, so it keeps working while raging and hands the partner a d8 in a party where there is nobody else to hand it to.
Skald.wants: A partner that carries Charisma and the pair's concentration slot — this body's own spell list switches off the moment it rages, and its area damage is zero.
uncertain: Rage switches off spellcasting, so the Bard 6 slot table contributes nothing to damage and `to_damage` is 0 in both acts that have one. The slots are still real between fights and out of Rage — Goon's overhaul makes ending Rage a free action in this build — which is why `rsc` is 2 rather than 0, but that costs a Rage charge every time and is not a routine.
The split names no Bard college. I scored College of Lore, because the three free proficiencies are the whole point of the `skills` niche; Swords or Valour would drop `skl` to 1 in every act.
The split names no Blood Hunter order either. Scored as a plain Crimson Rite (hemocraft 1d4 at Blood Hunter 3, +2.5 a hit, paid in hit points).
Frenzied Strike is priced at 2 uses a round on Lone Wolf's two Bonus Actions; see the caveat on the front-line Berserker.

Surge.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of Wild Magic) / Ranger 3 (Beast Master)
Surge.note: Barbarian 1 first, Wild Magic at 3 for Magic Awareness, Ranger 3 slotted in early for the companion, then Barbarian to 17 for Controlled Surge. Configuration scored: greatsword, Reckless Attack every turn, one Rage per fight and therefore one surge per fight; the wild-magic table is taken as rolled rather than chosen until Barbarian 14.
Surge.strength: Two things a duo cannot buy elsewhere. Goon's fix makes Magic Awareness add this body's proficiency bonus to both characters' saves against spells, which in a party of two is a party-wide anti-caster aura for free; and Bolstering Magic hands the partner a real spell slot or a d3 every rest cycle, which is the only cross-character resource transfer in the class list. The Beast Master companion is a third body in a party that otherwise has two.
Surge.wants: A partner that provides the damage spike and the crowd answer — this body converts its levels into party economy and saves, not into a kill.
uncertain: The wild-magic pool is 220+ effects across four mods and I cannot enumerate its damage distribution. The AoE line is one surge a fight amortised over four rounds, rising in Act III because Controlled Surge (Barbarian 14) lets the body pick the area effect rather than roll it. This is the softest number in the record.

`magic-awareness` is scored as a pair-scope blanket booster from Barbarian 3, per the registry. Goon's 1.1.3.6 changelog is what makes it proficiency-bonus-to-spell-saves rather than 1d4 to all saves; the entry is in the class file, not read from the pak here.
The Ranger's Companion is excluded from §1 and §2 per rule 2 and carried on `act` instead.
Surge.address: barbarian/Base game (Patch 8) — Path of Wild Magic:action-economy

Colossus.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Giant) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Colossus.note: Barbarian 1 first, Giant at 3, Barbarian to 17 for Demiurgic Colossus, Fighter 3 last for Great Weapon Fighting and the superiority dice. Configuration scored: greatsword in melee with Elemental Cleaver set to fire, Reckless Attack every turn; the thrown-weapon line is available but not the configuration priced here.
Colossus.strength: Elemental Cleaver is a second damage type welded onto every swing, which is the direct answer to Absolute Wrath putting layered physical resistance on ordinary enemies — and it doubles to 2d6 at 14. Demiurgic Colossus's +10 ft reach and Huge toggle solve the positioning problem a two-body party has, where there are no allies to body-block with.
Colossus.wants: A partner that holds the pair's concentration slot and clears crowds; this body's area damage is zero and its control is a shove routine.
uncertain: The class file calls Giant "the throwing build" and Goon's fixes make Reckless Attack, Brutal Critical and the +4/+8 Rage bonus apply to throws. I scored the melee configuration instead, because BG3 resolves Throw as its own Action rather than as an attack from the Attack action, so a thrown routine delivers 2 instances a round against melee's 4. If Throw does consume Extra Attack in this build the thrown line would beat the melee one and this record understates Act III.
Elemental Cleaver is priced as a per-hit rider on the same damage roll, so it adds no instance and collects no extra gear constant.
Reckless Attack is scored as routine advantage (×1.35) with its cost carried on `dur`.
Colossus.address: barbarian/Base game (Patch 8) — Path of the Giant:front-line

pools.name: ki
pools.underspend_reason: Monk 3 ki funds Friar's Bond once a fight; the remaining ki has no damage use on a raging Barbarian, and Martial Arts does not work with a shield.

Bearheart.note: Barbarian 1 first, Bear Heart at 3, Barbarian to 17 for Bestial Attunement, Monk 3 (Way of the Friar) last. Configuration scored: longsword and shield over Unarmoured Defence, Bear Heart, Elk aspect, Friar's Blessing as the bond variant, Reckless Attack every turn. It trades a greatsword's damage for two more points of AC and gives up every damage rider in the class.
Bearheart.strength: Bear Heart is resistance to everything but Psychic, and it multiplies against Lone Wolf's own halving rather than overlapping it — this is the single hardest body in the file to remove. Bestial Attunement at 14 is a real taunt, which is how the tougher half of a two-person party protects the softer one when the game has no aggro mechanic, and Friar's Bond puts a +1d4 on both bodies' saving throws from one bonus action.
Bearheart.wants: Damage. This body is a wall with a longsword; it needs a partner that actually kills things, and one with a crowd answer, because it has none.
uncertain: The Monk 3 dip may be dead weight. Friar's Bond is a Concentration ability and Rage forbids concentrating on spells. In BG3 monk ki abilities are not treated as spells for Rage's purposes (Flurry of Blows works while raging), so I scored Friar's Bond as live — but I could not confirm from the installed pak that the modded Friar's Bond is flagged the same way. If it is blocked, `friars-blessing` comes off the Act III saves block (rung 5 → 4) and `rsc` falls from 4 to 1.
Bear Heart's resistance is priced as ×1.9 on the effective-HP mitigation term rather than a flat ×2, because it does not cover Psychic.

Reckless Attack is scored on for both the ×1.35 damage multiplier and the enemy-advantage cost on `dur`. A tank that leaves the toggle off reads roughly one rung lower on `st` and one higher on `dur` in Act I.

Aspect of the Beast is scored as Elk (Primal Stampede, which Goon's 1.1.3.6 does fix). Crocodile, Honey Badger, Stallion, Tiger and Wolverine are still buggy in this build — those fixes are in v1.2.0.0, which Listo did not pull.

pools.name: pact slots
pools.underspend_reason: Rage forbids spellcasting, so the Warlock pact slots cannot be spent inside a fight this body is raging in — which is every fight.

Nullblade.note: Barbarian 1 first, Ginnungagap at 3 for Null Warrior, Barbarian to 11 for Relentless Rage, then Bard 6 and Warlock 3. Configuration scored: greatsword, Reckless Attack every turn, Rage up in every fight. No class reaches 13, so this pays six feats rather than seven.
Nullblade.strength: Listo's own balance notes say most of the added enemies are effectively wild magic sorcerers and warlocks, and this is the only chassis in the class list that answers them directly: Magic Syphoning is a counterspell that costs a Reaction and a Constitution check rather than a slot, refreshes on every Rage, and Lone Wolf hands the body a second Reaction to spend on it. Advantage on all saves against spells patches the Barbarian's Wisdom hole for free.
Nullblade.wants: A partner that supplies both damage types this body lacks and the pair's concentration slot; this one's own spell lists are switched off the moment it rages.
uncertain: Warlock 3 is dead weight on this split. Rage switches off spellcasting, so Eldritch Blast, Agonising Blast and the two pact slots are unavailable in every fight this body actually rages in. What survives is Wisdom + Charisma saves if Warlock were the level-1 class, which it is not here, and one feat. The split search does not know Rage blocks casting; this is the clearest case of it in the batch.

Bard 6's slots are dead for the same reason and carry `to_damage` 0. `rsc` 2 is outward healing cast between fights or after dropping Rage, which Goon's overhaul makes a free action — but it costs a Rage charge to re-enter.

Magic Syphoning is scored at `ctrl_s` 3 — a repeatable non-concentration interrupt that removes an enemy caster's action outright on a successful check. It arguably reaches rung 4 (control costing no concentration), but it only bites on casters and can fail the check, so I held it at 3.
Barbarian 11 does not reach Herald of Ginnungagap (14), so the Slow rider never lands on this chassis.

Ancestor.split: Barbarian 14 (Path of the Ancestral Guardian) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Ancestor.note: Barbarian 1 first, Ancestral Guardian at 3, Barbarian to 14 for Vengeful Ancestors, Bard 6 (Stormcalling) last. Configuration scored: greatsword, Reckless Attack every turn, Spirit Shield spent on the partner rather than banked. It has no area damage, no rest-free control, and a spell list that switches off while raging.
Ancestor.strength: This is the one chassis in the class list built around the failure mode a two-body party actually has. Spirit Shield is a Reaction that removes damage from the other character, Lone Wolf hands the body a spare Reaction to spend on it, and Ancestral Protectors makes the first enemy it hits attack the partner at disadvantage for half damage. Vengeful Ancestors at 14 turns all of that back into Force damage — the least-resisted type in the run.
Ancestor.wants: A partner that kills things and clears crowds; this body converts its Reactions into the partner's survival and delivers only par single-target damage.
uncertain: Vengeful Ancestors is priced at 1.5 Spirit Shields a round — the partner is hit about that often across the crowd/boss blend — at 4d6 prevented and therefore 4d6 returned as Force. Two a round would take Act II to rung 4.
`rsc` falls from 4 to 3 in Act III on the act table, not because the feature changed: 4d6 of prevention is a rung-4 answer to Act I's 5–16 damage hits and only a partial one against Act III's 13–40.
Rage switches off the Stormcalling spell list and Thundercall, so Bard 6 contributes Bardic Inspiration, Expertise, Song of Rest and Countercharm only; `to_damage` is 0.
Reckless Attack is scored on, with its cost on `dur`.

Spiker.note: Barbarian 1 first, Battlerager at 3, Barbarian to 17 for Spiked Retribution, Rogue 3 (Thief) last. Configuration scored: rapier and shield in medium metal armour — the armour is a requirement of Battlerager Armor and costs Unarmoured Defence — with Reckless Attack every turn, which is also what turns on Reckless Abandon's temporary hit points and makes Sneak Attack land.
Spiker.strength: Reckless Abandon pays a Constitution modifier in temporary hit points every single turn for doing the thing this body was going to do anyway, and Lone Wolf's second Bonus Action means the armour-spike attack fires twice a round instead of competing with itself. It is the rare Barbarian whose defensive resource has no rest clock at all.
Spiker.wants: Anything that touches a crowd or holds a concentration spell — this body has zero on both control axes and only an incidental splash on area damage.
uncertain: Reckless Attack's advantage depends on Strength rolling the attack. `5e Reckless Attack` v2 gates its boost on `IF(AttackRollAbility(Ability.Strength) and (IsMeleeWeaponAttack() or IsMeleeUnarmedAttack()))`, and this body swings a finesse weapon, where BG3 picks the higher of Strength and Dexterity automatically. Scored at Str 22 against Dex 18, so Strength rolls and the ×1.35 stands. A build that let Dexterity overtake Strength would lose the multiplier entirely — roughly a rung on `st` — and would also stop handing enemies advantage, which is the `dur` cost paired with it.
Battlerager Armor's spike attack is priced at 2 a round on Lone Wolf's two Bonus Actions; the class file records no once-per-turn cap but I could not confirm it from the pak.

Thief's Fast Hands is a third Bonus Action and cannot be represented — the format caps bonus actions at 8, which is 2 a round. A third spike a round would take Act I from 1.77 to about 2.0 and the rung from 4 to 5. This is a real capability the record silently omits.
The grapple half of Battlerager Armor needs Grappling Framework, which Listo does not ship; the class file says it falls back to 3 piercing on a Throw, which is not scored here.
Sneak Attack is scored once a turn (2d6 at Rogue 3) on the rapier, off Reckless advantage. Rogue 5's off-turn reaction Sneak Attack is out of reach on a 3-level dip.
Spiked Retribution's 3 piercing is the whole of the Act III AoE line — three adjacent attackers a round — and it is genuinely tiny.

Clawform.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Beast) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Clawform.note: Barbarian 1 first, Beast at 3, Barbarian to 17 for Call the Hunt, Fighter 3 last for the superiority dice. Configuration scored: Claws as the natural weapon, which needs an empty hand in both weapon sets and therefore gives up a shield, a two-hander and every weapon enchantment; medium armour, Reckless Attack every turn.
Clawform.strength: Claws add a third attack to each Attack action, and Lone Wolf gives the body two of those — six swings a round with no bonus action spent and no clock. Infectious Fury then spends an enemy's own Reaction attacking one of its allies, which is the only feature in the class list that adds to the party's action economy by subtracting from theirs; and Call the Hunt puts a permanent +1d6 a turn on the partner, which in a duo is a buff aimed at the only ally there is.
Clawform.wants: Crowd damage and control — this body is six single-target swings and nothing else, with zero on both control axes until the Battle Master dice arrive.
uncertain: The class file records that an extra Action from Haste starts a new Attack action and forfeits the bonus claw attack. I scored six claws a round on Lone Wolf's two native Actions, where that caveat does not apply — but if the engine treats the second Lone Wolf Action the same way it treats a Hasted one, this body delivers four claws a round, not six, and every act drops a rung.

Infectious Fury's 2d12 psychic is priced as the mode taken; the 'use its reaction to attack another creature' mode is carried on `ctrl_s` and `act` instead, because scoring both would be the same use twice.
Call the Hunt's +1d6 on the partner is not scored on this body's damage axes at all — it is the partner's damage. It is what `rsc` 2 and the `strength` line are about.
Reckless Attack is scored on: ×1.35 on the raw, with the enemy-advantage cost carried on `dur`.

Juggernaut.note: Barbarian 1 first for the Strength and Constitution saves and the d12, Juggernaut at 3, Barbarian to 17 for Unstoppable, Rogue 3 (Thief) last. Configuration scored: rapier and shield over Unarmoured Defence for AC 20, Reckless Attack up, and Resolute Stance treated as the per-round toggle it is — potential on both axes rather than a build-time choice, per rule 3.
Juggernaut.strength: Resolute Stance is the only on-demand source of blanket disadvantage on every attack against you in the class list, and its cost — disadvantage on your own attacks — is the cheapest cost in the game when the other player is the damage. That is how one of two bodies holds an encounter tuned for five. Hurricane Strike then hands the partner a free reaction melee attack, manufacturing action economy a duo has no other way to buy.
Juggernaut.wants: A partner that kills things and covers crowds — this body's job is to be the thing the encounter is aimed at, and it has no area damage and no rescue at all.
uncertain: Reckless Attack's advantage depends on Strength rolling the attack. `5e Reckless Attack` v2 gates its boost on `IF(AttackRollAbility(Ability.Strength) and (IsMeleeWeaponAttack() or IsMeleeUnarmedAttack()))`, and this body swings a finesse weapon, where BG3 picks the higher of Strength and Dexterity automatically. Scored at Str 22 against Dex 18, so Strength rolls and the ×1.35 stands. A build that let Dexterity overtake Strength would lose the multiplier entirely — roughly a rung on `st` — and would also stop handing enemies advantage, which is the `dur` cost paired with it.

Resolute Stance is scored as potential on both axes, not as a build-time pick. Rule 3 says a per-round tactical choice is not a configuration, and the toggle is checked at the start of each turn — so `st` is scored with Reckless advantage (×1.35) and `dur` is scored with the stance up (attacks against you at disadvantage, p_hit 0.50 → 0.25, a ×2.6 on effective HP). The two cannot both be true in the same round: running them together cancels both, and running the stance without Reckless costs ×0.65 on damage. If the model wants one configuration named, the stance-up read is `st` 1/1/1 and `dur` unchanged.

Unstoppable (Barbarian 14) is immunity to Frightened, Paralysed, Prone and Stunned while raging. That is worth a great deal against Listo's control-heavy encounters and there is no booster id for it, so it contributes nothing to the derived saves rung. Recorded here rather than rounded away.
Rogue 3 (Thief) buys Cunning Action, a feat and Sneak Attack off the rapier; Fast Hands' third Bonus Action cannot be represented because the format caps bonus actions at 8, which is 2 a round.

AoE 0 is the convention this batch holds throughout: §2 is scored as damage that reaches several enemies by the mechanism's own design, not as an attack routine aimed at different targets. The routine's crowd contribution is already priced by `scoring-model.md` §5's 0.5 single-target crowd coefficient, and the rubric's own anchor puts a two-target cleave at rung 0. If the convention is ruled the other way this body re-bases with every other martial in the roster.

Galvanic.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Lightning Vessel) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Galvanic.note: Barbarian 1 first, Lightning Vessel at 3, Barbarian to 17 for Electric Beast, Fighter 3 last. Configuration scored: greatsword, Lone Wolf's +4 on Constitution and Wisdom rather than the usual Dexterity pair — every number this subclass produces keys off the Constitution modifier — with Electrified Chains re-applied every turn and Reckless Attack up. The price is a three-proficiency save set instead of four.
Galvanic.strength: This is the only Barbarian whose damage scales with the stat it was already maxing for hit points and Unarmoured Defence, so the second Bonus Action Lone Wolf hands it goes straight into more damage rather than competing with Rage. It is also the only one carrying a real second damage type on every swing plus a genuine area burst, which against Absolute Wrath's layered physical resistance is worth more than the headline numbers suggest.
Galvanic.wants: A partner that covers Wisdom and Dexterity saves and holds the pair's concentration slot — this body spent Lone Wolf's proficiencies on Constitution and has only three disjoint saves to show for it.
uncertain: This is the least trustworthy row in the batch. Listo applies "CD's nerf patch" on top of Path of the Lightning Vessel; the patch ships inside the Wabbajack, is not a Nexus archive and is not in the manifest, so the class file's numbers are the unmodified mod's and Listo's are lower by an unknown amount. I scored Electrified Chains and Fulgurant Strike at their stated +2× Constitution modifier (+3× from Electric Beast at 14). At half those riders Act I falls from 2.58 to about 1.7 and the rung from 5 to 4.
Electrified Chains is priced as up every round — it lasts until the end of your turn, so it costs one of the two Bonus Actions each turn, which the bonus budget shows.
Roaring Crash fires once a fight, on entering Rage, and is amortised over four rounds at 4 targets ÷ 4 rounds = 1 instance a round, exactly as the rubric amortises one Fireball a fight.

The `st` line is a Constitution-scaled flat rider, so it does not decay the way a 1d6 does — the ratio still slides 2.58 → 1.96 because enemy HP outruns it, which is the arithmetic doing its job rather than a hand-written decay.
Fulgurant Strike is an interrupt rather than a bonus action and is carried on Reactions, which the format does not budget.

Wraith.split: Barbarian 11 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 6 / Warlock 3

pools.name: pact slots
pools.underspend_reason: Revenant's Rage disables spellcasting outright, so the Warlock pact slots cannot be spent in any fight this body rages in — which is every fight.

Wraith.note: Barbarian 1 first, Revenant at 3 for Ghost Armor, Barbarian to 11 for Relentless Rage, then Bard 6 and Warlock 3. Configuration scored: plate and shield with a longsword — Ghost Armor is what makes heavy armour wearable while raging — Lone Wolf's +4 on Constitution and Wisdom, Reckless Attack up, Haunt retargeted every time it dies. No class reaches 13, so it pays six feats.
Wraith.strength: Revenant's Rage stacks flat damage reduction 2 underneath physical resistance and Lone Wolf's own halving, and against an Act I crowd hit of 5.4 that arithmetic reduces the hit to under a point. Nothing else in the class file is close. Haunt then mirrors every point this body does take onto a frightened enemy as Necrotic, which turns being focused — the thing that kills two-body parties — into the damage engine.
Wraith.wants: A partner that can be kept alive without this body's help and that never needs to heal it: Revenant's Rage means it cannot be healed by any means, so a healer partner is spending its actions on itself alone.
uncertain: Bard 6 and Warlock 3 are both dead weight on this split, and worse here than on the Ginnungagap one. Revenant's Rage disables spellcasting explicitly (the 1.2.0.66-era change named in the class file), and the rage cannot be ended until combat ends — so unlike every other raging Barbarian in the batch, this body cannot drop Rage mid-fight to cast. Nine levels buy Bardic Inspiration, Expertise, Song of Rest, Countercharm and two feats. `rsc` is 0 rather than 2 for exactly that reason.

"Cannot be healed by any means" is a pair-level cost that no axis in this format can express. It does not lower `dur` — the mitigation is what makes the body durable — but it removes this body from the receiving end of a partner's entire Rescue axis. Read the `wants` line as load-bearing.

Haunt's damage mirror is folded into `st_raw` but not counted as an instance, because a reflected-damage effect collects no weapon item rider and counting it would inflate the gear constant. That is a deliberate conservative reading of the instance rule.
Immunity to Charm, Fear, Poison and Disease has no booster id and therefore contributes nothing to the derived saves rung, which sits at 2 on three disjoint proficiencies.
Barbarian 11 does not reach Wraithwalk (14).

AoE 0 is the convention this batch holds throughout: §2 is scored as damage that reaches several enemies by the mechanism's own design, not as an attack routine aimed at different targets. The routine's crowd contribution is already priced by `scoring-model.md` §5's 0.5 single-target crowd coefficient, and the rubric's own anchor puts a two-target cleave at rung 0. If the convention is ruled the other way this body re-bases with every other martial in the roster.

Tundra.split: Barbarian 14 (Path of the Storm Herald) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Tundra.note: Barbarian 1 first, Storm Herald at 3, Barbarian to 14 for Raging Storm, Bard 6 (Stormcalling) last. Configuration scored: Tundra aura throughout — the class file's own duo verdict — with a longsword and shield over Unarmoured Defence, the aura re-triggered as a Bonus Action every turn, and Reckless Attack up. Desert and Sea are the damage options and are given up.
Tundra.strength: Tundra hands the partner temporary hit points every single turn off a Bonus Action Lone Wolf duplicated, on no rest clock at all — which is the exact resource a party facing 120-supply long rests cannot buy. Shielding Storm at 10 then extends this body's cold resistance to the partner, and in a party of two both bodies are always inside a 10 ft aura, so an effect written for a five-body party covers this one entirely.
Tundra.wants: Damage and a crowd answer. This body is a mitigation stream with a longsword; its own single-target output falls to being outrun by Act III and its area damage is zero.
uncertain: Tundra deals no damage at all, which is why both damage lines are the bare weapon routine and `aoe` is 0 in every act. Desert instead would put 2–6 fire on every creature in the aura every turn and would read `aoe` 1 rather than 0; Sea would add 1d6–4d6 lightning to one target. The class file calls Tundra the duo pick and I scored that, per rule 3.

Rage switches off the Stormcalling spell list, Thundercall and Chorus of Thunder, so Bard 6 contributes Bardic Inspiration, Expertise, Song of Rest and Countercharm only; `to_damage` is 0 and `types` carries no Thunder.

`rsc` is held at 3 rather than 4 because the temporary hit points are 2 / 4 / 5–6 a turn against act hits of 5–16, 10–29 and 13–40. It is a real repeatable outward source on no clock, but it is an order of magnitude smaller than Twilight Sanctuary, which is the rung-4 anchor.

Raging Storm (Tundra) at 14 — a Strength save or speed 0, on every aura activation, no concentration — is what takes `ctrl_s` to 4 in Act II; it falls to 3 in Act III on the act table, not because the feature changed.

AoE 0 is the convention this batch holds throughout: §2 is scored as damage that reaches several enemies by the mechanism's own design, not as an attack routine aimed at different targets. The routine's crowd contribution is already priced by `scoring-model.md` §5's 0.5 single-target crowd coefficient, and the rubric's own anchor puts a two-target cleave at rung 0. If the convention is ruled the other way this body re-bases with every other martial in the roster.

Fury.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Zealot) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer)
Fury.note: Barbarian 1 first, Zealot at 3, Barbarian to 17 for Rage Beyond Death, Blood Hunter 3 last for Rite of the Dawn. Configuration scored: greatsword, Divine Fury set to radiant, Rite of the Dawn running (paid in hit points), Reckless Attack every turn.
Fury.strength: Two features aimed squarely at the thing that ends this run — losing one of two bodies. Warrior of the Gods lets the partner pick this body up with no Revivify scroll spent, and Rage Beyond Death means a raging Zealot simply cannot die until the Rage ends. Fanatical Focus is a save reroll per Rage rather than per rest, which against Listo's climbing boss DCs is worth more to a two-save class than any item.
Fury.wants: A crowd answer and a concentration holder; this body is radiant single-target damage and a refusal to die, with nothing on either control axis.
uncertain: `fanatical-focus` (a reroll per Rage) plus `danger-sense` are two partial boosters covering Dexterity and every save, which the registry composes into one blanket — so this body derives saves rung 5 from Act I. That is a real reading of the table but it is the whole of the difference between this Zealot and every other Barbarian in the batch, and it rests on a per-Rage reroll being priced as blanket coverage.
Divine Fury is scored once a round ('the first creature you hit each turn'), at 1d6 + half Barbarian level, on the same damage roll as the attack — so it adds no instance.

Rage Beyond Death (Barbarian 14) is priced as roughly doubling the pool inside a Rage on the effective-HP ratio, which is what takes `dur` from 4 to 5 in Act II. If the death saves it still forces are read as a real risk rather than a formality, this is a rung generous.
Rite of the Dawn is hemocraft 1d4 at Blood Hunter 3 and costs hit points to run; the drain is netted against the pool on `dur`, not shown separately.
Zealous Presence is 1/long rest — with 120-supply long rests it is a once-per-boss button, and is not scored as repeatable anything.

Tempo.note: Bard 3 for the College, Monk 5 for Extra Attack and ki, then Barbarian 3 for Rage and Reckless Attack; the Bardic Unarmed strike rides the Inspiration die so the class resource and the damage die grow together. It gives up the Bard's spellcasting for the length of every Rage, and it never reaches Magical Secrets breadth or a second Extra Attack.
Tempo.strength: Lone Wolf's second Bonus Action is the whole build: two Flurries a round turns Monk 6's seven ki into eight unarmed strikes a turn, and Reckless Attack's advantage is scale-invariant against Listo's +126% HP where a flat rider is not. Unarmoured Defence at Dex 22 / Wis 20 buys AC 21 with no armour to fund at 4x prices.
Tempo.wants: A body that holds the pair's concentration and answers crowds — this one is at 0 on AoE in every act and cannot cast at all while raging.
uncertain: Configuration chosen at build time (rule 3): the body Rages every fight from Act II, so its Bard spellcasting is off in combat. Scored as a raging melee body — AoE 0 in Acts II and III is a consequence of that choice, not of the College.

Whether Bardic Inspiration (the spell that triggers Dance's free Agile Strikes kick) is castable while Raging is untested; the free kick is excluded from Acts II and III, which costs about 0.25 instances a round.
Rage's +2 melee damage is assumed to apply to Bardic Unarmed Attack; the class file does not name unarmed explicitly.
College of Dance's Tandem Footwork (6), Improved Tandem Footwork (10) and Leading Evasion (14) are documented only as images on the mod page, so nothing is scored for them.

Unsettle.note: A control Bard that buys its armour and its one blasting engine from Zeal — heavy armour, martial weapons, and Consuming Fervor to maximise a Fireball twice a short rest. It spends most of its pool on control rather than damage, so it is at rung 0-1 on single-target in every act.
Unsettle.strength: Unsettling Words rolls the die before the status lands, so in a two-body party you know the subtraction before you commit the pair's one concentration slot — that is the whole lockdown plan, and Font of Inspiration puts it on a short-rest clock against 120-supply long rests. Unfailing Inspiration means a die spent on your only partner comes back when they fail.
Unsettle.wants: A body that converts control into kills — this one lands the save-or-lose and then has nothing to hit with.
uncertain: Silver Tongue (Eloquence 3) is on the mod's own Known Issues list as not working; the skills map credits it with nothing, so Persuasion and Deception are plain modifier + Expertise.

Act III ctrl_s 5 assumes a Magical Secrets pick at Bard 14 reaches Power Word Kill or Dominate Monster off the caster-level-20 9th slot; Expansion's 14/18 tranches are stated to require 5e Spells, which is installed, but the exact pool contents were not read.
to_damage is 0.4 rather than the 0.5 default because the lockdown plan spends the pool on control; the ctrl rungs are priced against the other 0.6.

Majesty.note: Cleric first for heavy armour, martial weapons and War Priest, then Bard 14 for Glamour's Unbreakable Majesty. It is a plate-wearing Charisma caster that swings twice a round from Cleric 6, and it pays for that with a damage ratio that never clears rung 1.
Majesty.strength: Unbreakable Majesty makes the first attack on this body each turn a Charisma save against its own DC — in a two-character party the aggro it sheds has nowhere else to go except the partner, so it works as a pair-level mitigation layer that a four-body party would waste. War Priest plus Lone Wolf's second Bonus Action is two free swings a round on a body already in plate.
Majesty.wants: A body that clears crowds — this one has no area engine past a single upcast blast a fight, and its control is a front-loaded Command.
uncertain: The split names no domain; War is chosen because it is the only domain with a true Extra Attack (CCC at 6) and it is what makes the Bard 14 / Cleric 6 shape a front-line body at all. Named in the note.
Acts II and III cast four of the six-to-seven levelled slots a fight rather than the full per-fight allowance, spending the rest on Actions; the surplus is priced as Endurance, not as damage.

Act III dur 4 credits Unbreakable Majesty at roughly a 1.3x effective-HP multiplier against the act's crowd hit. The save is Charisma against this body's own DC and the mod implements it through the interrupt system; the uptime against four attackers was not measured.

Lorewarden.note: Bard first for three level-1 skills, Lore 3 for three more and Cutting Words, Magical Secrets at 6, 10 and 14, then Cleric 5 (Knowledge) and a late Fighter 1 for Second Wind and shields. It is the skill chassis of the roster and it buys that with almost no single-target damage.
Lorewarden.strength: Every dialogue check in the run is rolled at the party-best total by the host, so one body carrying six proficiencies and four Expertise covers a two-character party outright; Peerless Skill at 14 is usable inside dialogue, which is the only in-run answer to a check you did not see coming. Magical Secrets under the Extender pulls from every installed list, so the pair's control breadth comes from one body.
Lorewarden.wants: A body that removes enemy action points permanently — this one is rung 0-1 on single-target in every act and its control is all long-rest slots.
uncertain: The split names no Cleric domain; Knowledge is chosen for the two double-proficiency skills and named in the note. It grants no heavy armour, which is why dur stays at 3.

Cutting Words is now a Charm in SG_Charmed and cannot be used on Deafened or charm-immune creatures (Goon), so it is priced as a rider that fails against a real share of Listo's bosses rather than as a universal answer.

Peerless Skill (Lore 14) adds an Inspiration die to the body's own check and is dialogue-usable, but it is a short-rest resource rather than a permanent modifier, so it is excluded from the skills map.

Aria.note: The only Bard College in the list that is a genuine blaster, taken deep for Electrifying Aria at 14 and dipped into Tempest for heavy armour and Destructive Wrath. Chorus of Thunder converts an Inspiration die into Concussion on a Constitution save, which is slot-free hard control that never touches the pair's concentration.
Aria.strength: Electrifying Aria is one Action that buys a whole fight: ten turns of area lightning that lowers every caught enemy's Constitution save by one per remaining turn while cutting the partner's crit threshold, then Finale! cashes it in as a mass Stun. In a two-body party that is the single best action-for-tempo trade available, and Concussion denying enemy reactions matters more when there are only two of you to be reacted at.
Aria.wants: A partner that is not thunder or lightning — both of this body's damage types are commonly resisted under Absolute Wrath, and it has no third.
uncertain: Otherworldly Archetypes entered Listo on a playtesting footing and the Stormcalling numbers come from the author's documentation site, not from a pak read. Electrifying Aria's ten-turn repeat is the single largest term in the Act III AoE and it is unverified in game.
Staccato Lightning is scored at six casts a fight (of eight bonus actions), assuming Conductor's concentration holds; a broken concentration removes about a third of the single-target raw.

Chorus of Thunder applied to Shatter is read as area Concussion, which is what carries ctrl_a to rung 4 from Act II. The mod text says 'your next Thunder damage spell' without restricting it to single-target.

Flourish.note: Swords 6 for Extra Attack and the Flourishes, War domain to 6 for a second Extra Attack source and War Priest, Barbarian 3 for Rage and Reckless Attack. Do not plan it around Arcane Acuity — the rework caps at three stacks and cannot be pre-stacked, so the published Acuity lock does not exist here.
Flourish.strength: Goon's rework gives all three Flourishes Interrupt counterparts, and Lone Wolf hands this body two Reactions to spend them with, so a spare reaction becomes damage rather than a Counterspell it cannot cast. Rage's physical resistance stacks under Lone Wolf's halving on a body already in plate.
Flourish.wants: Anything that answers a crowd and holds concentration — this body is at rung 0 on AoE from Act II and cannot cast while raging.
uncertain: The split names no Cleric domain and no Barbarian path; War is chosen for Extra Attack at 6 and War Priest, and the Barbarian 3 subclass contributes nothing that is scored.

Configuration chosen at build time: this body Rages from Act II, so its Bard spellcasting is off in combat. Blade Flourish is treated as a weapon action that merely expends an Inspiration die and therefore still works while Raging; Bardic Inspiration the spell does not.
Slashing Flourish's second target is the only AoE this body has from Act II, which is why aoe falls to 0.

Pathos.note: A reaction chassis: Poetry in Misery regains an Inspiration whenever anyone within 9m rolls a natural 1, Tale of Hubris cuts the crit threshold against whatever crit you, and Favored Soul hands the same Charisma the Bard already uses a Cleric domain list that Metamagic applies to. It gives up damage almost entirely.
Pathos.strength: Lone Wolf grants a second Reaction, so Poetry in Misery and Tale of Hubris can both fire in the same round — the subclass's one structural constraint is exactly the thing this run removes. Twinned Death Ward, Twinned Cure Wounds and Twinned Greater Restoration cover 100% of a two-person party for a single Metamagic pick, which is only true because the party is two.
Pathos.wants: A body that carries the pair's tempo — this one is rung 0-1 on single-target throughout and its area damage does not clear rung 3 until Act III.
uncertain: Favored Soul's domain is not named in the split; Life is assumed, which is what puts Revivify and Death Ward inside Metamagic range. Peace would trade those for Warding Bond, which the schema says Twinned cannot reach in a duo anyway.

Nimbus of Pathos is scored at nothing. It is a one-fight nuke that drops the target to 0 HP when it ends, and in a two-body party the dying character is 50% of the action economy — the class file's own warning.
Tragedy's feature names come from the Tal'Dorei source matched to level and effect; the mod page renders them as images. Effects verified, names not.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite lands on one weapon hit and has no area form; it cannot be spread across a group.

riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite lands on one weapon hit and has no area form; it cannot be spread across a group.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite lands on one weapon hit and has no area form; it cannot be spread across a group.

Valorsmite.note: Three Charisma classes stacked so that every slot in the pool is Divine Smite fuel: Valour 6 for Extra Attack, shields and martial weapons, Paladin 2 for Smite, Sorcerer 6 for Font of Magic to turn sorcery points into more of them. One primary ability funds attack support, spell DC and Smite alike, and the damage is flat enough to be outrun by Act III.
Valorsmite.strength: One ability score does every job on this body, so it needs no second stat and the point buy funds Constitution instead — and Font of Magic converts a resource the run refills on a long rest into burst on the fight that needs it, which matters when a long rest costs 120 supplies. Combat Inspiration puts the Inspiration die on the partner's AC or damage without a spell.
Valorsmite.wants: A body with an area engine and a real long-rest-free clock; this one is rung 1 on AoE in every act and its damage half is spent out of the same pool as its control.
uncertain: The split names no Sorcerer bloodline and no Paladin oath; Metamagic and Divine Smite are what the levels are taken for and neither depends on the pick, so nothing subclass-specific is scored.

Divine Smite is upcast at BG3's cap of 5d8, so it is a flat rider from Act II and the st ratio falls from 0.97 to 0.79 across the run with nothing having changed. That fall is arithmetic, not a judgement.
Paladin is taken after level 1, so it grants no heavy armour and no Wis/Cha save proficiency; the save set is Bard's and Lone Wolf's.

Dawnrite.split: Blood Hunter 17 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Dawnrite.note: Dual shortswords, a Crimson Rite on each, Curse Specialist's fourth Blood Maledict from level 3, and Battle Master dice on top — every resource it owns refills on a short rest. It buys that instance count by giving up a shield, and it has no area engine whatsoever.
Dawnrite.strength: Crimson Rite is the one melee rider in the list that does not decay: the hemocraft die climbs 1d6 to 1d8 to 1d10 and Brand of Sundering rolls it twice against the branded creature, so a six-instance routine keeps pace with +126% enemy HP where a flat 1d6 rider loses a third of its value. Curse Specialist also strips the Bloodless restriction, so the curses still work on the undead and constructs Act III is full of.
Dawnrite.wants: Anything that answers a crowd. This body is at rung 0 on AoE and rung 1 on area control in every act, and it has nothing at all aimed at the partner until Act III.
uncertain: Configuration fixed at build time (rule 3): two-weapon fighting with a Rite on each blade, not sword-and-board. That is worth two extra instances a round and costs the shield, which is why dur sits at 3 rather than 4.
Action Surge is excluded from the damage block per rule 2 and scored on Actions only.
Brand of Castigation retaliation (Int mod, doubled at 13) is counted as damage but not as instances — it is a passive interrupt, not a weapon attack, and whether item riders attach to it is unread.

Blood Curse of the Exorcist (15) is the only thing this body aims at its partner; it is scored rsc 2 in Act III as narrow condition removal, below the act's rung-3 row which wants 9th-tier restoration.

Crimson Rite requires a `Dippable` weapon and which of Listo's reworked weapons carry that flag is unverified in the class file; a best-in-slot blade that cannot take a Rite would cost this body a full rung.

Hybrid.split: Blood Hunter 17 (Order of the Lycan) / Rogue 3 (Thief)

pools.name: Hybrid Transformation
pools.underspend_reason: one transformation covers a four-round fight; the other two are the second and third fights of the cycle

Hybrid.note: Rogue first for the save pair, four skills and Expertise, then Blood Hunter 17 for the Lycan package: Dex-scaled unarmed strikes carrying their own Crimson Rite, Resilient Hide's proportional resistance, and Lycan Regeneration under half HP. It gives up Sneak Attack entirely, because unarmed strikes are not finesse weapons.
Hybrid.strength: Resilient Hide's resistance to non-magical physical is proportional, so it multiplies with Lone Wolf's halving rather than being washed out by inflated enemy damage — and Fast Hands plus Lone Wolf's second Bonus Action turns the Lycan's free unarmed strike into a repeating engine. Brand of the Voracious hands Advantage on the one creature a two-body party actually needs to kill.
Hybrid.wants: A body that can pick this one up and that answers crowds — Bloodlust turns a Lycan below half HP on the nearest creature, and in a duo the nearest creature is the partner.
uncertain: Configuration fixed at build time: the Lycan unarmed package, which excludes Sneak Attack — unarmed strikes are not finesse weapons, so the Rogue 3 dip contributes Fast Hands, Cunning Action and the skill base, not damage.

Fast Hands grants a third Bonus Action on top of Lone Wolf's two, but the damage block's bonus budget is fixed at 8 per fight, so the third bonus action is scored on Actions only and its damage is not counted. That understates st by roughly one instance a round.

Act III st credits Brand of the Voracious with routine Advantage (x1.35) on the branded creature only; the brand is one creature at a time on a short-rest clock, which is exactly the boss case §1 measures.
Bloodlust has no opt-out before Lycan 15 and the risk is not expressible on any axis: a failed Wisdom save below half HP turns this body on its partner. Treated as a note, not a score.
Heightened Senses grants Advantage on Perception, which the skills map cannot express as a modifier; the real Perception clear rate is roughly 15pp better than the map implies in every act.

Mutagen.split: Blood Hunter 17 (Order of the Mutant) / Ranger 3 (Gloom Stalker)
Mutagen.note: A longbow Blood Hunter whose whole kit refills on a short rest: Mutagencraft, Blood Maledict, Umbral Shroud and the Crimson Rite itself. Celerity raises the Dexterity score above the removed cap, and the build declines Cruelty so its Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saves stay clean.
Mutagen.strength: Long rests cost 120+ supplies here and short rests are free, so a class that refills everything between fights is buying a resource nobody else has — and Celerity's +3 to +5 to a raw ability score matters more than it reads because Listo removed the score cap. Strange Metabolism's flat Poison immunity is a large swing against the install's poison package.
Mutagen.wants: A crowd answer and an outward one: this body is 0 on AoE, 1 on area control and 0 on rescue in every act.
uncertain: Mutagen selection fixed at build time: Celerity, Precision, Reconstruction, Rapidity. Cruelty is declined — its extra attack would be worth roughly a rung on st but it imposes Disadvantage on Int, Wis and Cha saves, which is the trade this run cannot take.
Configuration is the longbow with Archery, not dual-wield melee; that is what makes this body ranged and is why it reads two instances a round below the Ghostslayer on the same class.
Dread Ambusher's extra first-turn attack is amortized over four rounds, so it contributes about a quarter of an instance a round.
The Impermeable mutagen is likely unpickable at the level 11, 15 and 18 selections because of a typo in the shipped SpellLists.lsx; it is not part of this build's four.

Sagacity.split: Bloodhunter 14 (Order of the Mutant) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)
Sagacity.note: Bard first for three level-1 skills, Lore's three more, Expertise and Magical Secrets at 6, then Blood Hunter 14 with Sagacity raising Intelligence above the cap. The Bard half stops at caster level 6, so its slots are frozen at third tier for the whole run and its damage and area control are outrun on purpose.
Sagacity.strength: It covers the two-character skill problem from one body — six proficiencies, Expertise, Jack of All Trades on everything else — while still being a medium-armour body with Extra Attack and a Rite, so the partner is not forced to be the melee half. Every combat resource it has refills on the free rest rather than the 120-supply one.
Sagacity.wants: A body with real spell tiers. This one's caster half is frozen at third level, so its area control falls to 1 by Act II and it can never hold the pair's high-tier control.
uncertain: dark-augmentation lands only in Act III: it is Blood Hunter 10 and this body is at Blood Hunter 9 at character 15. That single level is the whole difference between this record's Act II save evidence and the mono-Blood-Hunter bodies'.
Mutagen selection fixed at build time: Sagacity and Celerity, which is why Investigation rises faster than the proficiency bonus alone would carry it.
Cutting Words is a Charm in SG_Charmed under Goon's overhaul and fails against charm-immune and Deafened creatures, so it is priced as a conditional rider rather than a universal one.
rsc falls to 2 in Act III because the Bard half is frozen at third-tier slots while the act's rung-3 row asks for 9th-tier restoration; the capability did not get worse, the bar moved.

Castigate.split: Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Profane Soul) / Barbarian 3 / Paladin 6

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite lands on one weapon hit and has no area form.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite lands on one weapon hit and has no area form.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite lands on one weapon hit and has no area form.

Castigate.note: A rapier front-liner that stacks Rage, Reckless Attack and Divine Smite on a Crimson Rite, and takes Paladin exactly as far as Aura of Protection. Raging costs it its pact spellcasting, so the Profane Soul half contributes Brand of the Sapping Scar and the curse list rather than a spell plan.
Castigate.strength: Aura of Protection in a two-body party covers the entire party, and it stacks with Lone Wolf's own save proficiencies rather than overlapping them; Reckless Attack's Advantage is scale-invariant where the Smite dice are not. Brand of the Sapping Scar makes the partner's one control spell land without spending anybody's concentration.
Castigate.wants: A crowd answer and a controller — this body is 0 on AoE and 1 on area control in every act, and it cannot cast at all while raging.
uncertain: Configuration fixed at build time: this body Rages from Act II, so its pact slots are not cast in combat and its AoE goes to 0. The Profane Soul patron is not named in the split; Hexblade is assumed, which adds the proficiency bonus to the next damage roll against a cursed creature and is not separately scored.

Whether Divine Smite fires while Raging is unverified. BG3 implements it as a weapon action rather than a cast, which is why it is scored; if it is blocked, Acts II and III lose about 5 raw a round and st II falls from 3 to 2.
Paladin is taken after level 1, so it grants no heavy armour and no Wis/Cha save proficiency — the save set is Blood Hunter's plus Lone Wolf's plus Resilient (Wisdom).
aura-of-protection is a pair-scope booster and non-stacking; if the partner is also a Paladin 6 the renderer will drop one and this body's saves are worth less than the record implies.

Sapping.split: Bloodhunter 11 (Order of the Profane Soul) / Barbarian 3 / Wizard 6
Sapping.note: The one Blood Hunter shape where the dip and the class want the same ability: Profane Soul casts off Intelligence and so does Wizard 6, so one score drives the curse DCs, the Brand retaliation, Dark Augmentation and the spell list at once. It does not Rage — Barbarian 3 is here for the d12 die, Danger Sense and the physical resistance, not for Reckless Attack.
Sapping.strength: Brand of the Sapping Scar puts blanket Disadvantage on one creature's saves through a free interrupt that spends no concentration, so the pair's single concentration slot is still free for the partner — that is the exact bottleneck a two-body party hits. Blood Maledict is slot-free hard control refilling on the free rest.
Sapping.wants: A body with high-tier slots. This one's Wizard half is frozen at caster level 6, so its own control tops out at third tier and it is rung 0 on single-target damage from Act II.
uncertain: Configuration fixed at build time: this body does not Rage, because raging would switch off both halves of its plan. Barbarian 3 contributes hit dice, Danger Sense and physical resistance only; the subclass is not named in the split and nothing subclass-specific is scored.
The Wizard school is not named in the split either. Nothing school-specific is scored, so this record is the generic Wizard 6 dip and would move if a school were fixed.
The Profane Soul patron is not named; Great Old One is assumed for the area Frighten on crits, which is not separately scored.
ctrl_a falls from 3 to 2 in Act III purely because the Wizard half is frozen at third-tier slots while the act's par rises to sixth through ninth. Nothing about the chassis got worse.

Counterpoint.note: Cleric 1 → Fighter 1 (heavy armour, Defence) → Cleric 14 → Bard 5. Arcane Initiate buys two wizard cantrips that Potent Spellcasting then scales, and Counterspell arrives on the Cleric list at domain level 5. It gives up every armour and weapon upgrade a martial domain would have handed it, and Cleric 14 never reaches Arcane Mastery.
Counterpoint.strength: The only Cleric that holds Counterspell natively, and Lone Wolf's second Reaction is the thing that pays for it — a duo has no wizard to park that reaction on, and one denied enemy cast is worth more than a round of this body's own damage. Magic Missile's darts are separate damage rolls, so the act's gear rider is collected five to seven times a cast rather than once.
Counterpoint.wants: A body that can hold the pair's second concentration slot for hard control, because this one spends its own on Spirit Guardians and has nothing at rung 4 on either control axis.
uncertain: Arcane Abjuration only turns or banishes celestial/elemental/fey/fiend, so its area-control rung is scored at 2 rather than 3 — against the wrong bestiary it is worth 0.

Spell Breaker is recorded as spell-breaker, a pair-scope partial. On its own a partial buys no rung, so index 8 stays at 4; it only moves the pair value beside a partner carrying a second partial or a blanket.

Magic Missile is scored auto-hit at 1/0.65 relative to par and at one instance per dart. If the renderer's gear constant was not meant to attach per dart, the Act II/III single-target rung falls by one.

Charnelwright.note: Cleric 1-6 → Fighter 3 → Cleric 7-17. Reaper doubles a single-target necromancy cantrip from level 1 and Improved Reaper extends that to every 1st-5th tier necromancy spell at 17; Blessed Strikes is taken over Divine Strike, because this body casts rather than swings. What it gives up is Extra Attack — Fighter 3 stops two levels short.
Charnelwright.strength: Control Undead converts an enemy into the third body a two-person party structurally does not have, off a Channel Divinity charge a short rest refunds, and Action Surge from Fighter 2 gives a third Action in the round it matters. Reaper turning Toll the Dead into a two-target cantrip is what keeps the filler actions — four of the eight per fight — from being dead weight.
Charnelwright.wants: A body with real single-target burst, because this one converts its whole pool into area and its boss answer never rises above par.
uncertain: Control Undead and Turn Undead both key on creature type. The Actions and control-single rungs assume the Act II Shadow-Cursed Lands and Act III undead density make it reliable; in a fight with no undead this body is two rungs lower on both.
Blessed Strikes is chosen over Divine Strike (Expansion offers the swap per subclass). Scoring the Divine Strike configuration instead would move necrotic weapon damage up and cantrip damage down.
Improved Reaper at Cleric 17 doubles 1st-5th tier single-target necromancy. It is credited only through the cantrip line, because the domain's best area spells are already 4-target.

Torpor.note: Cleric 1 → Fighter 1 → Cleric 14 → Bard 5. Deep Slumber is a 1st-level, upcastable, non-concentration area spell that leaves Torpor behind — quarter movement, no reactions, and one of attack/action/bonus action. Cleric 14 never reaches The Third Eye, so the psychic-vulnerability capstone is bought and not delivered.
Torpor.strength: Torpor applies to the enemy exactly the tax Lone Wolf lifts off you: a Torpored enemy gets one thing per turn while each of your bodies gets three. Inception spends a Channel Divinity charge to give the target disadvantage on the first save, which is what makes a duo's single controller land at all when there is no second caster to stack with.
Torpor.wants: A damage body, because this one's whole slot budget converts to control and its single-target line never clears par in any act.
uncertain: Deep Slumber's numbers come from the DTO documentation site rather than the installed pak; the area-control rung 4 rests on it being non-concentration.
Inception consumes the Channel Divinity charge when the spell is cast, so it competes with nothing else this domain wants — but it is a passive toggle and may fire on a spell you did not want it on.

Doomsayer.note: Cleric 1-14 then Bard 6. Eldritch Contagion is a bonus-action, no-concentration debuff on one enemy every round, and Prophecy of Doom does the same to a whole sphere off a Channel Divinity charge. The Bard tail arrives at 15 with only a secondary Charisma behind it, so Stormcalling's own save DCs are weak and it is taken for Countercharm, Song of Rest and short-rest Inspiration.
Doomsayer.strength: Two control engines that spend no concentration at all, which in a duo means the pair's two slots are still both free — that is the rung-4 clause on both control axes, and almost nothing else in the Cleric list satisfies it. The Eldritch Effect table's 'move or act, not both, and no reactions' is the mirror image of what Lone Wolf hands you.
Doomsayer.wants: A body that can actually kill things: this one's single-target line sits at rung 1 in every act and its area damage is ordinary.
uncertain: Every Eldritch Effect is rolled at random from an eight-entry table. The control rungs are scored on the table's average usefulness; a plan that needs a specific condition cannot use this domain at all.
Area control falls to 4 in Act III because Cleric 14 never prepares a 9th-tier Cleric spell and Bard 6 knows nothing above 3rd — the top two slots are upcast fodder only.
Domain level 6 grants advantage on saves against Charmed and Frightened, and Bard 6's Countercharm grants the same to both bodies. Neither has a booster id, so both contribute nothing to index 8.

Anvilward.note: Cleric 1 → Fighter 1 (Defence style) → Cleric 14 → Bard 5. Blessing of the Forge and Soul of the Forge each add a point of AC on top of heavy armour and a shield, and Soul of the Forge adds fire resistance at domain 6. Cleric 14 stops one level short of Saint of Forge and Fire, so the non-magical physical resistance never arrives.
Anvilward.strength: AC 23 by the end of Act I with no attunement spent, on a body that also casts the full Cleric list — against a crowd of three attacks a round that is the difference between taking the fight and losing half the party. Artisan's Blessing's reaction lets either body punch through physical resistance, which is the specific hole Absolute Wrath opens.
Anvilward.wants: Control at rung 4 or better, because this body's own area answer is one concentration spell and it has nothing that removes an enemy turn without paying for it.
uncertain: AC 23 assumes Plate plus a shield plus Blessing of the Forge on self plus Soul of the Forge plus the Defence style. Putting Blessing of the Forge on the partner's weapon instead drops this body to AC 22 and the durability ratio to 1.63, still rung 4 but at the band's floor.
A Wisdom Cleric wearing Plate does not meet its Strength requirement, so this body walks slowly. That is not priced anywhere in the model.

riders.name: Path to the Grave
riders.single_axis_reason: Vulnerability lands on one cursed creature and is consumed by the next damage instance it takes, so it cannot be spread over an area.

riders.name: Path to the Grave
riders.single_axis_reason: Vulnerability lands on one cursed creature and is consumed by the next damage instance it takes, so it cannot be spread over an area.

riders.name: Path to the Grave
riders.single_axis_reason: Vulnerability lands on one cursed creature and is consumed by the next damage instance it takes, so it cannot be spread over an area.

Deathknell.note: Cleric 1 → Fighter 1 → Cleric 14 → Bard 5. Sentinel at Death's Door turns a critical hit against either body into an ordinary hit, Wisdom-modifier times a long rest, and Circle of Mortality maximises every die that picks the partner back up. Cleric 14 forgoes Keeper of Souls and the 9th-tier domain pair.
Deathknell.strength: With Enemy Critical Hits on and exactly two bodies, one crit is how a fight is lost, and this is the only chassis in the Cleric list that deletes that outcome outright — using the second Reaction Lone Wolf hands you and would otherwise waste. Path to the Grave hands the partner's biggest single hit a vulnerability window off a short-rest charge.
Deathknell.wants: A partner whose damage arrives in one big instance, because Path to the Grave doubles exactly one hit and is wasted on a many-roll engine.
uncertain: Path to the Grave is credited to this body's own single-target line. In practice a duo spends it on the partner's biggest hit, where it is worth more and shows up on no axis at all.
Sentinel at Death's Door is scored as Rescue (it is aimed outward at the partner) and is not also counted in durability; the self-facing half of it is therefore unscored.

Witchbreaker.note: Cleric 1-8 → Bard 6 (Swords) at 9-14 → Cleric 9-14. Taking the Bard block in the middle band buys Extra Attack at character 14 rather than 20, which is the whole reason the split is ordered that way. Witch Hunter's Strike doubles against a concentrating target and hands back temporary hit points; Cleric 14 gives up the five-target Spell Shield at 17.
Witchbreaker.strength: Everything it does is aimed at enemy casters, which is what actually removes one of two bodies in this install — Spell Shield gives the partner resistance to spell damage and advantage on saves against spells for one short-rest charge, and in a two-person party that charge covers half the team. Rebuke Invoker turns Lone Wolf's spare Reaction into a punish every time something casts.
Witchbreaker.wants: An area answer: two attacks a round is all this body brings to a crowd until Extra Attack lands, and its area-control rung never rises above 2.
uncertain: Witch Hunter's Strike does not stack with the Divine Strike interrupt (the mod author's own caveat), so from Cleric 8 the two riders only combine if the Divine Strike action is used manually. The damage line assumes they are used on separate swings.

Spell Shield is recorded as spell-shield, a pair-scope partial rather than a blanket. Scored as blanket it would take this body to index 8 rung 5 in every act; as a partial it needs a second partial beside it to buy the rung.
Scored with a greatsword and no shield (AC 19). A longsword-and-shield configuration is AC 21 and one rung of single-target lower.

Loremaw.note: Cleric 1 → Fighter 1 → Cleric 14 → Bard 5. Cat's Cleric Changes gives Knowledge Magical Secrets at domain 6 and 10, which is where Fireball, Haste and Counterspell enter a Cleric's list; the concentration slot is spent on Haste rather than Spirit Guardians, and that choice is what the area line is scored against. Cleric 14 never reaches Divine Foreknowledge.
Loremaw.strength: Haste on the partner is the largest single action-economy purchase available to a two-person party, and Magical Secrets is the only route that puts it on a Wisdom chassis that is also the pair's healer. Fireball off the same list gives a Cleric the four-target burst its own spell table simply does not contain.
Loremaw.wants: A partner who converts an extra Action into real output — Haste on a body with one attack a round buys almost nothing.
uncertain: Blessings of Knowledge grants double proficiency in two of Arcana, History, Nature and Religion. None of those is a check the Skills axis scores, so the domain's headline skill feature is worth nothing on index 7 — the niche this seed was filed under is not supported by the rubric.

CCC does not state how many Magical Secrets picks land at domain 6 and 10, or which lists they draw from. Haste, Fireball and Counterspell are assumed available; if the selector is narrower, Actions falls from 3 to 1 and the area line falls a rung.

Holding Haste means this body cannot also hold Spirit Guardians. The area figures are scored on Fireball and its upcasts alone, which is why they are lower than a Spirit-Guardians Cleric's despite a bigger spell list.

Vigilkeep.note: Cleric 1-14 → Bard 5 → Barbarian 1 at 20.
