Preserve Life restores five times the Cleric level across the party off a Channel Divinity charge that a short rest refunds, and Disciple of Life inflates every levelled heal on top. Cleric 14 never reaches Supreme Healing, and Blessed Healer was patched down to self-only.
Vigilkeep.strength: Short Rest Full Heal is off, healing potions are nerfed and a long rest costs 120-plus supplies, so a repeatable out-of-combat heal on a short-rest clock is worth more here than in any ordinary run — it is the axis Lone Wolf actively makes worse, and this is the chassis that fixes it for both bodies.
Vigilkeep.wants: Control and area damage: this body has a rung-1 area-control line and nothing that removes an enemy turn, so the partner must be the one that shapes the fight.
uncertain: Barbarian 1 is scored as a hit die and a skill only. Rage blocks spellcasting in BG3, so the resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing that the dip appears to buy is unusable on any round this body casts — the durability rung rests on Preserve Life, not on Rage.
Durability credits one Channel Divinity charge per fight as self-directed healing, net of the Action it costs. Crediting both charges would put the ratio above 2.0 in Acts I and II.
Preserve Life heals the partner as well as the caster; it is scored in Rescue for the outward half and Durability for the self half, which risks double-counting one charge.

Dawnflare.note: Cleric 1-14 → Bard 6 (Lore). Radiance of the Dawn is an area radiant burst off a Channel Divinity charge, so it is spent twice a fight and refunded on every short rest; Potent Spellcasting at domain 8 puts Wisdom on every cantrip. Cleric 14 forgoes Corona of Light, and the Lore tail runs on a secondary Charisma.
Dawnflare.strength: A repeatable four-target burst that costs no spell slot at all is the resource shape a 120-supply long rest rewards, and Radiance of the Dawn is radiant — the least-resisted damage type in Act II under Absolute Wrath. Warding Flare and Cutting Words then spend both of Lone Wolf's Reactions on making single attacks miss, which is how a pair of two survives a crowd.
Dawnflare.wants: Hard control: this body burns its Reactions on mitigation and holds Spirit Guardians, so it has nothing that takes an enemy turn away outright.
uncertain: Warding Flare is scored at Wisdom-modifier uses per long rest, roughly 1.7 per fight, which is what holds durability at rung 3 rather than 4. If Listo's build makes it per short rest the rung rises.
In Act III the eight action-slots are all spent (two Channel Divinity, six levelled casts) with no filler left, so the caster's cantrip line contributes nothing that act.

Thornwarden.note: Cleric 1-8 → Ranger 3 (Beast Master) at 9-11 → Cleric 9-17. Nature is the only domain with Shillelagh on its own list, so Wisdom rolls the quarterstaff as well as the spell DC and no feat is spent buying the melee option; Blessed Strikes is taken over Divine Strike. What it buys the dip for is the Beast Master companion, and it pays three character levels of Cleric progression for it.
Thornwarden.strength: A duo is one body short of a party, and this is the cheapest permanent third body in the Cleric list — the companion scales with the ally curve (+34% HP, +1 AC per four levels) rather than sitting frozen, and Master of Nature at 17 takes a charmed enemy as a fourth. Shillelagh means the same Wisdom that drives the DC also swings, so nothing is split.
Thornwarden.wants: A body that removes enemy turns, because this one's control lines sit at 2 and its answer to a crowd is damage rather than denial.
uncertain: Listo made Shillelagh a level-1 spell that must be recast after a long rest, and cleric.md flags a conflict between the changelog and the docs on whether the effect is permanent. The melee option is scored as available; if uptime is worse than that, this body loses its only weapon line.
Whether the domain's level-1 druid cantrip pick can still take Shillelagh is unverified now that it is a levelled spell. Scored off the domain-spell grant instead, which is not in doubt.
Master of Nature at 17 is scored as one extra body. Expansion implements it as taking control of a charmed creature, so it is gated on Charm Animals and Plants landing first.

Lampsnuffer.note: Cleric 1-14 → Bard 6 (Stormcalling). Invocation of Night puts out every light in 9m and Blinds everything that fails a Constitution save for rounds equal to the Cleric level — fourteen of them, off a Channel Divinity charge. Cleric 14 stops three levels short of the Truesight and the Blind-and-Frighten aura, and the Bard tail runs on a secondary Charisma so Stormcalling's own DCs are weak.
Lampsnuffer.strength: Blind for the length of the fight, on a whole group, for a charge a short rest refunds and no concentration at all — which means the pair's two concentration slots are both still free, and a blinded enemy is one that cannot use the action economy Listo gave it to outnumber you. Ward of Shadows then spends Lone Wolf's spare Reaction imposing disadvantage on the one attack that would drop a body.
Lampsnuffer.wants: Damage. This body's single-target line never leaves rung 1 and its area damage is ordinary; it buys time rather than spending it.
uncertain: Invocation of Night fails against anything that cannot be Blinded. The rung-5 area-control claim assumes that is a minority of Listo's bestiary; against undead and constructs it is worth nothing.
Ward of Shadows' use count is not stated in the class file. It is scored at Wisdom-modifier uses per long rest, matching Light's Warding Flare, which is what holds durability at 3 rather than 4.

Stellar Bodies (the mod's own 4th-level spell, two orbiting stars, up to four when upcast) is not credited in the damage block; whether it holds concentration is unrecorded and Spirit Guardians already occupies the slot.
Area control falls to 4 in Act III because Cleric 14 never prepares a 9th-tier Cleric spell and Bard 6 knows nothing above 3rd.

Writ.note: Cleric 1-14 → Bard 6 (Stormcalling). Voice of Authority turns every levelled spell aimed at an ally into a free weapon attack from that ally, and Embodiment of the Law casts an enchantment as a bonus action Wisdom-modifier times a long rest. Cleric 14 never reaches Order's Wrath or the 9th-tier Dominate Person on the domain list.
Writ.strength: In a four-person party Voice of Authority picks one of three allies; with exactly one partner it is unconditional — every heal, every Aid, every Shield of Faith you cast buys a swing from the other body, every turn, for no resource. That is the one structural answer in the Cleric list to a duo being two Actions short of the party the encounters are tuned for.
Writ.wants: A partner who hits hard with a single weapon attack, because Voice of Authority hands out attacks and not Actions — it is wasted on a caster.
uncertain: The Actions rung 4 rests on Embodiment of the Law being a genuine extra cast in the round. It is Wisdom-modifier uses per long rest — about two a fight — not an at-will bonus action, so it is a third Action twice rather than every round.
Voice of Authority's implementation picks a random enemy in the ally's weapon range. Against a bad target that free attack is wasted, and none of the model can see it.
Ego Whip is a Mystra's-only domain spell and Mystra's is not installed, so the level-7 domain pair is one spell short.
Control-single falls from 4 to 3 after Act I: a bonus-action Command is no-concentration repeatable control, but one denied turn stops being decisive once enemies carry Act II action economy.

Concord.note: Cleric 1 → Fighter 1 (heavy armour, Defence) → Cleric 14 → Bard 5. Emboldening Bond is a permanent d4 on both bodies' attacks, checks and saves; Protective Bond lets this one teleport in and eat a hit aimed at the partner. The Fighter level exists because Peace grants the weakest armour of the strong domains, and Cleric 14 never reaches Expansive Bond, so the redirect is always taken at full damage.
Concord.strength: The bond is sized by proficiency bonus and there are exactly two of you, so it is always fully online — a party of four could never say that. Emboldening Bond is a blanket save booster on both bodies at once against the one axis Listo inflates hardest, and Protective Bond converts durability the pair's minimum was throwing away into a floor it does not otherwise have.
Concord.wants: A partner soft enough to be worth catching for: the bond only pays when this body is the tougher half, and it needs someone else to supply damage and area control, both of which sit at 1 here.
uncertain: Peace 3 is the Cleric's only Warding Bond, confirmed by pak sweep. Both bond ids are recorded from Act I because Warding Bond lands at character 4 and Protective Bond at character 7.
Aura of Purity is a Mystra's-only domain spell and Mystra's is not installed, so the level-7 domain pair is one spell short.

The redirect is scored only through the schema's doubling of the partner's rung. Protective Bond costs this body a Reaction per interception and takes the damage at full until Cleric 17, which it never reaches; neither cost shows on any axis.

Rhonasborn.note: Cleric 1-8 → Sorcerer 3 (Storm Sorcery) at 9-11 → Cleric 9-17. Haste is on the domain list, which is the reason the Sorcerer dip is here at all: three levels buy Twinned and Quickened, and Twinned Haste covers a two-person party entirely. The concentration slot is spent on Haste and never on Spirit Guardians, which is what the damage block is scored against. Strength grants heavy armour but, oddly for the domain, no martial weapons.
Rhonasborn.strength: Twinned Haste is the single largest action-economy purchase in the game for a party of two — in a four-body party Twinned reaches half the team, here it reaches all of it — and no other Cleric domain has Haste on its own list to twin. The Avatar of Battle line then hands the same body permanent resistance to non-magical physical at 17.
Rhonasborn.wants: A partner that converts Actions into damage, because this body deliberately spends its own concentration and most of its slots buying that partner extra turns; its own damage sits at rung 1 and 2.
uncertain: Whether BG3 Metamagic applies to a spell granted by a Cleric domain rather than by the Sorcerer class is not established here. Twinned Haste is the whole point of this split; if Metamagic is gated to Sorcerer-sourced spells, Actions falls from 4 to 3 and Rescue from 5 to 4 in Acts II and III.

Durability rises to 4 in Act II on Avatar of Battle II's resistance to non-magical physical during the transform, credited at two charges a long rest over three fights, and stays there in Act III on the permanent version at Cleric 17. That is a genuine back-loaded rise, not an act-relative artefact.
The domain grants heavy armour and no martial weapons, so there is no weapon line worth scoring; Divine Strike's weapon-type rider is bought and unused.

pools.name: Channel Divinity (Destructive Wrath)
pools.underspend_reason: Only one of the two levelled casts a fight is thunder or lightning; with the concentration slot on Spirit Guardians there is no second elemental cast for the other charge to maximise.

pools.name: Channel Divinity (Destructive Wrath)
pools.underspend_reason: Only one of the two levelled casts a fight is thunder or lightning; with the concentration slot on Spirit Guardians there is no second elemental cast for the other charge to maximise.

pools.name: Channel Divinity (Destructive Wrath)
pools.underspend_reason: Only one of the two levelled casts a fight is thunder or lightning; with the concentration slot on Spirit Guardians there is no second elemental cast for the other charge to maximise.

Stormanvil.note: Cleric 1-6 → Fighter 3 (Battle Master) at 7-9 → Cleric 7-17. Heavy armour, martial weapons, Divine Strike to 2d8 at 14, and Destructive Wrath maximising a thunder or lightning cast on a short-rest charge. The split stops two levels short of Fighter 5, so this front line never gets Extra Attack and swings twice a round against par's four.
Stormanvil.strength: Wrath of the Storm is a reaction that punishes every melee attacker, and Lone Wolf hands out two Reactions rather than one, so a body that wants to be hit gets paid twice a round for it. Destructive Wrath is a short-rest charge in a run where a long rest costs 120-plus supplies, and Goon moved its trigger to when damage is dealt so it is never spent on a miss.
Stormanvil.wants: Something that clears crowds. Two attacks a round is why this body's single-target line sits at rung 1 in all three acts — it is a durable anchor, not a killer.
uncertain: Scored with a greatsword and no shield (AC 19). Sword and board is AC 21 and one rung of durability higher, at the cost of roughly a fifth of the single-target line.

Action Surge is excluded from the damage block by rule 2 and priced on the Actions axis instead, where it is scored as rung 2 — a third Action once per short rest, with no multiattack or bonus-action engine under it to reach rung 3.
Superiority dice are omitted from the Act I block: Fighter 3 lands at character 9, one level past the end of the act band.
The thunder and lightning line is the body's whole elemental output. Spirit Guardians supplies a radiant or necrotic fallback, which is why no Absolute Wrath multiplier is applied.

pools.name: Channel Divinity (Destructive Wrath)
pools.underspend_reason: Only one of the two levelled casts a fight is thunder or lightning; with the concentration slot on Spirit Guardians there is no second elemental cast for the other charge to maximise.

Skyfall.note: Cleric 1-14 → Bard 6 (Stormcalling). The same domain played as a caster: Destructive Wrath maximises the area casts rather than a weapon rider, and the Stormcalling tail adds Thundercall, Conductor and Staccato Lightning on the same two damage types. Cleric 14 forgoes Stormborn, and the Bard half runs on a secondary Charisma.
Skyfall.strength: A maximised four-target thunder cast twice a fight off a charge two short rests refund is exactly the resource shape a 120-supply long rest rewards, and Wrath of the Storm plus Chorus of Thunder's Concussion give both of Lone Wolf's Reactions something to do every round. Concussion also strips the enemy's reactions, which matters more when there are only two of you to be reacted at.
Skyfall.wants: A partner with a damage type outside thunder and lightning, and a second concentration slot for hard control — this one holds Spirit Guardians and never removes an enemy turn outright.
uncertain: Thunder and lightning are this body's only real damage types once Spirit Guardians is stripped out. Under Absolute Wrath a partner sharing either type leaves the pair with no answer; no multiplier is applied here because the radiant fallback exists, but it is thin.
Chorus of Thunder and the Conductor line come from the DTO documentation site, and the pack entered Listo on a playtesting footing. They are credited in the control rungs, not in the damage block.
Act I spends only one Channel Divinity charge because a Cleric 8 casts two levelled spells a fight and only one of them is elemental.

Fourfold.note: Cleric 1-8 → Rogue 3 (Thief) at 9-11 → Cleric 9-17. Improved Duplicity at 17 puts four illusory copies on the field, moved with a bonus action, and Thief's Fast Hands adds a third bonus action on top of Lone Wolf's two. Before 17 this is the weakest chassis of the eight vanilla domains, and the Listo buff mod the docs recommend for Blessing of the Trickster is not installed.
Fourfold.strength: Enemy AI in this install selects by softness and there is no taunt, so four decoys on a two-body party is the closest thing to one — every attack spent on a duplicate is an attack not spent on the half of your party that dies. Rogue 1's Expertise arrives at character 9 and is most of what this body contributes outside a fight.
Fourfold.wants: A partner that can carry Acts I and II alone: everything this chassis is worth arrives at Cleric 17, and until then it has no armour grant, no weapon grant and no area control at all.
uncertain: Invoke Duplicity holds concentration in BG3, so the duplicates and Spirit Guardians cannot both be up. The damage block is scored on Spirit Guardians and the Act III durability and Actions rungs on the duplicates; the two configurations are mutually exclusive and the record cannot say so in one number.
Durability rises to 4 in Act III purely on four decoys absorbing attacks. That is a soak estimate, not a mitigation term the rubric names, and it is the softest number in this record.
Divine Strike is poison, which is among the most resisted types in the game. It is bought and effectively unused; the scored damage is Spirit Guardians and cantrips.

Duskvigil.note: Cleric 1 → Fighter 1 → Cleric 14 → Warlock 5. Twilight Sanctuary is a 9m sphere that hands 1d6 + Cleric level temporary hit points to every creature ending its turn inside, for one Channel Divinity charge that a short rest refunds. The Warlock tail arrives at 16 for two 3rd-level pact slots and Agonizing Blast, and Cleric 14 never reaches Twilight Shroud.
Duskvigil.strength: Every resource this body leans on refills on a short rest, in a run where a long rest costs 120-plus camp supplies and Short Rest Full Heal is off — the sanctuary covers both bodies at once because there are only two of them, and four Eldritch Blast beams across two Actions collect the act's gear rider eight times where par's greatsword collects it four.
Duskvigil.wants: Hard control. This body buys survival and sustain and never removes an enemy turn; its control rungs sit at 2.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is scored at four beams (character 5/10/17 plus the Expansion beam) times Charisma 16, which is a secondary stat on a Wisdom chassis. At Charisma 12 the Act III single-target rung falls to 1.

Twilight Sanctuary's temporary hit points refresh rather than accumulate, so durability credits one round's worth absorbed per round, not four rounds banked. The outward half is scored in Rescue and the self half in Durability, which risks counting one charge twice.

Endurance rises 2/3/4 because the short-rest half of the kit arrives late: pact slots and at-will Eldritch Blast only exist from character 16. That is a genuine back-loaded rise, not act-relative drift.

Hammerfall.note: Cleric 1-8 → Fighter 3 (Battle Master) at 9-11 → Cleric 9-17. Cat's Cleric Changes gives War Domain a real Extra Attack at domain 6, which no other Cleric in the list has, and War Priest stacks a bonus-action swing on top. Divine Strike reaches 2d8 at 14 and Avatar of Battle at 17 adds resistance to non-magical physical.
Hammerfall.strength: It is the only Cleric that clears single-target par, and it does it at character 6 — Extra Attack plus Lone Wolf's second Action is three to four swings a round on a body that still casts the whole Cleric list, heals, and wears plate. Guided Strike's +10 off a short-rest charge turns the swing that matters into a hit rather than a gamble.
Hammerfall.wants: Area control. This body has none at all — rung 1 in every act — and its answer to being outnumbered is to kill things one at a time.
uncertain: Extra Attack for War Domain comes from Cat's Cleric Changes, written for Listo. cleric.md flags that the published docs still deny it; the whole single-target result here depends on the mod behaving as the changelog says.
War Priest charges are a long-rest pool (six at Cleric 11), so the bonus-action swing is about two a fight, not one a round. Scored at pool over three fights.

Guided Strike's +10 to an attack roll is folded into the weapon line as a 6% uplift on the attack portion rather than a separate term; the rubric has no accuracy mechanic below the advantage multiplier.
Scored with a greatsword and no shield (AC 19, rising to rung 4 in Act III on Avatar of Battle's physical resistance).

Hazoretborn.note: Cleric 1-8 → Bard 6 (Swords) at 9-14 → Cleric 9-14. Zeal is the only domain with Fireball on its own list and Consuming Fervor maximises it, twice per short rest, from Cleric 6. The Bard block sits in the middle band so Extra Attack lands at character 14; Cleric 14 gives up Blaze of Glory.
Hazoretborn.strength: A maximised Fireball is 48 to 72 guaranteed damage on four targets for a charge two short rests refund — that is the whole shape a 120-supply long rest rewards, and it is the only Cleric line in the roster that clears area par by a factor of two in every act. Priest of Zeal scales its bonus swings on Wisdom, so the same stat that runs the spells runs the extra attacks.
Hazoretborn.wants: A body that is not fire. Consuming Fervor names fire or thunder, and under Absolute Wrath a partner sharing either leaves this pair with one resisted answer and no other.
uncertain: No Absolute Wrath multiplier is applied to the Fireball line, because Consuming Fervor explicitly names fire or thunder and that satisfies the rubric's second-damage-type escape. The thunder alternatives (Shatter, Destructive Wave) are materially weaker than Fireball, so the escape is real but not free; applying the 0.5 on half of encounters instead would cost one single-target rung in Act III.

Fireball is credited on both damage axes under rule 3 — full value on a single target for the boss line, four targets for the crowd line. Both readings use the same two Channel Divinity charges and cannot happen in the same fight.

Consuming Fervor is read from the installed pak (TooltipUseCosts 'ChannelDivinity:1'), so it is twice per short rest from Cleric 6 rather than the domain's own interrupt resource, which refunds itself.

Emberclock.note: Cleric 1-8 → Sorcerer 3 (Draconic Bloodline) at 9-11 → Cleric 9-17. The same domain played as a Wisdom caster rather than a front line: Strength stays at the 15 heavy armour needs and the damage is Consuming Fervor on an upcast Fireball, twice a fight, refunded on every short rest. Reaching Cleric 17 buys 9th-tier Cleric spells and Mass Heal; the Sorcerer dip buys Twinned and Quickened.
Emberclock.strength: Two maximised upcast Fireballs a fight cost no spell slot at all, and two short rests a long rest means six of them per rest cycle — the one resource shape that survives a 120-supply long rest economy. Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Greater Restoration then cover a two-person party completely for one Metamagic pick.
Emberclock.wants: Control and a front line. This body stands still, casts, and has nothing that stops an enemy reaching it.
uncertain: Skills falls 2/1/1. This body has no proficiency in any of the three recorded checks — Zeal grants none, a Sorcerer dip grants none, and the DC bands rise while an untrained Wisdom modifier does not. The fall is the rubric working, not an error.

Whether BG3 Metamagic reaches a spell granted by a Cleric domain rather than by the Sorcerer class is unestablished. Twinned Death Ward and Greater Restoration are Sorcerer-list spells here, so Rescue does not depend on it; nothing else in this record does either.
Fireball upcast damage uses BG3's +1d6 per level above 3rd, so 14d6 at a 9th slot, maximised to 84. Vanilla tabletop capping the upcast lower would cost one area rung in Act III.

Summerwarden.note: Druid 1-5, Peace Cleric 1-3, then Druid to 17: a bonus-action rescue engine built on the Balm of the Summer Court die pool (one die per Druid level, up to half of it spent in a single bonus action as heal and matching temp HP), with Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow maximising every die from Druid 6. It gives up almost all personal damage — it swings a Shillelagh quarterstaff and little else.
Summerwarden.strength: The whole kit is aimed at the other body and costs no Action: 8d6+Wis of heal and 8d6+Wis of temp HP in one bonus action, doubled in value by Lone Wolf's halved damage, and Lone Wolf's second bonus action lets it fire twice a round. Walker in Dreams is a free short rest for the party once per long rest, which is real money at 120+ supplies a camp, and Peace 3 adds an Emboldening Bond that a two-body party keeps online permanently.
Summerwarden.wants: A body that actually removes enemy action points — this one is single-target rung 1 and falls to 0, so the partner has to carry the whole tempo block.
uncertain: Rescue is capped at 5 by outward magnitude, not by form: Dreams has no prevention (no Death Ward on the Druid list) and Cleric 3 stops short of Greater Restoration. The Act II/III 5 rests on Hidden Paths (bonus-action extraction of the partner) reading as prevention in a duo.
Balm of the Summer Court is authored as ally-only (Rescue, never Durability) on the pak reading in druid.md; if it can be self-targeted, dur rises and rsc does not fall.
Circle of Dreams levels 15-20 are (unverified) in druid.md; the Act III row assumes nothing lands after Walker in Dreams at 14.

Tempestshell.split: Druid 14 (Circle of Stormchasers) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)

riders.name: Storm Shift (+Wis to L/T/C damage rolls)
Storm Shift (+Wis to L/T/C damage rolls)
Storm Shift (+Wis to L/T/C damage rolls)

Tempestshell.note: Bard 1 first for Dex+Cha saves and three skills, then Druid 5 / Bard 3, Bard to 6, Druid to 14. Storm Shift is the spine: one Wild Shape charge buys 3x Druid level temp HP until long rest and adds the Wisdom modifier to every Lightning, Thunder or Cold damage roll. It gives up the ninth-tier Druid list — spells known stop at 7th.
Tempestshell.strength: Storm Shift refreshes off a short-rest Wild Shape charge, so the temp-HP bar is available every fight rather than once a day, and the +Wis rider lands on every roll of a many-instance storm engine rather than once per cast. Stormchasers 10 makes its Lightning/Thunder/Cold ignore Resistance and treat Immunity as Resistance, which is the answer to Absolute Wrath for a two-body party that cannot field a spare damage type.
Tempestshell.wants: A body that holds the pair's concentration slot for hard control — this one spends its own on Conductor and has no answer above Hold Monster.
uncertain: Storm's Reach's damage table is locked at the level-12 value per druid.md, so the Act III row uses PB 5 dice with no per-die growth; if the lock is on the die count rather than the die, Act III st is a shade high.
Bard 6 in College of Stormcalling grants Conductor rather than Magical Secrets, so this body has no Revivify route; rsc 3 rests on Greater Restoration off a 5th-level slot at caster level 9+.
Rule 4's resisted-type multiplier is not applied from Act III because Stormchasers 10 ignores Resistance on its own damage; in Acts I-II the body carries bludgeoning Shillelagh as the second type.

Emberpact.note: Fighter 1 opens for Str+Con saves, heavy armour and the Druidic Warrior fighting style (Shillelagh plus Guidance without spending a slot on either); Druid to 5 for Conjure Animals, Warlock to 5 for Pact of the Chain and short-rest slots, then Druid to 14. It gives up spell tier — Warlock pact slots do not combine, so the Druid list stops at 7th.
Emberpact.strength: It is the largest body count a two-character party can field: the Wildfire Spirit is permanent and casts your spells from its own position, which is the only second point of AoE origin a duo can generate, on top of Conjure Animals, Summon Beast and a Chain familiar that gets Extra Attack at Warlock 5. Blazing Revival is an automatic second life, and in a run where losing either body ends the fight that is worth more than its damage.
Emberpact.wants: A body that can actually kill a boss — this one is single-target rung 1 in every act and buys its value in extra turns, not in damage.
uncertain: Cauterizing Flames and Blazing Revival levels are (unverified) in druid.md (5e puts them at 6 and 14); Blazing Revival is priced into the Act III durability ratio only.
Act III `act` 4 is claimed on body count (Wildfire Spirit + Conjure Animals + Summon Beast + a Chain familiar with Extra Attack), not on a third Action — Fighter 1 buys no Action Surge.
Agonizing Blast is priced at Cha 14, not the Warlock-primary 20+: this is a Wisdom body and Eldritch Blast earns its keep here on instance count, not on the modifier.

riders.name: Winter Spirit (+Wis Cold on spells, +1d6 Cold on melee)
Winter Spirit (+Wis Cold on spells, +1d6 Cold on melee)
Winter Spirit (+Wis Cold on spells, +1d6 Cold on melee)

Hoarfrost.note: Bard 1-3 for Dex+Cha saves, three skills and Expertise, then Druid to 11 for Winter's level-10 Prone clause, then Bard to 6 and Warlock to 3. Winter Spirit is one Action for 5x Druid level temp HP, +Wis Cold on every damage-dealing Druid spell and +1d6 Cold on melee; the cost is that the body never reaches a 7th-tier Druid spell.
Hoarfrost.strength: Winter 10 turns every failed save against a Cold Druid spell into Prone — mass hard control off spells it was casting anyway, costing no concentration, which is the one thing the pair's two concentration slots cannot buy twice. The temp-HP bar rides a short-rest Wild Shape charge, so it is up in every fight rather than once a day.
Hoarfrost.wants: A body with a non-Cold answer for the encounters Absolute Wrath layers cold resistance onto, and one that can close a boss out — this one's single-target control tops out at Hold Monster.
uncertain: The split names 'Bard 6' with no college; scored as a generic Bard 6 (Font of Inspiration, Song of Rest, Countercharm) with no college feature claimed. A Lore or Stormcalling pick would move ctrl_s and rsc up a rung.
Druid 11 / Bard 6 is caster level 17, so 8th- and 9th-level slots exist but the highest spell either class knows is 6th; every high-tier figure here is an upcast 6th-level Cold spell.
Rule 4's resisted-type multiplier is not applied: Shillelagh bludgeoning and Eldritch Blast force are both live second types, so cold resistance does not halve the whole engine.

riders.name: Winter Spirit (+Wis Cold on spells, +1d6 Cold on melee)
Winter Spirit (+Wis Cold on spells, +1d6 Cold on melee)
Winter Spirit (+Wis Cold on spells, +1d6 Cold on melee)

Rimeledger.note: Rogue 1 opens for four skill proficiencies and Expertise x2 at level 1 — the largest starting skill pick in the game — then Rogue 3 for Cunning Action, Druid to 11 for Winter's Prone clause, Bard 3 for a second Expertise pair and Bard to 6. It does not use Sneak Attack: the body swings a Shillelagh quarterstaff, which is not finesse.
Rimeledger.strength: Four Expertise slots on a Wisdom body is the only way a two-character party covers Perception against Listo's 15-25 trap band and still has a dialogue face; every check takes the party-best total, so a single body carrying both is worth more here than in a four-body party. Winter 10's Prone-on-failed-save arrives at Act III and is slot-free crowd control on top.
Rimeledger.wants: A body that carries the boss fight — this one's control back-loads to Act III and its single-target damage is flat par.
uncertain: The split names 'Rogue 3' and 'Bard 6' with no subclass or college; no subclass feature is claimed for either. A Swashbuckler or Lore pick would add skills the record does not credit.

Sneak Attack is deliberately scored at zero — Shillelagh's weapon list (club, quarterstaff, mace, morningstar, sickle, spear, trident) contains no finesse weapon, so the Rogue levels here are skills and Cunning Action only.
Winter's Prone clause lands at Druid 10, which this levelling order reaches at character 16; if Druid is front-loaded instead, ctrl_a 4 moves into Act II and skl falls a rung there.

Wrathcaller.split: Druid 14 (Circle of Wrath) / Bard 6 (College of Lore)

riders.name: Wrath stacks (+1 spell damage per stack, max = Wis mod)
Wrath stacks (+1 spell damage per stack, max = Wis mod)
Wrath stacks (+1 spell damage per stack, max = Wis mod)

Wrathcaller.note: Bard 1-3 first for Dex+Cha saves, six skill proficiencies and Cutting Words, then Druid to 5, Bard to 6 for Magical Secrets, then Druid to 14. Aspects of Wrath is a slot-free scaling cantrip engine that builds Wrath stacks (max = Wisdom modifier, each +1 spell damage); it buys no summon-free durability and no temp HP.
Wrathcaller.strength: Cutting Words is a reaction-priced debuff and Lone Wolf hands this body two reactions a round off a short-rest Inspiration pool, so it can subtract a die from two enemy attacks or saves every round without spending an Action or its concentration. Magical Secrets at Bard 6 — four levels early — buys Revivify or Hypnotic Pattern outright, which is what a duo with no Cleric otherwise cannot have.
Wrathcaller.wants: A body that can eat hits: this one is a d8 in medium armour with no mitigation layer, and the pair's Durability floor will be whichever half is softer.
uncertain: druid.md records Circle of Wrath's documentation as stopping at level 14, so 15-20 is (unverified); the Act III row claims nothing past Eye of the Storm.

Durability 2 is the honest arithmetic for a d8 body at par AC with no mitigation layer (pool ratio 1.15/1.20/1.14 against par), and sits on the 2/3 band edge in Acts I-II — a single point of magic AC would move it to 3.
The Bard 6 Magical Secrets picks are scored as Revivify (rsc 3 from Act II) and Hypnotic Pattern (ctrl_a); a different pair of picks changes both.

Deepwell.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Land) / Barbarian 1 / Paladin 2

riders.name: Divine Smite off Druid slots
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides a melee weapon hit and cannot be delivered to a group; the same slots are scored on aoe as area casts instead, which is why aoe_raw carries the whole damage share on its own.

riders.name: Divine Smite off Druid slots
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides a melee weapon hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as area casts instead.

riders.name: Divine Smite off Druid slots
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides a melee weapon hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as area casts instead.

Deepwell.note: Barbarian 1 opens for Str+Con saves and a d12 hit die, Paladin 2 bolts Divine Smite onto every Druid slot, and Druid runs to 17 for Natural Recovery — the only in-adventuring-day slot refund in the class. Rage is scored as unused: a raging body cannot cast, and this one is a full caster.
Deepwell.strength: Natural Recovery turns two short rests into a second and third spell pool, which is what a run charging 120+ supplies a long rest actually pays for; Divine Smite converts those refunded slots straight into melee damage off a Shillelagh quarterstaff, so the pool never sits idle whichever way the fight goes.
Deepwell.wants: A body that covers Perception and town dialogue — this one is skills rung 1 in every act and has nothing but a Barbarian's two proficiencies.
uncertain: Rage is scored as contributing nothing on Durability: it grants physical resistance but forbids spellcasting, and this body's whole plan is slots. If a Listo change lifts that restriction, dur rises a rung in every act.
Natural Recovery's charge growth (2/3/5/7...) is taken from druid.md; the Act III end 4 rests on those charges restoring enough slot level across two short rests to cover a hard fight on their own.
The Paladin 2 oath is unspecified in the split, so no oath feature or Channel Oath option is claimed — only Divine Smite and Lay on Hands.

riders.name: Divine Fury (+1d6 + half Barb level, first hit each turn while raging)
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Fury fires on the first hit each turn only, so it cannot be spread across a group; the Druid slots that feed aoe are scored there in full.

riders.name: Divine Fury (+1d6 + half Barb level, first hit each turn while raging)
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Fury fires on the first hit each turn only; the Druid slots that feed aoe are scored there in full.

riders.name: Divine Fury (+1d6 + half Barb level, first hit each turn while raging)
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Fury fires on the first hit each turn only; the Druid slots that feed aoe are scored there in full.

Moonhide.note: Barbarian 1-3 first for Str+Con saves and Zealot, then Druid to 17. The Wild Shape Overhaul makes Barbarian rage strikes and Reckless Attack work inside beast form, and a raging body cannot cast anyway — so the two halves stop competing. It gives up damage scaling: WSO deleted the vanilla Wild Shape damage bonus, so the beast routine is close to flat.
Moonhide.strength: Two full extra HP bars per fight off a short-rest Wild Shape pool, taken at physical resistance while raging, on a body the enemy AI will preferentially target anyway — and Zealot's Warrior of the Gods lets the partner pick this body up with no Revivify scroll, which is the exact failure mode a two-character party loses runs to.
Moonhide.wants: A body that scales its damage: this one's beast attacks are flat and fall from rung 2 to rung 1 across the run, so the partner has to be the one still growing in Act III.
uncertain: WSO gives base beast damage only for CR 1/2 (2d4) and CR 1 (2d6); CR 2 and CR 3 figures are inferred at 2d8 plus the form's rising attack ability. The Act II/III st rows are the least anchored numbers in this record.

Durability 5 rests on two Wild Shape bars per fight (Moon's 2 charges per short rest) at a beast-form AC of 15 against par 17, with one Rage per fight halving physical damage. If excess damage carried over from a broken form, or if beast AC is lower than 15, the ratio drops toward rung 4.
Rage is authored as spent 1 of 3 per fight because a Rage lasts the whole four rounds; the pool is long-rest so the 3-per-cycle limit is what binds.
druid.md flags that WSO was built expecting `5R Druid` (not installed) to restore Primal Strike and Fount of Moonlight; Moon 6's Primal Strike is claimed as making beast attacks magical only.

Undertow.split: Druid 14 (Circle of the Sea) / Barbarian 1 / Monk 5
Undertow.note: Barbarian 1 opens for Str+Con saves, Monk runs to 5 for Extra Attack, Flurry of Blows and Stunning Strike, then Druid to 14 for Wrath of the Sea and Oceanic Gift. Monk's Dextrous Attacks overrides Shillelagh, so the body punches on Dexterity and spends Wisdom on AC, the Ki save DC and Crashing Wave. It gives up spell tier — the Druid list stops at 7th.
Undertow.strength: Monk Unarmoured Defence puts it at AC 20 with no armour, no shield and no gold at Listo's 4x prices, and Lone Wolf's second bonus action doubles both the Flurry engine and Wrath of the Sea's Crashing Wave. Stunning Strike is slot-free hard control on a short-rest clock, which is the one kind of control that never competes with the pair's two concentration slots.
Undertow.wants: An area answer for Act I — this one is aoe rung 0 until the Druid list opens up, so the partner has to be the crowd body early.
uncertain: Crashing Wave is authored as a Constitution save for half (Nd6 Cold, N = Wis mod) and scored with the save-based single-target factor 0.775/0.65. druid.md states the save and the push but not whether a success negates outright; if it negates, st falls about 8% in every act.

ctrl_s 5 in Act II is claimed on Stunning Strike as slot-free hard control on a short-rest clock, sitting alongside Hold Monster at Druid 9 — the rubric's Act II rung-5 clause is written around Chains of Carceri, which is the same shape.

Ki 6 is scored as fully spent on Flurry and Patient Defence for damage/durability and also as the Stunning Strike budget for ctrl_s, which rule 3 as amended permits for a fungible resource; a single fight cannot in fact do both at once.

Tideturn.split: Druid 14 (Circle of the Sea) / Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul)
Tideturn.note: Sorcerer 1 opens so that Constitution and Charisma come free from the class and Lone Wolf's +4 can go on Wisdom and Dexterity, then Druid to 5 and Sorcerer to 3 for Metamagic and the Peace domain's Warding Bond. Favored Soul is taken for its level-1 medium armour and shields, which a Sea Druid otherwise has anyway — what it really buys is Warding Bond and Twinned Spell on a Wisdom chassis.
Tideturn.strength: Wrath of the Sea gives a Constitution-save push on a bonus action with no concentration and no slot, and Lone Wolf's second bonus action fires it twice a round — so the pair's two concentration slots stay free for Evard's Black Tentacles and Hold Monster rather than being spent on soft control.
Tideturn.wants: A body that can see and talk: this one has no Perception proficiency at all and reads rung 1 on Skills from Act II.
uncertain: Crashing Wave is scored as a Constitution save for half at the single-target factor 0.775/0.65; druid.md states the save and the 5m push but not whether a success negates.

The Favored Soul domain is authored as Peace, which sorcerer.md establishes as the only route to Warding Bond in the class (`LHB_FavoredSoul_Domain_Peace` at Sorcerer 3). Choosing Life instead trades the redirect block for Revivify at Sorcerer 5 and would raise rsc a rung in Act I.
Favored Soul's Extra Attack at Sorcerer 6 lands at character 18 and is redundant with Druid 5's Wild Strike; nothing is claimed for it.

Totemcall.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Shepherd) / Ranger 3 (Beast Master)
Totemcall.note: Ranger 1 opens for three skill proficiencies and martial weapons, Ranger 3 buys the Beast Master companion, then Druid runs to 17. Its own damage is negligible in every act — everything it is worth is on the board in other bodies, and rule 2 scores none of that here.
Totemcall.strength: It fields more actors than any other body in the list: Conjure Animals and Summon Beast are non-concentration and last until long rest, Flock of Familiars adds more, and the Beast Master Panther re-summons on a *short* rest, uses your proficiency bonus, saves like a PC and takes ability score improvements when you do. Every Spirit Totem is an aura pointed at the other character, which in a party of two is a party-wide buff.
Totemcall.wants: A body that removes enemy action points on its own turn — this one is single-target rung 1 in all three acts and buys its value in other actors.
uncertain: The Hawk Totem grants advantage on Perception, which is worth roughly +3.5 on the 15-25 trap band but is not a modifier; the `skills` map records the flat number only, and index 7 is set to agree with the map rather than with the advantage.

act 4 in Act III is claimed on 9th-tier upcast Conjure Animals (druid.md: upcasting conjures more animals) plus a short-rest-refreshing Panther, not on a third Action — the rubric's Act III rung-4 row is written around Action Surge.
Mighty Summoner's level is (unverified) in druid.md; nothing is claimed for it beyond the summons already counted under `act`.
Guardian Spirit and Faithful Summons are (unverified) and are scored as absent.

riders.name: Symbiotic Entity (+1d6 on weapon attacks, Halo doubled)
Symbiotic Entity (+1d6 on weapon attacks, Halo doubled)
Symbiotic Entity (+1d6 on weapon attacks, Halo doubled)

Sporeblight.note: Druid 1 opens for Int+Wis saves and a Perception proficiency, Zeal Cleric 1-3 buys heavy armour, martial weapons and Priest of Zeal's bonus-action attack, then Druid runs to 17. Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Constitution and Dexterity rather than Wisdom, so two Act I feats are spent bringing Wisdom to 20 — that is what buys the four-disjoint save set.
Sporeblight.strength: Symbiotic Entity is 4 temp HP per Druid level off a short-rest Wild Shape charge, so a 68-point buffer is up in every fight, and it doubles Halo of Spores — which fires on a *reaction*, and Lone Wolf hands this body two of those every round for free. The Dealer's Choice variant lets Halo and Symbiotic Entity carry different damage types, which is the cheapest answer to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances in the class.
Sporeblight.wants: A face and a scout: this body has one skill proficiency that matters and is rung 1 on Skills in every act.
uncertain: Spreading Spores is scored at three targets a round and as coexisting with Halo of Spores; in vanilla BG3 hurling the spores consumes Symbiotic Entity, and druid.md does not say whether the Dealer's Choice variant changes that. If it does consume it, aoe drops a rung in Acts II and III.

Halo of Spores is authored as firing on both of Lone Wolf's reactions every round, at half damage on a successful save (the Dealer's Choice change). That is two instances a round of gear-constant income and is the single largest contributor to the Act III st ratio.

The four-disjoint save set costs two Act I feats spent on Wisdom ASIs, because Lone Wolf's +4 is placed on Constitution and Dexterity instead. Placing it on Wisdom instead drops sav to a three-disjoint set and frees both feats.

act 4 in Act III is claimed on body count (Conjure Animals upcast, Summon Beast, familiar, four Fungal Zombies); the rubric's Act III rung 5 wants uncapped undead, which Spores' Animate Dead at Druid 5 might reach under `Animate Dead++` — not established from the class file.

Starcompass.split: Druid 14 (Circle of the Stars) / Bard 5 / Barbarian 1
Starcompass.note: Bard 1 opens for Dex+Cha saves and three skills with Expertise at Bard 3, then Druid to 12 for Cosmic Omen and Twinkling Constellations, then Bard 5 and Barbarian 1. Rage is scored as contributing nothing — a raging body cannot cast, and everything this one does is a slot or a Wild Shape charge.
Starcompass.strength: Listo's `Star Druid Tweaks` moves Cosmic Omen onto a *short* rest, so three or four swings of plus-or-minus 1d6 on an attack or a saving throw are available every fight rather than once a day — in a two-body party where one failed save ends the run, that is insurance you can actually afford to spend, and it stacks with Song of Rest and short-rest Bardic Inspiration on the same clock.
Starcompass.wants: A body that can take a hit: this one is a d8 caster at par armour with no mitigation layer, and Durability is the pair's weaker half.
uncertain: Durability 2 is the 2/3 band edge, not a clear rung: the eHP ratio is 1.18 / 1.22 / 1.16 for a d8 caster at par AC 17 with Constitution 18 from Lone Wolf. I rounded down here and on Circle of Wrath so the two mitigation-free Druids read alike; a single point of magic AC moves both to 3.

Barbarian 1 is scored as a multiclass node (weapons and shields only). If it were instead the level-1 class it would still give a four-disjoint save set, but the three Bard skill proficiencies and both Expertise picks would go, dropping skl to about 1 in every act.

The Act II aoe rise to rung 4 and the Act III fall are both real: Twinkling Constellations at Druid 10 lets Dazzling Breath and Luminous Arrow run side by side, and Breath then freezes at 4d6 while par keeps climbing.
The split names 'Bard 5' with no college; no college feature is claimed beyond Font of Inspiration, Song of Rest and Expertise.

Quiverstorm.note: A Sharpshooter longbow Fighter whose whole rider budget is the ten short-rest Arcane Arrows, with Gloom Stalker's opener and a Rogue 3 tail for Sneak Attack. It buys a large repeatable rider pool and pays for it with a low base damage die and no spell list at all.
Quiverstorm.strength: Ten Arcane Arrows come back on every short rest, which is the clock that matters when a long rest costs 120+ supplies — and because a Bursting Arrow is one attack plus a splash on the neighbours, each arrow collects the act's gear constant three times where par's Fireball collects it four for a whole cast.
Quiverstorm.wants: A body that will hold the pair's one concentration slot and answer crowds with real area control, because this one is 1 on control-area in every act.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.
Arcane Shot damage taken as a flat 2d6 rider; the class file does not state it, and Arcane Shot Improved (+2d6) sits at Fighter 18, which this split never reaches.
The AoE reading spends every arrow as Bursting Arrow and assumes two additional targets inside the 3m splash. Rule 3 makes that legitimate as potential, but a looser pack would drop the rung.
Assassin's crit-on-surprised and advantage-before-first-turn are not routine and are excluded from the raw.

Rallying Horn.note: A greatsword Banneret that spends its Action Surge on the partner rather than on itself, with Thief 3 for a third bonus action. It gives up every spell list and both control axes for pure economy and a short-rest outward heal.
Rallying Horn.strength: Inspiring Surge turns one Action Surge into the partner's reaction attack, and in a two-body party there is exactly one recipient, so none of the ally-count scaling is wasted; Rallying Cry then heals that same partner for the full Fighter level on the short-rest clock Second Wind already runs on.
Rallying Horn.wants: A body that brings control on both axes and can hold concentration, because this chassis is 1 on control-single and 0 on control-area in every act.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.
Sneak Attack counted once a round (the on-turn use only); a greatsword Banneret rarely generates the off-turn reaction attack the Cunning Strike rework allows.
Inspiring Surge reaches two allies only at Banneret 18; this split stops at Fighter 17, so it stays one.

Envoy.note: A Fighter 11 core opened at Fighter 1 for heavy armour, with a six-level Bard block bought purely for double Expertise and a Paladin 3 tail for smites. Its 22 sits on Charisma, not on the stat that rolls the attack, and the damage arithmetic shows it.
Envoy.strength: Two characters have to clear every check in the campaign, and Expertise on Perception plus Expertise on Persuasion is the only thing in this split that a partner cannot respec into cheaply — while Fighter 11 still keeps the body on the front line rather than making it a pure face.
Envoy.wants: A partner who out-damages it, since this body deliberately trades single-target output for the skill coverage a duo cannot otherwise buy.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.
The split names no subclasses, so the Banneret address is carried but no Banneret feature is scored; Royal Envoy's doubled Persuasion is NOT in the skills map, which uses Bard Expertise instead.
Feat count taken as 7: floor sums give 6 and Fighter 11's off-cadence feat adds one. The brief's worked example calls 11/6/3 six.
Level order assumed Fighter 1-5, Bard 1-6, Fighter 6-11, Paladin 3 — Expertise lands at character 8.

Commander.note: Five superiority dice on a short rest, spent on Commander's Strike and Trip Attack, with a Swords Bard 3 tail for Flourishes and Expertise. It has no spell list worth the name and buys everything it does off one small refreshing pool.
Commander.strength: Every resource on this body refills on a short rest — dice, Second Wind, Action Surge — which is the only clock that pays when a long rest costs 120+ supplies; and Commander's Strike spends one of six attacks to give the partner a whole extra attack, which is a better trade in a duo than in a party of four.
Commander.wants: A body that answers crowds, because this one is 1 on both AoE and control-area in every act and cannot clear the added-encounter bodies Listo throws at a duo.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.
Commander's Strike is scored as Actions, not as this body's damage — the partner's attack is theirs.
Improved Combat Superiority (d12) is Battle Master 18; Fighter 17 stops one level short, so the die stays d10 in Act III.

Warmage.note: Fighter 11 opened at level 1 for heavy armour and Strength/Constitution saves, with a six-level Wizard block for Haste, Counterspell and one Fireball a fight, and Paladin 3 for smites. The Wizard levels cost it hit points and one action-slot a fight.
Warmage.strength: Haste on the partner is the one thing in this split a martial cannot buy any other way, and in a duo the partner is 50% of the action economy — a second Action on them is worth more than a third on this body, which already has Action Surge.
Warmage.wants: A body with real rescue, because this one has none until Paladin 3 arrives in Act III and even then only Lay on Hands.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.
The split names no subclasses; the Battle Master address is carried but no superiority dice are scored.
Shield is not scored into AC: eleven slots cannot fund a cast most rounds while also paying for Haste and one Fireball.

Brute.note: Sword-and-board Fighter 11 with Brute Force as its only damage rider, Heavy Armour Master on top of plate and shield, and a Cleric 6 block for Spirit Guardians and outward healing. Brutish Durability at Fighter 7 puts a d6 on every save it ever rolls.
Brute.strength: Heavy Armour Master's flat reduction is worth 1.6x effective HP against the three crowd hits a round Listo's added encounters actually deal, and Lone Wolf has already halved the number it subtracts from — the two stack in the direction a duo needs, because there is no taunt and no spare body.
Brute.wants: A partner that carries the pair's damage, since this chassis buys its floor by giving up almost everything on both tempo axes.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.
The split names no subclasses. Brute Force and Brutish Durability are scored from the address; if the body is not actually a Brute the +1d4/+1d6 rider and the blanket save booster both go.
Act II spends none of the Cleric slots on damage (to_damage 0.0); they are the body's rescue and control budget.

Pikewall.note: A polearm Cavalier opened at Cleric 1 for Wisdom/Charisma saves, heavy armour and Twilight Sanctuary, then eighteen Fighter levels of reaction engine — Unwavering Mark, Warding Maneuver, Hold the Line and Vigilant Defender. It has no spell list past level 1 slots.
Pikewall.strength: Lone Wolf hands every body a second Reaction and a second Bonus Action, and this is the one chassis built to spend both every round: two Polearm Master strikes and an opportunity attack on anything that moves inside its reach, while Twilight Sanctuary temp-HPs the partner every round for a Channel Divinity a short rest refunds.
Pikewall.wants: A ranged body that can kill what this one has pinned, and something that answers crowds beyond a zone of opportunity attacks.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.

One opportunity attack a round is counted from Act II, when Hold the Line makes enemies provoke on any movement inside reach; Act I counts none. This is the single biggest assumption in the raw and it is worth one combat log.
Warding Maneuver is scored as rescue-4 prevention in Act II; its Constitution-modifier uses are long-rest, which is why it falls to 3 in Act III.

Edgecase.note: A crit-fishing greatsword Champion with a two-level Barbarian node bought for Reckless Attack, taken after Fighter 1 so heavy armour survives. Everything it has goes into the attack roll; it has no rescue, no area damage and no control.
Edgecase.strength: Reckless Attack is repeatable advantage, which is one of the very few things that does not cancel against par — 1.35x on the whole raw, every round, on a body that already swings six times — and an 18-20 crit range plus Heroic Warrior's free reroll every turn compounds on top of it.
Edgecase.wants: A partner that can heal or redirect, because Reckless Attack hands every enemy advantage back and this body has 0 rescue and no answer once it is the one being focused.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul (FeatsOverhaul.pak): Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, gated only on HasHeavyArmor - the convention was right. Great Weapon Master is NOT: it is +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty), a toggle whose expected value against par AC is roughly neutral in Act I and negative from Act II. It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.

Reckless Attack taken as routine, so the x1.35 advantage multiplier is applied to the whole weapon raw; the mirrored cost (enemies attack it with advantage) is priced into the durability ratio at 0.65/0.84.
Rage counted at two charges across three hard fights, so its physical resistance is worth roughly x1.5 rather than x2 on the durability ratio.

Borrowed Time.note: Opened at Artificer 1 so Battle Ready puts Intelligence on the weapon's attack and damage, which is the same stat Timeless Knowledge's sorcery points and Alacrity's initiative run off - a genuinely single-stat Fighter. It gives up heavy armour to do it, since Fighter is the multiclass node here.
Borrowed Time.strength: Borrowed Time grants an Action to any entity you choose, and in a two-body party there is exactly one worth choosing; the Steel Defender then imposes disadvantage on attacks aimed at that same partner, so one chassis supplies both the extra Action and the reason the partner survives to use it.
Borrowed Time.wants: A body that can hold concentration and answer crowds, because this chassis is 0 on AoE in every act and carries only three distinct proficient saves.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.

Borrowed Time and Action Surge cannot be used in the same turn, and the recipient is Desynchronized for two turns afterwards (one attack, action OR bonus action, half movement). The extra Action is scored as real but not free.

Borrowed Time reads 'any entity you choose', so aiming it at an ENEMY is a net control play - they gain one Action and lose most of two turns. Scored at control-single 3 rather than 4 because the Action is handed over first.
The Steel Defender is excluded from the damage axes under rule 2 and scored on Actions instead.
Chronobreak is Fighter 18 and this split stops at 17, so the mass Borrowed Time never arrives.
This subclass entered Listo 'for testing' per the changelog and is the least battle-tested option in the Fighter file.

Revenant Echo.note: Fighter 11 opened at level 1 for heavy armour, with the echo as a second threatened zone and Unleash Incarnation converting every Attack action into an extra melee strike. Wizard is scored as Evocation and Paladin 3 as Oath of Devotion; the split names neither.
Revenant Echo.strength: The echo is the closest thing to a third body a martial can field: it occupies a space 9m away, flies, is immune to conditions, and Shadow Martyr lets it eat an attack aimed at the partner once per short rest - which is the only reason a duo's squishier half survives being caught out of position.
Revenant Echo.wants: Real area damage and a second control axis, because this chassis is 0-1 on AoE and its whole kit points at one target at a time.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.

Unleash Incarnation is counted as this body's own extra attack rather than as the echo acting, at Constitution-modifier uses per long rest, so one a fight. If it reads as a summon's attack, rule 2 excludes it and single-target drops.
Legion of One (Echo Knight 18) was never implemented by the mod and Echo Avatar (7) is deliberately absent under Listo's RAW progression file, so neither is scored.
Sentinel is assumed for the echo's opportunity-attack lockdown - the mod author flags it as the intended pairing - which is what carries control-single 3.

Warcaster.note: Sword-and-shield Eldritch Knight with every school restriction removed, so it prepares from the full Wizard list; War Magic at 5 and Improved War Magic at 12 fold a cantrip and then a levelled spell into the Attack action. The Bladesinging levels are bought for slots only - Bladesong cannot run in the heavy armour this body wears.
Warcaster.strength: It is the only Fighter that turns Action Surge into a second spell, and with Lone Wolf already granting a second Action that is three passes of attack-plus-cast a round - a duo cannot field a separate caster, so a front-liner that carries Fireball, Haste and Counterspell itself is covering a whole missing body.
Warcaster.wants: Any outward rescue at all: the Wizard list has none, this chassis scores 0 on rescue in every act, and a duo that loses either half loses the fight.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.

Bladesong is NOT scored: it forbids medium and heavy armour and shields, and this body wears plate and a shield. The Wizard 3 block therefore buys slots and nothing else, which makes the Bladesinging parenthetical close to inert on this split.
Booming Blade scales on CHARACTER level (1d8/2d8/3d8 at 5/11/17) and is counted once a round, since PHB2024 War Magic is once per turn and Action Surge - which resets it - is excluded by rule 2.
Shield is folded into AC at roughly +1 average rather than +5, since half the slot pool is already booked to damage.
Whether Expansion's Improved War Magic at 18 and the OneDnD one at 12 stack is unverified in the class file; Fighter 17 reaches neither of the 18s.

Kinetic.note: Fighter 11 with a Psionic Energy pool sized at twice the proficiency bonus, spent almost entirely outward: Protective Field reduces damage to an ally within 9m, on their turn, from range. Wizard is scored as Evocation and Paladin 3 as Oath of Devotion; the split names neither.
Kinetic.strength: Lone Wolf hands every body a second Reaction and this is one of very few martials with something worth spending it on that is not an attack - Protective Field is mitigation aimed at the OTHER character, which no amount of this body's own armour can substitute for when there is no taunt and no spare body.
Kinetic.wants: A partner that brings crowd damage, because this chassis is 0-1 on AoE and its control is a single-target prone routine.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.
Protective Field is scored as rescue only, never as this body's own durability - the rubric forbids scoring one feature on both, and the reaction niche points it outward.
Psionic dice are twice the proficiency bonus on a LONG rest with one regained per short rest, so a fight gets pool/3 + 1: three, four and five by act.
Psionic Strike is once per turn and rides an existing attack roll, so it adds damage but no instance.
Bulwark of Force (15) and Telekinetic Master (18) are past Fighter 11 and are not scored.

Dragonrider.note: A greatsword Fighter whose subclass is really a permanent third combatant: the amethyst dragon shares your initiative, acts on its own without costing a bonus action, and grows with level. Rogue 3 adds Fast Hands and Sneak Attack; the dragon costs camp supplies on top of a 120-supply long rest.
Dragonrider.strength: Rallying Surge turns one Action Surge into a reaction attack for up to three allies, and in a duo that means the partner AND the dragon both act off it - a two-body party gets the full value of a feature written for a party of four, while the dragon resummons on a short rest rather than a long one.
Dragonrider.wants: Area damage and outward rescue: this chassis is 0 on AoE in every act and has nothing that keeps the partner up.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.
The dragon and its Gravity Breath are excluded from BOTH damage axes under rule 2 and scored on Actions instead, which is why AoE reads 0 despite a 9m cone being available four to five times a day.

Endurance is 4 rather than 5 because camp-supply cost scales with camp population and a long rest already costs 120+; the dragon is the only chassis feature in this batch that makes resting more expensive.
The mod author warns the dragon uses custom Osiris scripting, very likely needs a fresh playthrough, and pathfinds badly indoors. Treat the whole subclass as less stable than its numbers suggest.
Enduring Commander (18) and two-ally Inspiring-style surges are past Fighter 17 and are not scored.

Runecarver.note: Five runes, every one invocable twice per short rest from Rune Knight 15, on a body that also toggles Reckless Attack from a three-level Zealot node taken after Fighter 1. Rune save DCs run off Constitution, not Intelligence, which is the one stat this build was buying anyway.
Runecarver.strength: Almost the entire kit is on the short-rest clock and Master of Runes doubles it - in a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies, a chassis whose control, mitigation and damage riders all refill for free between fights is spending a different currency from everyone else.
Runecarver.wants: Area damage and outward healing, because this chassis is 0 on AoE in all three acts and its only outward tool is a save-forcing reroll.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.
Reckless Attack is taken as routine (x1.35 on the whole weapon raw) and its mirror is priced into durability at 0.65/0.84. It is a Barbarian 2 toggle with no Rage requirement per the class file.

frost-rune and danger-sense are both PARTIAL boosters, but they cover Constitution and Dexterity respectively - two of Wisdom/Constitution/Dexterity - so the schema's two-partials rule makes them one blanket and the save row reads 5 from Act I.
Hill Rune's physical resistance and Rage's do not stack; the durability ratio takes one x2 layer at roughly 1.8 blended, reliable every fight only from Rune Knight 7.
Cloud Rune redirects an attack to a RANDOM other creature within 9m, which in a two-body party can be the partner. It is not scored as rescue.
Rune inscription persistence across rests is flagged partly unverified in the class file.

Courtier.note: Sword-and-shield Fighter 11 whose subclass buys a saving throw the rest of the roster cannot: Elegant Courtier at Samurai 7 grants a third save proficiency outright, and one Resilient feat on top of it puts this body at all six. Fighting Spirit supplies advantage for a turn a fight and temporary hit points.
Courtier.strength: A failed save removes half of a two-body party's action economy, and this is the only chassis in the batch that can be proficient in every save at once - Elegant Courtier plus one feat does what no amount of AC or hit points does against Listo's climbing boss DCs.
Courtier.wants: A body that carries single-target damage, since this chassis spends its subclass on saves and its Cleric block on rescue.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.
Fighting Spirit is three uses per LONG rest, so its advantage covers one turn in four; the x1.35 is applied at a quarter weight rather than across the routine.

Elegant Courtier's third save proficiency is taken as Charisma (Wisdom already being covered by Lone Wolf), and one Resilient feat supplies Intelligence from Act II, which is what carries the save row to all six.
Rapid Strike (15) and Strength Before Death (18) are past Fighter 11 and are not scored.
Same Cleric 6 block as the Brute build on this split, so the Act III Spirit Guardians arithmetic is deliberately identical; the two bodies differ on saves and durability, not on area damage.

Steady Aim.note: The Sharpshooter SUBCLASS, which has no relationship to the Sharpshooter feat and does not use it. Steady Aim adds two plus half the Fighter level to every hit against one target for a turn, three times per short rest, and Close-Quarters Shooting lets the archer stand in the front line it is named for.
Steady Aim.strength: Steady Aim refills on a short rest and covers three rounds in four, and the Archery style's +2 to hit is one of the few accuracy bonuses par has no answer to - so this body gains against the reference on both the damage and the hit-chance side while spending nothing that a long rest has to replace.
Steady Aim.wants: Area damage and outward rescue: this chassis is 0 on AoE and 0 on control-area in every act, and its only outward tool is a Ranger 3 heal.
uncertain: Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter are +5/+9/+11 damage (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage) against a -3/-5/-6 attack-roll penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_AttackPenalty). Expected value against par AC is neutral in Act I and negative from Act II, so the toggle is scored OFF and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only. Heavy Armour Master is confirmed as DamageReduction(All,Flat,3/5/5), all damage, on heavy armour.

The subclass is named for the feat and does NOT take it: with the toggle off this body keeps the Archery style's +2 to hit, which raises h from 0.65 to 0.75 and is worth x1.154 on the raw. That bonus does not cancel against par, which carries no fighting style - it is the mirror of the Great Weapon Master penalty.
Steady Aim is three uses per SHORT rest lasting until end of turn, so it covers three rounds in four; its +2 + half Fighter level is +6/+8/+10 by act.
Rapid Strike (15) is counted as one bonus-action attack a round in Act III; Snap Shot is Fighter 18 and is not reached.
Thrown weapons do not count as ranged weapons for Steady Aim or Rapid Strike.

Riposte.split: Mesmerist 14 (Aspect of the Daredevil) / Rogue 3 (Swashbuckler) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)

riders.name: Sneak Attack 2d6 (Rogue 3, once per turn)
riders.single_axis_reason: Sneak Attack fires once per turn on one target and cannot be spread; the half-caster slots that feed aoe are scored there in full.

riders.name: Sneak Attack + superiority dice
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a single weapon hit on one target; the half-caster slots that feed aoe are scored there in full.

riders.name: Sneak Attack + superiority dice + Phasic Challenge
riders.single_axis_reason: All three ride a weapon hit on one target, and Phasic Challenge is literally a duel that excludes everyone else.

Riposte.note: Mesmerist 1 opens so the class hands over Dexterity and Charisma saves and Lone Wolf's +4 can go on Constitution and Wisdom — mesmerist.md's own recommendation — which costs most of the feat budget bringing Charisma and Dexterity up by hand. Rogue 3 is Swashbuckler for Sneak Attack without a flanker; Fighter 3 is Battle Master because its dice are the only Fighter resource on a short-rest clock.
Riposte.strength: The Superior Defense boon adds Charisma to AC on top of Dexterity while unarmoured, so one stat buys the spell DC, the Feint DC and the armour class at once — and at AC 22-24 enemies miss constantly, which is the trigger for Parry and Riposte's free Feint. Lone Wolf's two reactions plus the third at Mesmerist 9 turn that into three extra damage instances a round, which is where the gear constant actually pays.
Riposte.wants: An area answer and a concentration holder — this body is area-control rung 1-2 and never casts above a 4th-level slot.
uncertain: The Act II/III instance count of 7.5 rests on three Riposte reactions a round (two from Lone Wolf, one from Daredevil's Deeds at Mesmerist 9) actually triggering — Parry and Riposte auto-Feints anyone who *misses* you, so it is self-reinforcing with the high AC but it is not guaranteed every round.

Superior Defense is authored as AC 20 / 22 / 24 unarmoured (10 + Dex + Cha + 1 + 1 per 5 Mesmerist levels). That single boon is what carries dur from 3 to 5; picking a different Daredevil Boon drops it to about rung 2.

Panache is long-rest outside crits and kills with a one-handed piercing weapon, and Extra Attack is gated on holding 3 of it. Act I is scored at exactly 3 Panache (Mesmerist 5), so dedicating any to Improved or Greater Feints would remove Extra Attack outright.
rogue.md says a Rogue taken as a later class grants one skill and no Expertise; the record claims no Expertise at all, which is the main reason skl sits at 2 rather than 3.
Swashbuckler has no features from 13 to 20 and Sneak Attack is frozen at 2d6 from a 3-level dip — that decay is inside the ratio and no extra rule is applied on top.
Riposte.address: mesmerist/Aspect of the Daredevil — the melee/skirmisher archetype:reaction

Evilseye.split: Mesmerist 14 (Aspect of the Eyebiter) / Sorcerer 6 (Favored Soul)

riders.name: Painful Stare + Manifold Stare (2d8 twice per turn)
riders.single_axis_reason: Painful Stare only fires on the one creature the Hypnotic Stare is fixed to, so it cannot be spread across a group.

riders.name: Painful Stare + Manifold Stare (2d8 twice per turn)
riders.single_axis_reason: Painful Stare only fires on the single creature under the Hypnotic Stare.

riders.name: Painful Stare + Manifold Stare (2d10 three times per turn)
riders.single_axis_reason: Painful Stare only fires on the single creature under the Hypnotic Stare.

Evilseye.note: Mesmerist 1 opens for Dexterity and Charisma saves so Lone Wolf's +4 lands on Constitution and Wisdom, then Mesmerist to 5, Favored Soul to 6 with the Life domain, then Mesmerist to 14. Both classes run on Charisma, so nothing is split — the cost is spell tier, since neither half knows a spell above 3rd.
Evilseye.strength: Hypnotic Stare is a permanent, resourceless, concentration-free penalty to one enemy's saves, and the Eyebiter hangs Disorientation and Sapped Magic on it so the same penalty also hits that enemy's attack rolls, damage and spell save DC — a boss lockdown that never competes with the pair's two concentration slots. The Resistance boon turns the same Stare into resistance to *all* damage from Mesmerist 10, which is a proportional layer on a body that never takes off its Stare.
Evilseye.wants: A crowd answer — the Stare is one target at a time and this body's area control falls to rung 1 by Act III.
uncertain: Manifold Stare's interaction with the level-12 and level-18 Painful Stare die increases is ambiguous in mesmerist.md ('with the normal die increases at 12 and 18 still applying'). Act III is scored at 2d10 three times per turn with no level-12 increase applied, which is the conservative reading; the generous one adds about 16 raw and would still leave st at rung 2.
