ctrl_s falls 5 to 4 because the act table raises the bar, not because the chassis got worse: Act I's rung 5 is Hold Person plus a repeatable rider, which this body has at character 8, while Acts II and III want slot-free *hard* control on a short-rest clock, which the Eyebiter never gets.

The Favored Soul domain is authored as Life (Cure Wounds at 1, Lesser Restoration at 3, Revivify and Beacon of Hope at 5). Peace would swap Revivify for Warding Bond, but this body is d8/d6 in medium armour and a poor bond carrier.
Eyebiter's L13 permanent See Invisibility and L17 True Seeing (auto-pass Perception) are out of reach at Mesmerist 14 and are scored as absent — they would move skl by a full rung.
Sorcery points are 6 and long-rest, so a Quickened or Twinned cast is about one per fight; nothing is claimed for Metamagic beyond that.
Evilseye.address: mesmerist/Aspect of the Eyebiter — the debuff/damage archetype:lockdown

Bondkeeper.split: Mesmerist 12 (Aspect of the Trickster) / Paladin 3 / Warlock 5

riders.name: Divine Smite off half-caster slots
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides a melee weapon hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as area casts and Eldritch Blast beams instead.

riders.name: Divine Smite off half-caster slots
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides a melee weapon hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as area casts and Eldritch Blast beams instead.

Bondkeeper.note: Mesmerist 1 through 8 first, so both Trickster Boons and the Tier-2 tricks are online before anything else, then Paladin 3 for medium armour, shields and Divine Smite, then Warlock 5 for Eldritch Blast and short-rest pact slots. Every one of the three classes runs on Charisma. It gives up its own turn almost entirely in Act I — single-target and area both score 0 there.
Bondkeeper.strength: Hypnotic Bonds are `3 + Mesmerist level` and refresh on a *short* rest, so this body has eleven to fifteen free-action interventions per rest in a run where a long rest costs 120+ supplies. Mesmeric Mirror makes an incoming attack on the partner automatically miss, Compel Alacrity hands the partner Haste as a free action, and Healing Bond puts temp HP on them every time any of it fires — all of which matter far more when the party is two bodies than when it is four.
Bondkeeper.wants: Someone to point all of this at: it is a pure force multiplier, so it wants the highest-damage body in the field, not another support.
uncertain: Both Trickster Boons are spent on Fortifying Tricks (dur) and Healing Bond (rsc); the record claims both because L4 and L8 are two separate picks. Mocking Machinations or Spirited Trick instead would move dur or rsc down a rung.

act 4 in every act is claimed on Compel Alacrity handing the partner Haste as a free action off a short-rest pool — the rubric's rung-5 clause is 'an Action handed to the other body', but this chassis never has the Extra Attack the Act I rung-5 row also asks for.

rsc 4 in Act III is the act table's own rung-4 row read literally ('prevention that survives the act's damage, plus a no-action outward source, on a short-rest clock'). Rung 5 there wants 9th-tier restoration or Mass Heal, and a half-caster capped at 4th-level slots cannot reach either.

Charisma has to be raised entirely by point buy and half-feats because Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Constitution and Wisdom; that is what buys the four-disjoint save set and it consumes most of the six feats.

`towering-ego` switches off while the body is under a mind-affecting condition (mesmerist.md), so it prevents rather than cures; the id is authored as the registry defines it and no discount is applied.
Bondkeeper.address: mesmerist/Aspect of the Trickster — the support/buff archetype:short-rest

Tempestborn.note: Monk to 14 for Diamond Soul, then Stormcalling. Elemental Strikes are set to replace the default unarmed attack so the opportunity attack carries the extended range, the element and the push/pull rider. Build-time picks: attuned to thunder so the Way and the College share a damage type; two Elemental Bursts a fight in Act I and three from Act II, which is what buys the aoe rung and costs the single-target one; and the Bard pool spent on control rather than damage.
Tempestborn.strength: Push and pull land on the enemy's turn through an opportunity attack, and Lone Wolf hands this body two Reactions to do it with — control bought entirely outside its own action budget, which is the scarcest thing a two-character party owns. Elemental Burst then lets it pick the damage type of its area answer at cast time, which is the cleanest reply to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances in the class.
Tempestborn.wants: A partner that carries single-target burst: this body trades its Actions for area coverage and falls to par on st by Act III. It reaches a real ctrl_a rung only once Chorus of Thunder lands in Act III.
uncertain: SETTLED FROM THE PAK. `Projectile_MPHB2024_ElementalBurst_Container` in WarriorOfTheElementsPHB2024...pak reads UseCosts "ActionPoint:1;KiPoint:2", TargetRadius 18, AreaRadius 4, SpellRoll "not SavingThrow(Ability.Dexterity, SourceSpellDC(10, context.Source, Ability.Wisdom))", and deals three Martial Arts dice on a failed save, half on a success, in a player-chosen element. monk.md marked this `(unverified)`; it is a real area engine and is now scored. It is weaker than Ascendant Dragon's Breath because it consumes the whole Action rather than replacing one attack of it.

Elemental Burst's dice are the Martial Arts die, which stops at 1d10 for a Monk 14, so the burst does not scale between Acts II and III while par does. That decay is the whole of why st falls to rung 2 and aoe holds at 2 in Act III.
Stride of the Elements (11) is `StrideOfTheElements_Passive`, a marker passive with no Boosts or StatsFunctors and a Fly icon — movement utility only. It is scored on no axis.
Elemental Epitome (17) is not reached by this Monk 14 build; the lockdown chassis therefore gets none of Destructive Strides, Elemental Resistance or Empowered Strikes.

Opportunity attacks are credited at 0.5 a round. Lone Wolf grants two Reactions and this body's whole plan is to be walked past, but an OA only happens if an enemy moves, so a full 1.0 a round is not defensible.
Chorus of Thunder is what lifts ctrl_a to 3 in Act III: one Bardic Inspiration, a short-rest resource from Bard 5, no concentration, and Concussion denies reactions and caps the target at one action.

Markwarden.note: Monk all the way to 17 for the 1d12 Martial Arts die and Elemental Epitome, then Cavalier 3 for Unwavering Mark and Action Surge. It gives up any spell list whatsoever to buy the deepest ki pool in the roster — 18 points refilled twice a cycle — and a reaction routine. Build-time picks: two Elemental Bursts a fight in every act, both bonus actions on Flurry rather than on Step of the Wind, and Empowered Strikes as the level-17 interrupt.
Markwarden.strength: Two Reactions, an opportunity attack that carries the Way's push/pull rider, and Unwavering Mark forcing a marked enemy to swing at this body instead of the other one — in a party of two, redirecting attention onto the tougher half is the only substitute for a tank the game does not otherwise let you have.
Markwarden.wants: Everything off the spell list: area damage, area control, and outward rescue. It is 0 on aoe in every act and cannot pick its partner up at all.
uncertain: SETTLED FROM THE PAK. `Projectile_MPHB2024_ElementalBurst_Container` in WarriorOfTheElementsPHB2024...pak reads UseCosts "ActionPoint:1;KiPoint:2", TargetRadius 18, AreaRadius 4, SpellRoll "not SavingThrow(Ability.Dexterity, SourceSpellDC(10, context.Source, Ability.Wisdom))", and deals three Martial Arts dice on a failed save, half on a success, in a player-chosen element. monk.md marked this `(unverified)`; it is a real area engine and is now scored. It is weaker than Ascendant Dragon's Breath because it consumes the whole Action rather than replacing one attack of it.

Elemental Epitome (17) resolves into three pak passives and all three are now scored. `ElementalEpitome_Passive2` applies ELEMENTAL_RESISTANCE_MONK_*, which is a literal Boosts "Resistance(Fire, Resistant)" on the attuned element — that confirms the proportional layer behind dur 4 in Act III rather than leaving it a guess. `ElementalEpitome_Passive3` unlocks Interrupt_EmpoweredStrike_*, DealDamage(LevelMapValue(MartialArts)) on a non-critical Elemental Strike hit, off ActionResource(Interrupt_EmpoweredStrike,1,0); it is scored as a one-per-turn single-target rider.

`ElementalEpitome_Passive` unlocks Destructive Strides — an aura applying one Martial Arts die to every enemy in it once per turn, gated on Step of the Wind. It is a genuine Spirit-Guardians-shaped area engine and it is NOT scored here, because Step of the Wind costs the bonus action this build spends on its second Flurry. Taking it instead reads aoe 2 and st 2 in Act III rather than aoe 1 and st 3 — a real alternative build, and rule 3 forces one configuration.
Stride of the Elements (11) is `StrideOfTheElements_Passive`, a marker passive with no Boosts or StatsFunctors and a Fly icon — movement utility only. It is scored on no axis.

Unwavering Mark's uses scale with the Strength modifier and Strength is this body's dump stat, so it is roughly one use per long rest. It is scored as rung-1 redirection on rsc and claims nothing on ctrl_s.
Opportunity attacks are credited at 0.5 a round, as on the lockdown variant.
Action Surge is deliberately absent from the damage block (axis-rubrics.md rule 2) and scored on `act`, which holds this body at 3 in Act III where a monk with no third Action falls to 2.

Mercygiven.note: Monk to 11 first, then Bard 6 and a Warlock 3 tail, so Flurry of Healing and Harm is online at character 11 and everything after it is slots. Build-time pick: the ki goes to Flurry and Hands of Harm, not to Quickened Healing, and the Bard pool is spent on control and outward healing rather than damage.
Mercygiven.strength: From Monk 11 every Flurry strike can be a free Hands of Healing aimed at the partner, and Lone Wolf's second bonus action buys two Flurries a round — so this body heals the other half of the party without ever spending an Action, off a pool that refills on a short rest while a long rest costs 120+ supplies.
Mercygiven.wants: A partner that owns the pair's concentration slot and answers crowds: this body is 0 on aoe in all three acts and never clears 1 on ctrl_a.
uncertain: rsc falls from 4 to 3 between Acts II and III. The Act II rung-4 row names Flurry of Healing and Harm explicitly; the Act III rung-4 row additionally demands prevention that survives the act's damage, and this body stops at Bard 6 so it never reaches Death Ward. Scored to the rung-3 ladder line (repeatable outward healing on a short-rest clock plus Physician's Touch condition removal) rather than claiming the higher row.
Implements of Mercy grants two proficiencies from a skill list the pak does not enumerate in the class file; Insight and Medicine are assumed.

Nightstep.note: The scout monk: Monk to 11, then Bard 6 for Expertise and slots, then Warlock 3. Shadow Arts buys Hide, Pass Without Trace and Darkness off the ki pool, and Dungeon Delver buys the Perception expertise the Monk skill list cannot. It gives up any damage rider at all — the Way adds nothing to a strike.
Nightstep.strength: A two-character party has no dedicated scout and no spare action to spend looking for traps; this body covers stealth, repositioning and party-wide Pass Without Trace off the same short-rest pool that funds its Flurries, and its Perception expertise is the only thing in the pair standing between the run and Listo's 15–25 trap band.
Nightstep.wants: Damage that is not bludgeoning and an answer to crowds — it deals one damage type against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances, and sits at 0 on aoe and 1 on ctrl_a.
uncertain: Shadow Arts' Darkness holds concentration, so the chassis-level `concentration` flag is false only because the plan does not ride it; a player who does maintain Darkness gives up the pair's slot and should be read a rung lower on saves.

Dungeon Delver is read as granting proficiency as well as expertise in Perception and Sleight of Hand. If it only doubles an existing proficiency, this body has neither on the Monk list and every Perception figure above drops by two proficiency bonuses.

Wyrmfist.note: Monk 5 then Barbarian 3 by character 8, back to Monk 11 by 14, Bard 6 last. Rage is taken for its physical resistance rather than its damage bonus, which is Strength-keyed and inert on a Dexterity monk. Build-time picks: Draconic Strike attuned to fire, Aspect of the Wyrm used as the resistance aura rather than Frightful Presence when the partner is exposed.
Wyrmfist.strength: It is the only Monk in the list that hands the *other* character a defensive buff — Aspect of the Wyrm's resistance covers allies in the aura, which in a party of two means the whole party — and Breath of the Dragon gives a class with no area answer a real one without spending a bonus action, which is where Lone Wolf's second Flurry already lives.
Wyrmfist.wants: A body that holds the pair's concentration slot and brings hard area control; this one's ctrl_a is a movement-blocking fear aura at best and its Act I aoe is a single rung.
uncertain: Rage's resistance is applied as a partial proportional layer (physical share of incoming damage taken at 0.70), giving a mitigation multiplier of about 1.54 rather than the flat 2.0 the rubric's anchor table uses for a blanket resistance. A full 2.0 would put dur at 5 in every act.

SETTLED FROM THE PAK, not an assumption: `5e Reckless Attack` (10924) restores the RAW Strength gate. `5E_RECKLESS_ATTACK` in RecklessAttack5e_Combined.txt reads Boosts "IF(AttackRollAbility(Ability.Strength) and (IsMeleeWeaponAttack() or IsMeleeUnarmedAttack())):Advantage(AttackRoll)". This body rolls its attacks off Dexterity, so it gets no advantage and no x1.35 multiplier. The clause does cover unarmed strikes, so a Strength-based unarmed body would get it.
Rage's +2/+3/+4 damage bonus is scored as inert for the same Strength-keyed reason.

Astralguard.note: The single-stat Monk: the astral arms roll attack and damage off Wisdom, so Dexterity and Strength stay at point-buy and the spare points go to Constitution. Monk to 11 for Body of the Astral Self, then Bard 6 and Warlock 3. It gives up Unarmoured Defence's second half — AC 18 rather than 20 — to buy hit points and a reaction that eats elemental damage.
Astralguard.strength: Lone Wolf grants a second Reaction and this is the class's only body that has something to do with it: Deflect Energy twice a round reduces acid, cold, fire, force, lightning and thunder by 1d10 + Wisdom each, against an enemy roster whose damage Absolute Wrath has made mostly elemental. The arms also deal force, the least-resisted type in the list.
Astralguard.wants: Area damage and area control — this body is 0 on aoe in every act — and a partner willing to be the one enemies pick on, because its AC is the lowest of any Monk here.
uncertain: Deflect Energy is priced as a flat mitigation multiplier of about 1.3, on the assumption that roughly 40% of incoming damage is one of the six types it covers. That assumption is what moves dur from 3 to 4 in Acts II and III.
Lone Wolf's +4 is placed on Wisdom and Constitution rather than Wisdom and Dexterity, which is what leaves AC at 18/18/19; the saves set follows from that pick.

Palewatch.note: Rogue is the level-1 class, which is the whole point: four skill proficiencies and Expertise on two of them at character 1, where a Rogue taken as a dip would grant one skill and no Expertise. Monk 11 follows for the astral arms and Body of the Astral Self, then Bard 6 for two more Expertises. Build-time picks: Rogue 3 into Thief, and Lone Wolf's +4 on Wisdom and Constitution rather than Dexterity.
Palewatch.strength: It is the only body here that clears Listo's untelegraphed half — Perception against a 15–25 trap band and Investigation against secret doors — at better than even odds, and in a two-character party those checks have no third body to fall back on. The arms also make Wisdom do attack, damage, AC and save DC at once, so the skill investment costs it nothing in stats.
Palewatch.wants: Area damage and area control; it is 0 on aoe in all three acts. It also wants a partner who can hold a concentration spell, since this body never casts one.
uncertain: Act I is Rogue 3 / Monk 5, so the ki pool is 6 and one point of it goes to the Arms; that is why Act I delivers 6.5 instances a round rather than 8, and why st reads 3 rather than 4 as on the other Monks in this batch.
Sneak Attack is not credited anywhere: the astral arms are unarmed strikes and not a finesse weapon, so this body has no legal Sneak Attack vehicle while the arms are up.
Deflect Energy is priced as a flat mitigation multiplier of about 1.3 on the assumption that ~40% of incoming damage is one of the six types it covers; that is what moves dur to 4 from Act II.

Bellwarden.note: Monk to 14 for Diamond Soul, then Stormcalling. Build-time picks, all forced by rule 3: Friar's Blessing as the Bond variant (+1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws on both bodies) rather than Faith, Valor or Retribution; a shield kept up under Guardian of Light; and Lone Wolf's +4 on Wisdom and Constitution, which costs it Dexterity and therefore a rung of single-target damage.
Bellwarden.strength: Friar's Bond covers the entire party from level 3 because the party is two — Shared Resolve and Community are dead weight here, and what is left is per-turn temporary hit points on both bodies, a free teleport to the partner, and a +1d4 on every save either of them rolls, all from one bonus action and one ki.
Bellwarden.wants: A partner that does not need the concentration slot, because this body holds it for the whole run, and one that brings the single-target damage this build traded away for Wisdom.
uncertain: Guardian of Light's advantage on Concentration checks is recorded under the `war-caster` id, which ledger-schema.md states is keyed to the effect rather than the feat and names this feature explicitly.
The eighth Flurry is displaced by the Bond's own bonus action on the first round; instances are still counted at eight a round because the Bond lasts the fight and only costs the one action.

Pacifying Sweep is scored on ctrl_a rather than aoe: its damage is a single weapon roll per target and the Pacified condition ends the moment either body damages the target, which is why it holds rung 3 rather than 4.

Keenedge.split: Monk 11 (Way of the Kensei) / Bloodhunter 3 / Bard 6

riders.name: Deft Strike
riders.single_axis_reason: Kensei's Deft Strike adds a Martial Arts die to one melee weapon hit per turn; it rides a single roll and cannot be aimed at a group.

riders.name: Crimson Rite (1d4)
riders.single_axis_reason: The Rite adds its Hemocraft die to each weapon hit; it has no area delivery on this body.

riders.name: Deft Strike
riders.single_axis_reason: One melee weapon hit per turn; single roll only.

riders.name: Crimson Rite (1d4)
riders.single_axis_reason: Rides each weapon hit; no area delivery.

riders.name: Deft Strike
riders.single_axis_reason: One melee weapon hit per turn; single roll only.

Keenedge.note: A Kensei who fights with a longsword in the Attack action and unarmed strikes off both bonus actions, with Blood Hunter 3 for a Crimson Rite rider and Bard 6 bolted on last for slots. Build-time picks: kensei weapon over pure unarmed, Rite of the Flame, and the Bard pool spent entirely on control and healing rather than damage.
Keenedge.strength: Agile Parry puts +2 AC up on every turn for free, which is the cheapest durability in a party that has no spare body to absorb a focus; and eight separate damage rolls a round means the act's gear kit is collected eight times against par's four, so a duo's single weapon kit is worth twice as much strapped to this body as to a two-attack partner.
Keenedge.wants: A body that supplies area damage and area control — this one is 0 on aoe in every act and never rises above 1 on ctrl_a, so a crowd is entirely the partner's problem.
uncertain: Sharpen the Blade (+3 attack and damage for up to 3 ki) is scored as inert: the act's gear constant k already assumes an enchanted weapon, and the feature explicitly does nothing to a weapon that already carries an enchantment bonus.
`dark-augmentation` is listed in the schema registry as Blood Hunter 2, but bloodhunter.md puts Dark Augmentation at class level 10. This body stops at Blood Hunter 3, so no booster was authored.
The Bard 6 pool is declared to_damage 0.0 — every slot goes to control and outward healing. A player who spent half of it on Shatter would trade roughly one st rung for one aoe rung.

Deathward.split: Monk 11 (Way of the Long Death) / Cleric 6 / Paladin 3

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee weapon hit; it adds no roll of its own and has no area form.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Rides one melee weapon hit; no area form.

Deathward.note: Monk 11 for Mastery of Death, then Twilight Cleric 6 and a Paladin 3 tail for Divine Smite. It swings a shortsword in the Attack action so the Smites have a legal weapon and punches with the bonus actions. Build-time picks: Twilight domain over a heavy-armour one (armour would switch off Unarmoured Defence), Oath of Devotion, and the pair's concentration slot committed to Spirit Guardians from Act III.
Deathward.strength: Mastery of Death converts a drop to 0 HP into one ki, repeatably, off a pool that a short rest refills — in a duo, losing either body usually ends the fight, so this is the only line in the roster that removes that failure mode rather than delaying it. Twilight Sanctuary then taps temporary hit points into both characters every round for a Channel Divinity charge the same short rest refunds.
Deathward.wants: A partner who does not need the concentration slot and who can carry the skills load: this body reads 0 on skl by Act III and cannot roll Perception or Persuasion at all.
uncertain: Mastery of Death is priced as a 1.5x multiplier on the effective pool — roughly one extra life a fight off a 12-ki pool — which is what carries dur from 4 to 5. It could reasonably be priced higher; it is repeatable until the ki runs out.
Touch of Death's temporary hit points are credited at two kills a fight. Fewer kills, or a fight against a single boss, removes about a third of the pool bonus.
Divine Smite requires a melee weapon attack, so it rides only the four Attack-action shortsword hits and never a Flurry strike; the Flurry strikes stay unarmed.
Act III commits the pair's one concentration slot to Spirit Guardians, which is why aoe rises to 2 and why §5/§6 do not also claim that slot.

Palmstrike.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Open Hand) / Rogue 3 (Thief)

riders.name: Sneak Attack (2d6)
riders.single_axis_reason: Sneak Attack rides one existing weapon roll per turn and is available once on the turn; it has no area form and adds no instance.

Palmstrike.note: Monk to 17 for Quivering Palm and the 1d12 Martial Arts die, then Thief 3 for Fast Hands. It fights with a shortsword in the Attack action so Sneak Attack has a legal weapon, and unarmed off the bonus actions. What it gives up is any spell list at all: no rescue, no area damage, no area control beyond splitting Flurry strikes across two targets.
Palmstrike.strength: Fast Hands stacks on top of Lone Wolf's two bonus actions for a third Flurry every round, and Open Hand's Topple and Push ride every one of those strikes at the Ki Save DC for no resource — control that costs no action at all is what a two-body party cannot buy any other way.
Palmstrike.wants: Everything it does not do: area damage, area control, and any way at all to pick the partner up. rsc is 0 in all three acts and aoe is 0 in all three.
uncertain: Fast Hands' third bonus action is deliberately excluded from the damage block: axis-rubrics.md rule 2 restricts §1 and §2 to the Lone Wolf floor of two Actions and two Bonus Actions, and the surplus is scored on `act` instead. Counting it would put st at rung 4 in Act III.

Sneak Attack is credited only because the Attack action uses a shortsword; monk unarmed strikes are not a finesse weapon. If the pak allows Sneak Attack off unarmed strikes the rider applies to a larger set of rolls but the rung does not move.

ctrl_s is held at 5 across all three acts on the concentration argument: Topple and Push land on every Flurry strike at the Ki Save DC for no resource, and Stunning Strike is slot-free hard control on a short-rest clock. Save-DC control does not decay.

Ironpalm.split: Monk 11 (Way of the Open Hand (vanilla)) / Cleric 6 / Artificer 3
Ironpalm.note: Monk 11 for the Open Hand technique riders, Tempest Cleric 6 for Destructive Wrath and Thunderbolt Strike, Artificer 3 for an Eldritch Cannon. From Act II it spends one of its eight action-slots a fight on a maximised Shatter, which is what buys the aoe rung and costs it a rung of single-target by Act III. Build-time picks: Tempest domain, Artillerist, and no armour so Unarmoured Defence stays live.
Ironpalm.strength: Topple and Push ride every one of the eight Flurry strikes Lone Wolf's two bonus actions buy, at the Ki Save DC, for no resource at all — and Thunderbolt Strike turns a maximised Shatter into mass knockback. Control that costs neither concentration nor an action is the only kind a two-body party can afford to layer.
Ironpalm.wants: Outward rescue and skills. rsc is 0 in Act I and this body cannot roll Perception or Persuasion at all, reaching skl 0 by Act III.
uncertain: Destructive Wrath maximises the Shatter it is spent on, which is the only reason a 2nd/3rd-tier area spell reaches a rung at all here; Goon's fix moves the trigger to when damage is dealt, so a charge is never wasted.

The Eldritch Cannon is scored as one extra body on `act` and contributes no damage: axis-rubrics.md rule 2 excludes summons and extra bodies from the damage axes, and the Cannon's flat dice are close to irrelevant by Act II anyway.

st falls to a bare 1.13x par in Act III because one of the eight action-slots goes to the Shatter. Holding all eight on attacks would read rung 3 and drop aoe to 0; the lockdown niche is why the cast was kept.

Sunbolt.split: Monk 14 (Way of the Sun Soul) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)

riders.name: Searing Arc Strike (Burning Hands, upcast to 3rd)
riders.single_axis_reason: Burning Hands is a fixed 15-ft cone; it has no single-target mode, and the ki that funds it is the same ki the bonus bolts want, which is why both raws are stated against the same pool.

riders.name: Searing Arc Strike (Burning Hands, upcast to 7th)
riders.single_axis_reason: Cone only, no single-target mode; competes with the bonus bolts for the same ki.

riders.name: Searing Arc Strike (Burning Hands, upcast to 7th)
riders.single_axis_reason: Cone only, no single-target mode; competes with the bonus bolts for the same ki.

Sunbolt.note: The one Monk in the list that fights entirely at range: Radiant Sun Bolt replaces the Attack action's strikes with 30-ft ranged spell attacks rolling off Dexterity, and one ki buys two more as a bonus action. Monk 14 for Diamond Soul, then Stormcalling. Build-time pick: the ki goes to bolts or to Searing Arc Strike, never both in the same round, and the body stays at range — which is what costs it Stunning Strike.
Sunbolt.strength: Radiant is the least-resisted type in the list after Force, so this body keeps its damage against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances where a physical Monk does not; and a character who contributes at full output without ever closing is worth more in a party of two, where every step taken is half the party's positioning.
Sunbolt.wants: Single-target control and a front line. Standing at range means Stunning Strike never fires, so ctrl_s is 1 in every act, and the partner absorbs everything that closes.
uncertain: ctrl_s is 1 rather than 4 because Stunning Strike needs a melee hit and this configuration never makes one. Rule 3 forces one configuration at build time; a player who closes to melee trades the ranged reach discount for a rung of ctrl_s.

The Searing Arc Strike aoe carries rule 4's resistance multiplier from Act II (fire, 0.75 effective across the encounter mix). Searing Sunburst is radiant and dodges that, but it costs an Action rather than a bonus action and its dice stop scaling at 3 ki, so it was the weaker of the two from Monk 14 onward and is not the routine scored.

`meta` leads with Dexterity rather than Wisdom: monk.md records Sun Soul as the one Way that scales on Dexterity and does not benefit from the Ki Save DC change, so Dexterity is genuinely the primary here. That changes what this body contends with a partner over.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee weapon hit and cannot be spread; the aoe row is the greatsword's cleave, which is all this body has.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee weapon hit on one target.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee weapon hit on one target; the Act III aoe row is Cloudkill off the 17th-level oath spell plus cleave.

Ironcrown.note: Single-class Paladin, greatsword and plate, Lone Wolf's +4 on Strength and Constitution so the level-1 Wisdom and Charisma saves stay disjoint from it. Charisma is bought with the first two feats. Nothing is dipped, so it never gets a bonus-action engine or a third Action — its whole turn is two Attack actions and whatever it smites with.
Ironcrown.strength: Conquering Presence is a mass Wisdom-save Frighten off a Channel Oath charge that a short rest refunds, so it lands once a fight without touching either concentration slot — and Aura of Conquest then charges every frightened body half the paladin's level in psychic each turn. Guided Strike is +10 applied *after* seeing the roll, which in a duo is a guarantee on the one attack that has to land.
Ironcrown.wants: Eyes and a voice: no Perception, no Investigation, skills rung 1 in every act. It also has no area damage worth the name until Cloudkill at 17.
uncertain: Divine Smite is capped at 5d8 here. The Oathbreaker section of paladin.md says Unholy Smite is upcastable to slot level 9 'so it works at level 20', which implies base Divine Smite may also scale past 4th-level slots in this install; if it does, Act III st rises toward rung 3.

ctrl_a 4 rests on Conquering Presence (Action, mass Wisdom save, Frightened 1 minute, Channel Oath, no concentration). Act I arguably reaches rung 5 on the ladder's 'slot-free repeatable area control on a short-rest clock' clause; I held it at 4 because one Channel Oath charge is one cast a fight, not a repeatable clock.
Aura of Conquest's speed-reduction half does nothing in BG3 per the mod author, so only the psychic damage is scored.
Act III uses seven attack slots rather than eight because Cloudkill needs an Action; Acts I and II have no levelled spell worth an Action and spend all eight attacking.

Dreadchoir.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Conquest) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as Shatter-tier area casts instead.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as area casts instead.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as area casts instead.

Dreadchoir.note: Paladin 1 opens for heavy armour and Wisdom/Charisma saves so Lone Wolf's +4 lands on Dexterity and Constitution — four disjoint saves covering all three of Wis, Con and Dex before the aura is even counted. Rapier and shield rather than a greatsword, and Charisma is bought with feats. Bard 6 arrives late, so Conductor and Staccato Lightning are an Act III addition only.
Dreadchoir.strength: It stacks two crowd answers that cost no concentration: Conquering Presence off a short-rest Channel Oath, and Chorus of Thunder's Concussion, which knocks prone and strips the target's reactions and all but one action. Aura of Protection then hands the partner the paladin's Charisma modifier on every save in a 9m aura — in a two-body party that is the whole party.
Dreadchoir.wants: A body that deals real single-target damage: this one buys control with the actions it would otherwise be killing with, and never passes rung 2 on the boss axis.
uncertain: Bard 6 lands at character 18-20 under this levelling order, so Conductor, Staccato Lightning and short-rest Font of Inspiration are all Act III only. Front-loading Bard instead would move ctrl_s and end up a rung in Act II and cost Aura of Protection its early arrival.
Divine Smite capped at 5d8 — same caveat as the single-class Conquest record.
Paladin 14 never reaches the 17th-level oath spells, so Dominate Person and Cloudkill are not scored here even though the oath lists them.

Lightbearer.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Devotion) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master) / Sorcerer 3 (Draconic Bloodline)

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee hit; Act I aoe is the greatsword's cleave and nothing else.

riders.name: Divine Smite + superiority dice
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as Shatter-tier casts instead.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite + superiority dice
riders.single_axis_reason: All three ride a melee hit; the same slots are scored on aoe as upcast area casts instead.

Lightbearer.note: Fighter 1 opens for Strength and Constitution saves, heavy armour, a fighting style and Second Wind, then Paladin to 6 for Aura of Protection by character 7, then Fighter 2-3 and Sorcerer 3. Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Strength and Charisma, which keeps both the attack stat and the aura's scaling stat at 20 from level 1 and costs no feats — the price is a three-entry proficiency set that only reaches rung 4 because the aura is blanket.
Lightbearer.strength: Action Surge, Battle Master dice and Channel Oath all refill on a short rest, and Commander's Strike spends a superiority die to hand the *other* character an immediate weapon attack — a genuine extra action in a party that only has two bodies to spend. Aura of Devotion's charm immunity at Paladin 7 covers the partner at 9m, which is the answer to this list's rebuilt enemy casters.
Lightbearer.wants: An area engine and a scout — it is aoe rung 0 in Act I and has one skill proficiency that matters.
uncertain: Sorcerer 3 is taken in Act II under this order, so Draconic Resilience's unarmoured AC 13 is dead weight in plate and Elemental Affinity (Sorcerer 6) is never reached. The three levels are bought for Metamagic and the slot table only; the Amethyst ancestry is chosen for a Force damage type nothing resists.
Improved Divine Smite lands at Paladin 11, which this order reaches in Act III — that is why st holds flat at rung 2 rather than rising in Act II.
Lone Wolf on Strength and Charisma leaves the proficiency set at three entries, so sav rests entirely on Aura of Protection being read as a blanket booster. Without the aura this body is rung 2.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee hit; the aoe row is Eldritch Blast beams split across targets plus cleave.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee hit; the aoe row is Eldritch Blast split across targets plus cleave.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit; the aoe row is Eldritch Blast split across targets plus cleave.

Vigilkeeper.note: Paladin 1-6 first for heavy armour, Wisdom/Charisma saves and Aura of Protection by character 6, then Warlock to 5. Longsword and shield rather than a greatsword, because Eldritch Blast carries the ranged half of the routine. Charisma is bought with feats since Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Strength and Constitution.
Vigilkeeper.strength: Almost every resource on the sheet refills on a short rest — two 3rd-level pact slots, Channel Oath, Divine Sense, Fey Presence — against a long rest that costs 120+ supplies, and Eldritch Blast underneath it all is at-will. Fey Presence is a slot-free area charm-or-fear from a level 1 dip, which is how two characters survive being outnumbered.
Vigilkeeper.wants: Single-target control above Command: this body's boss answer is damage, and its control axis falls to rung 1 by Act III.
uncertain: The routine deliberately shifts action-slots from the sword to Eldritch Blast as beams accumulate (2 of 8 in Act I, 4 of 8 in Act III). That is what carries st across the acts — the melee half alone would fall, because Divine Smite's pool grows far slower than enemy HP.

axis-rubrics.md warns that a Paladin's own slot table beats a Warlock dip for Endurance; end 4 here is claimed on the *breadth* of short-rest resources (pact slots, Channel Oath, Divine Sense, Fey Presence) plus at-will Eldritch Blast, not on slot count.
Archfey's Misty Escape and Beguiling Defences are Warlock 6 and 10 and are not reached.

Dawnbeam.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Illumination) / Bard 6 (College of Stormcalling)
Dawnbeam.note: Paladin 1 opens for heavy armour and Wisdom/Charisma saves, Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Dexterity and Constitution, and the body shoots rather than swings — which is what the oath is for. That choice costs it Divine Smite entirely, since a smite needs a melee weapon attack, so its damage is bow attacks and Bard spells with no rider pool underneath.
Dawnbeam.strength: A ranged radiant paladin is a shape nothing else in the roster has: it keeps Aura of Protection and Aura of Courage on the partner at 9m while standing outside the melee that Listo's inflated encounters generate, and radiant is the damage type Act II resists least.
Dawnbeam.wants: A melee body to hold the line it is shooting past — and one that can smite, because this one gave that up.
uncertain: Oath of Illumination is the least verifiable subclass in this batch. paladin.md recovers exactly one feature name for it — Aura of Brilliance — and states there is no published level-by-level breakdown; Listo added the pack 'for testing'. Every number here is the *base* Paladin chassis plus Bard 6, with nothing credited to the oath itself. If Aura of Brilliance is a real damage or defence aura the record is a rung light somewhere.

Divine Smite is scored at zero because the build shoots. That is the single biggest difference between this record and the other Paladin front-liners, and it is a build choice the oath's own pitch ('smite your foes from a distance') forces.
Listo's global 9m/15m aura patch predates this subclass by four versions, so paladin.md marks its coverage of Illumination unverified; the aura is scored at the patched radius anyway.

Vowbreaker.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of Vengeance) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master) / Warlock 3 (The Hexblade)

riders.name: Divine Smite + Hexblade's Curse, all under Vow of Enmity advantage (x1.35)
riders.single_axis_reason: Smite and the Curse both ride a melee hit on the single vowed target; the aoe row is one levelled area cast plus cleave.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Hexblade's Curse + superiority dice, under advantage (x1.35)
riders.single_axis_reason: All three ride a melee hit on the vowed target.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite + Curse + dice, under advantage (x1.35)
riders.single_axis_reason: All of them ride a melee hit on the vowed target.

Vowbreaker.note: Paladin 1 opens for heavy armour and Wisdom/Charisma saves so Lone Wolf's +4 can go on Constitution and Dexterity, giving four disjoint saves covering all three key abilities before the aura. Hex Warrior at Warlock 1 puts Charisma on the sword, so this is the one Paladin in the batch that is genuinely single-stat — longsword and shield, everything scaling off one number.
Vowbreaker.strength: Vow of Enmity is advantage for ten turns off a Channel Oath charge a short rest refunds, so the advantage is routine rather than an opener — worth a flat 1.35x on the whole attack-roll portion of the routine, which is one of the few multipliers in the model that does not cancel against par. Stacked with Hexblade's Curse and four superiority dice it is the highest single-target ratio in the Paladin set.
Vowbreaker.wants: A crowd answer. This body deletes one target extremely well and is area-damage rung 1 until Act III.
uncertain: The x1.35 advantage multiplier is applied to the whole attack-roll portion in every act. It qualifies as routine rather than situational because Vow of Enmity runs ten turns off a Channel Oath charge that a short rest refunds — one charge covers one four-round fight exactly. If Channel Oath is contested by Abjure Enemy in play, the multiplier should come off and st drops to about rung 2.

Monster Tactician is NOT a Paladin feature and is not scored here. axis-rubrics.md §8 names it immediately after Stern Gaze (Inquisitor), and the only occurrence in the data is inquisitor.md:231, where it is Vengeance INQUISITION's level-3 feature — the Inquisition, not the Oath. An earlier version of this record credited it and read skl 1/3/3; without it the body has two Paladin skill proficiencies and nothing else, so skl is 1 in every act.
Hold Monster is a 17th-level Vengeance oath spell and Paladin 14 never reaches it; ctrl_s 4 rests on Battle Master manoeuvres being no-concentration control rather than on the oath list.
Persuasion and Intimidation are scored at Charisma 20 by character 8 (both Act I feats spent on ability improvements) rather than the point-buy 17, which is what the damage block also assumes.

Greenward.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of the Ancients) / Bard 6 (College of Swords)

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee hit; Act I aoe is cleave alone, since Blade Flourish needs Bard 3.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite + Blade Flourish dice

Greenward.note: Paladin runs to 7 first so both auras are online by character 7, then Bard to 6 for Blade Flourish, Expertise and a short-rest Inspiration pool. Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Dexterity and Constitution, which keeps the level-1 Wisdom and Charisma saves disjoint from it and puts a scimitar in its hand instead of a greatsword.
Greenward.strength: Aura of Warding halves spell damage for both characters inside 9m, and in a party of two that is the whole party — against a list whose rebuilt enemy casters are the main source of unavoidable damage. Stacked on Aura of Protection from the level before, one body is carrying the other's saves and the other's spell mitigation at the same time.
Greenward.wants: Something that kills things: this body is single-target rung 2 flat and area rung 1, and it spends its Channel Oath on control rather than damage.
uncertain: Aura of Warding is scored as halving 40% of incoming damage (this list's enemy casters), giving a x1.25 mitigation term. That fraction is the least anchored number in the record — at 60% spell damage the ratio clears 2.4 and dur becomes 5 in every act.

rsc 4 rests on Aura of Warding being read as prevention aimed at the partner. It is not damage redirection and has no `redirect` id, and Durability is Personal, so there is no other axis that can see a pair-wide mitigation aura at all.
Undying Sentinel (Paladin 15) and Elder Champion (20) are outside a 14-level Paladin and are not scored.
Bard 6's Extra Attack is redundant with Paladin 5's and nothing is claimed for it.

Blackflame.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of the Bleak Walkers) / Fighter 3 (Champion) / Warlock 3 (The Hexblade)

riders.name: Divine Smite + Hexblade's Curse + Black Flames
riders.single_axis_reason: All three ride one melee hit on one target; Act I aoe is the weapon's cleave alone.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Curse + Black Flames + Champion crit range
riders.single_axis_reason: All of them ride a melee hit on one target.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite + Curse + Black Flames + crit range
riders.single_axis_reason: All of them ride a melee hit on one target.

Blackflame.note: Paladin 1 opens for heavy armour and Wisdom/Charisma saves so Lone Wolf's +4 lands on Constitution and Dexterity, and Hex Warrior at Warlock 1 puts Charisma on the sword — one stat drives the attack, the smite DC, the aura and the AC-adjacent boons. Champion is taken for crit range, not for its late features; Heroic Warrior is Fighter 10 and never arrives.
Blackflame.strength: Three crit-range effects stack on one body — Improved Critical, Hexblade's Curse and the level 7 aura's stacking minus-one — and the aura hands that last one to the partner as well, which compounds with a partner making many attacks off Lone Wolf's second Action. Death's Maw is flat damage reduction equal to the proficiency bonus that lasts until the next long rest, which is the cheapest standing mitigation in the class.
Blackflame.wants: A crowd answer and a face for the checks Intimidation does not cover — this body is area rung 0 to 1 throughout.
uncertain: Death's Maw's flat reduction only applies while standing within 2m of a corpse, so it is scored at 60% uptime. That single assumption is what makes dur 5 in Act I and 4 afterwards — the flat term decays from x1.94 to x1.37 across the acts exactly as axis-rubrics.md predicts for flat-only mitigation, and the uptime discount is mine, not the file's.

The stacked crit range (Improved Critical 19-20, plus the level 7 aura's minus-one, plus Hexblade's Curse) is folded into the raw as a small flat bonus (+2 in Act II, +5 in Act III). The model has no crit term, so this is an estimate rather than a derivation.
Black Flames is flat 2d10 until Paladin 15, which this split never reaches — that is why st front-loads at rung 3 and falls to 2.
The level 7 aura hands the partner a stacking crit-threshold reduction. No axis in the model can see a pair-wide offence buff, so it is recorded here and scored nowhere.

Crownguard.split: Paladin 17 (Oath of the Crown) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Divine Smite rides one melee hit; this body's aoe is cleave alone.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit on one target.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit on one target.

Crownguard.note: Paladin 1-6 first for heavy armour, Wisdom/Charisma saves and Aura of Protection by character 6, then Fighter for Action Surge and Battle Master, then Paladin to 17. Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Strength and Constitution, so the save set is four disjoint entries but covers only two of the three key abilities — the aura is what lifts it.
Crownguard.strength: Crown's Channel Oath is the only taunt in the roster, and a taunt is exactly what a Lone Wolf duo cannot otherwise buy: BG3 has no aggro, so enemy AI picks the softer body, and this forces it onto the one wearing plate and carrying the aura. Riposte then converts every forced attack that misses into a free reaction attack, and Lone Wolf hands this body two reactions a round to spend.
Crownguard.wants: An area damage engine — its own is cleave and nothing else, rung 0 to 1 in every act.
uncertain: The taunt itself is scored on ctrl_a and rsc, not on dur, and that is a modelling gap rather than a judgement: pulling attacks off the partner raises the pair's floor, but `redirect` in ledger-schema.md is a closed set of three Warding-Bond-family ids and a compelled-attack effect is not one of them. Scored as prevention aimed at the partner instead.

Riposte is priced at four reaction attacks a fight (the superiority pool), not at Lone Wolf's two reactions a round, because the dice bind first. The Champion Challenge synergy — forced attacks generate more misses to riposte off — is real but not double-counted.

Exalted Champion is Paladin 20 and this split stops at 17; Unyielding Saint at 15 is scored on saves only, and the renderer has no id for advantage on Strength and Constitution saves specifically, so it contributes nothing.
The Royal Decree cantrip Listo adds from mod.io has unverified mechanics per paladin.md and is scored as absent.

riders.name: Divine Smite / Lunar Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: A smite rides one melee hit; Act I aoe is cleave alone, before Spirit Guardians at Paladin 9.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit; the aoe row is Spirit Guardians, which is scored on damage and therefore not claimed on ctrl_a.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite + Fount of Moonlight
riders.single_axis_reason: All three ride a melee hit; the aoe row is upcast Spirit Guardians, scored on damage rather than ctrl_a.

Silverward.note: Paladin to 7 first so Aura of Protection and Aura of Moonlight are both up by character 7, then Twilight Cleric 3 for Twilight Sanctuary, then Paladin to 17. Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Dexterity and Constitution, leaving the level-1 Wisdom and Charisma saves disjoint — four proficiencies covering all three key abilities, plus a blanket aura on top.
Silverward.strength: Aura of Moonlight is flat damage reduction equal to Charisma modifier on every hit either character takes, and it stacks with resistance; Divine Guardian is a Channel Oath that halves all damage on the *other* body for ten turns; Twilight Sanctuary tops both up with temporary hit points every single round off a Channel Divinity charge a short rest refunds. Three separate mitigation layers, all pointed at a party of two, all on short-rest clocks.
Silverward.wants: Damage. This body is the most survivable thing in the roster and removes enemy action points at close to par — the partner has to be the one ending fights.
uncertain: Aura of Moonlight's flat reduction against the Act I crowd hit of 5.4 nearly nullifies it — the rubric's `(hit - reduction)/hit` formula returns a multiplier above 13. I clamped the crowd term at x3 before blending, because an unclamped value would put this body at four or five times par effective HP on the strength of one aura. The clamp is mine and is the single largest judgement in this record.

Spirit Guardians is claimed on aoe only. axis-rubrics.md's 'One pool, one axis' rule states explicitly that a damage effect holding concentration occupies one of the pair's two slots and may not also be claimed on §5/§6, so ctrl_a is scored on Full Moon alone.
Lunar Champion (Paladin 20) is out of reach at 17, so the `lunar-champion` booster is deliberately not authored despite this being the oath that grants it.

paladin.md marks Listo's global 9m/15m aura patch as unverified for this v10.0-era subclass; the aura is scored at the patched radius, which for a two-body party is the difference between covering the partner and not.

Moonpact.split: Paladin 14 (Oath of the Moon (Selûne-inspired)) / Fighter 1 / Warlock 5

riders.name: Divine Smite / Lunar Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: A smite rides one melee hit; Act I aoe is cleave alone, before any Warlock levels.

riders.name: Divine Smite
riders.single_axis_reason: A smite rides one melee hit; the aoe row is Eldritch Blast beams split across targets plus cleave.

riders.name: Divine Smite + Improved Divine Smite + Fount of Moonlight
riders.single_axis_reason: All three ride a melee hit; the aoe row is Eldritch Blast split across targets plus cleave.

Moonpact.note: Fighter 1 opens for Strength and Constitution saves, heavy armour, a fighting style and Second Wind, which lets Lone Wolf's +4 go on Charisma and Wisdom — Charisma 20 from level 1 is what makes Aura of Moonlight's flat reduction worth having early. Paladin to 7 for both auras, then Warlock 5. Strength is bought back with feats, so this is the feat-poorest body in the batch at six.
Moonpact.strength: Nearly the whole sheet reloads on a short rest: three Channel Oath options including Divine Guardian, two 3rd-level pact slots, Second Wind and Divine Sense, against long rests that cost 120+ supplies. Eldritch Blast at Charisma 22 sits underneath all of it as at-will damage that needs no clock at all, so the short-rest pool is spent on keeping the partner alive rather than on damage.
Moonpact.wants: Skills and a concentration holder — Investigation is untrained in every act and this body's own control is one Channel Oath charge a fight.
uncertain: Aura of Moonlight's crowd-hit term is clamped at x3 exactly as on the Paladin 17 Moon record; without the clamp the Act I ratio exceeds 4.7. Both Moon bodies stand or fall on that clamp.

The routine shifts action-slots from sword to Eldritch Blast as beams accumulate (none in Act I, four of eight in Act III), which is what makes st rise rather than hold — the melee half alone falls, because the smite pool grows far slower than enemy HP.

Constitution sits at 16 rather than 18 because Lone Wolf's +4 went on Charisma and Wisdom; that costs roughly a fifth of the hit-point pool against the other Moon record and is the main reason its Act III ratio is the tighter of the two.
axis-rubrics.md warns a Paladin 17's own slot table beats a Warlock dip for Endurance. end 4 here is claimed on the breadth of short-rest resources and at-will Eldritch Blast, not on slot count.

riders.name: Unholy Smite under Spiteful Suffering advantage (x1.35)
riders.single_axis_reason: A smite rides one melee hit; the aoe row is one Stormcalling area cast plus cleave.

riders.name: Unholy Smite + Aura of Hate, under advantage (x1.35)
riders.single_axis_reason: Both ride a melee hit on one target.

riders.name: Unholy Smite + Improved Unholy Smite + Aura of Hate, under advantage (x1.35)
riders.single_axis_reason: All of them ride a melee hit on one target.

Spitegrave.note: Paladin 1-6 for heavy armour, Wisdom/Charisma saves and Aura of Protection, then Bard to 6, then Paladin to 14. Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Strength and Constitution and Charisma is bought with feats. The oath's cost is real and permanent: Unholy Smite replaces Divine Smite outright, so every point of smite damage is Necrotic and none of it is Radiant.
Spitegrave.strength: Spiteful Suffering is advantage on attack rolls against the target for *everyone*, off a Channel Oath charge a short rest refunds — routine advantage is a flat 1.35x that does not cancel against par, and it is one of the few things in the model that a duo gets twice from one body spending one charge. Aura of Hate then adds the Charisma modifier to every melee hit on top.
Spitegrave.wants: A radiant or force damage type. This body's smite damage is entirely Necrotic, which is the wrong half of the Act II shadow-cursed and undead matchup, and Aura of Hate buffs nothing a normal partner is.
uncertain: This is the highest single-target ratio in the Paladin set and it rests on two multipliers landing together: Spiteful Suffering's advantage (x1.35, treated as routine because one Channel Oath charge covers one four-round fight) and Aura of Hate's flat +Charisma on every melee hit from Paladin 7. Remove either and it drops to about rung 3.

Rule 4's resisted-type multiplier is NOT applied, because the weapon's slashing and Stormcalling's lightning are both live second types. But the smite portion specifically is all Necrotic — paladin.md calls it 'a straight downgrade against the shadow-cursed and undead enemies of Act 2, and an upgrade against very little' — so the Act II figure is the most optimistic of the three.

Aura of Hate buffs 'you and nearby fiends and undead'. It does nothing for an ordinary partner and is scored as self-only; it would only become a pair effect against a Ghastly Ghouls undead partner, which is a race choice, not a chassis property.
Supernatural Resistance is Paladin 15 and Dread Lord is 20; neither is reachable at Paladin 14.

Standardbearer.note: A Lionheart opened at Paragon 1 for heavy armour and Constitution/Charisma saves, spending a Charisma-modifier bank of short-rest Banner Charges and one of its two attacks a round on the partner rather than on the enemy. Standardbearer.strength: Red Banner and Tag Team Maneuver each hand the partner an off-turn weapon attack and Yellow Banner hands them Charisma-modifier AC, none of which is diluted by ally count when the party is two; Unwavering Standard at Paragon 6 then puts the whole bank on the short-rest clock a 120-supply long rest makes precious.
Standardbearer.wants: A body that converts extra attacks into real damage, because this chassis spends its own tempo buying the partner's and is being outrun on single-target by Act III.

It is therefore toggled OFF here and this body's raw carries weapon plus ability modifier only.

Blade Skill save DCs are never stated on the mod page, which the class file flags: taken as 8 + proficiency + Charisma. Lionheart's banner-triggered Forceful Blade uses a fixed DC 12 + half level, so the two formulas may genuinely differ.

Banner Charges taken as Charisma modifier 3/4/5, every charge spent each fight; each costs one of this body's two attacks, which is what drives the single-target fall.
Vanguard's Charge (Paragon 9) is priced as blanket Disadvantage on attacks against this body from Act II, worth 0.65/0.36 on the durability ratio - the largest single term in its dur row.
Level order assumed Paragon 1-11, then Wizard 6, then Paladin 3, so Haste arrives only in Act III.

Shifting Court is scored as rescue 0 rather than as prevention: the rubric caps damage redirection at rung 1, and a position swap moves the danger from one half of the pair to the other.

The area reading assumes the Force and Thunder Focus attacks reach 1.6 targets on average. A looser pack drops AoE a full rung.

Lone Wolf's +4 must include Charisma on a single-stat Spellblade, which duplicates Paragon 1's own Charisma save and leaves three distinct proficient saves - the Charisma trap the class file names, and the reason Act I saves sit low.
Focusblade.address: paragon/Spellblade — the exception the skill suspected, but not a caster:front-line

Sixfold.note: Pure Paragon 20, the only split that reaches Paragon Of Legend and its +4 Charisma above the usual ceiling, taking the stat that rolls both attack and damage to 25. Everything it owns runs on six d10 Willpower Dice that return on a short rest; it has no spell slots, no spell list and never holds concentration.
Sixfold.strength: Nothing on this body is on a long-rest clock, which is the entire argument when a long rest costs 120+ supplies and short rests are free - and Will Over Weave at 13 is a Counterspell costing no slot, which a duo carrying no dedicated caster otherwise cannot buy at all.
Sixfold.wants: A body that answers crowds with control rather than damage, and one that can pick this one up: it is 0 on control-area and 0 on rescue in all three acts.

Feat count taken as 7 from Listo's 3/6/9/12/13/15/18 cadence; the Paragon class file says six, and whether the class's own 4/8/12/16/19 entries stack with the universal mod is flagged unverified there.

Charisma 25 in Act III comes from the level-20 capstone, which breaks the ceiling Lone Wolf and the ASI feat both stop at. Every Act III number here depends on that capstone, and any dip out of Paragon costs it.
Beloved By Mana's advantage on damage rolls priced at +10 percent; Beyond All Limits and the level-17 finisher are once per long rest and excluded from the per-round raw.
Sixfold.address: paragon/Spellblade — the exception the skill suspected, but not a caster:short-rest

Fallingrain.note: The throughput Paragon. Wisdom of Water turns every Willpower Die the body was already spending into a free-action extra melee attack, so the Blade Skill pool buys damage twice; Fighter 2 adds Action Surge and Second Wind on the same short-rest clock.
Fallingrain.strength: Falling Rain costs a free action, so Lone Wolf's second Action does not merely double the attacks - it doubles the Blade Skills, each of which throws another free attack on top - and the entire engine refills on a short rest instead of out of a 120-supply long rest.
Fallingrain.wants: Anything that handles a crowd: this chassis is 0 on AoE, 0 on control-area and 0 on rescue in every act, and the split rule makes 5+0 worse than 3+3.

Falling Rain read as one free-action attack per Willpower Die spent, using 1d4 in place of the weapon's damage dice but keeping ability and feat modifiers. If it replaces those too, the single-target raw drops about a rung.
Fanning the Flames priced at +1.5 Fire a hit on average, since stacks clear at the start of each of this body's turns.
Wisdom of Void costs 6 dice once per long rest and is excluded from the per-round raw.

Kennel.split: Ranger 17 (Beast Master) / Druid 3 (Circle of the Land)
Kennel.note: Ranger 1 first for the Strength and Dexterity saves, Beast Master at 3 for the Panther, Ranger to 17 for Share Spells, Druid 3 last. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Hunter's Mark up and re-targeted free, the Panther companion, and Conjure Animals held from Ranger 9 — `13458` makes it non-concentration until long rest, so it does not fight Hunter's Mark for the slot.
Kennel.strength: A duo is two bodies against encounters rebuilt for five, and this is the chassis that answers that literally rather than with damage. The Panther uses your proficiency bonus, is proficient in every saving throw, gains ability score improvements when you do, and can Help — the revive-and-advantage action — as a bonus action; Conjure Animals then adds a maintained set that survives until the next long rest. Share Spells at 15 makes one buff cover two actors.
Kennel.wants: Damage of any kind. This body's own single-target line is being outrun by Act II and its area damage is zero — everything it has, it delegates.
uncertain: Rule 2 excludes summons and extra bodies from §1 and §2 entirely, so the Panther, Summon Beast and Conjure Animals contribute nothing to either damage axis and everything to `act`. That is the rule working as written, but it means the damage rows read as a bare bow while the body actually fields three to five actors. Read `act` 5 as the score.

`act` 5 in Acts II and III is Conjure Animals at Ranger 9 made non-concentration until long rest by `13458` — the rubric's own named rung-5 example, sitting on a Druid at 5 — plus the Panther and Bestial Fury at 11. Act I is 4 (Panther plus Summon Beast, a multi-body set without the Conjure tier).

Druid 3 (Circle of the Land) adds nothing to the bow and its 2nd-tier concentration spells (Moonbeam, Flaming Sphere) cannot run beside Hunter's Mark. It buys Goodberry, Wild Shape on a short-rest clock and one feat. Not dead weight, but close to it on the damage axes.

AoE 0 is the convention this assignment holds throughout: §2 counts damage that reaches several enemies by the mechanism's own design, not an attack routine aimed at different targets. The routine's crowd contribution is already priced by `scoring-model.md` §5's 0.5 single-target crowd coefficient. If the convention is ruled the other way this body re-bases with every other martial in the roster.

Dawnstrike.split: Ranger 11 (Conclave of the Dawnstriders) / Barbarian 3 / Wizard 6
Dawnstrike.note: Ranger 1 first, Dawnstriders at 3 for Valkyrie, Ranger to 11 for Divine Flurry, Wizard 1–6 next, Barbarian 3 last. Configuration scored: two-handed greatsword on Strength — Zeal builds two stacks a hit with a two-hander — Herald of the Sun toggled to Radiant, Hunter's Mark up, Divine Flurry spent about 1.2 times a fight off the 3rd-tier slots, and Rage never entered. No class reaches 13, so it pays six feats.
Dawnstrike.strength: Herald of the Sun converts every weapon attack to Radiant, which is the second least-resisted type in the run and the direct answer to Absolute Wrath's layered physical resistance — and Divine Flurry then buys five extra attacks with the critical threshold lowered by two, for the one turn that ends a fight. The Barbarian dip is worth more here than on any other split in this assignment, because Reckless Attack's advantage is gated on a Strength melee attack roll and this is the only Ranger in the batch that makes one.
Dawnstrike.wants: A crowd answer and a body that can hold the fort through the Faded window — this one's burst turn is followed by a turn at −2 to every attack roll, and a duo has no third body to cover it.
uncertain: Act III carries a ×1.35 and Acts I and II do not, and that is the Reckless Attack pak clause doing its work. `5e Reckless Attack` v2 boosts only `IF(AttackRollAbility(Ability.Strength) and IsMeleeWeaponAttack())`; this body qualifies, but the Barbarian levels land at characters 18–20, so the multiplier exists in Act III alone. Reckless does not require raging, which is why the dip is live here while its Rage is not. The paired cost is carried on `dur`, which falls from 3 to 2 in Act III on enemy advantage (p_hit 0.65 → 0.88).
Rage itself is dead weight — entering it would switch off the Wizard block and break Hunter's Mark's concentration. Scored as never entered. Danger Sense is recorded from Act III.

Divine Flurry is priced net: it replaces an Action's two attacks with five, so +3 attacks a use, at about 1.2 uses a fight off `to_damage` 0.4 of the slot pool, with a flat ×0.95 on the whole round to carry the Faded penalty (−2 to attack rolls per stack until the end of the next turn). If Faded is worse than that in practice — it stacks per Flurry attack — Act III falls to 1.24 and stays rung 3.

Zeal is priced at roughly 0.6 extra attacks a round: 2 stacks a hit with a two-hander, 4 hits a round, 7 stacks to trigger. Valkyrie's own Extra Attack on landing is not counted as a gain, because Valkyrie consumes the Action that would have produced two attacks anyway; it is scored as a gap-closer, which is what it is in a duo that has to cover a whole battlefield.
Pursuit of Valor is Ranger 15 and out of reach at Ranger 11, so the kill-a-marked-target-for-a-free-Valkyrie loop the class file describes never comes online.

Drakeward.note: Ranger 1 first, Drakewarden at 3, Ranger to 17 for Perfected Bond, Fighter 3 last. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Hunter's Mark up, drake essence set to fire, Infused Strikes running, Drake's Breath spent about once a fight out of the levelled pool.
Drakeward.strength: Infused Strikes adds 1d6 of the drake's essence to any creature's weapon hit within 30 ft that the drake can see — in a two-body party that is a permanent damage rider on the partner as well as on this body, which is the only cross-character damage buff in the class list. Reflexive Resistance is a second life-saving reaction and Lone Wolf hands the body the spare Reaction to spend it with.
Drakeward.wants: Area damage and control. The drake and the breath weapon are this body's whole crowd answer and the breath is a long-rest clock; everything else it does points at one target.
uncertain: Infused Strikes is priced as firing on every hit, which is the single largest assumption in this record. The class file reads "adds 1d6 of the drake's essence type when any creature within 30 ft that it can see hits with a weapon attack" and states no once-per-turn cap. If it is in fact once a turn, Act I falls from 1.30 to 1.09 and the rung from 3 to 2. I did not open the pak to settle it.

Drake's Breath is 8d6 at Ranger 11 and 10d6 at 15, once per long rest free or off a 3rd+ slot; priced at about one use a fight out of `to_damage` 0.3 of the pool, amortised at 4 targets ÷ 4 rounds = 1 instance a round exactly as the rubric amortises one Fireball a fight.
Fire is a commonly resisted type, but the body also deals Piercing, so rule 4's ×0.5 does not apply. Choosing acid or poison essence would be worse, cold or lightning about the same.
The author's own caveat — that taking this subclass may require a new playthrough or the drake animates incorrectly — is a real risk to the whole chassis and no axis can express it.

Glamour.note: Ranger 1 first, Fey Wanderer at 3 for Otherworldly Glamour, Ranger to 17 for Misty Wanderer, Bard 3 (Lore) last for Expertise and three free proficiencies. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Hunter's Mark up, Dreadful Strikes, and Glamour's free proficiency taken on Persuasion.
Glamour.strength: Otherworldly Glamour adds this body's Wisdom modifier to every Charisma check, which in a two-character party is the whole face problem solved without a point of Charisma — and it stacks with Lore Expertise to put Persuasion at +16 against Act III's 18–22 town band while the same body is the one carrying Perception. Misty Wanderer then repositions both characters on a free Misty Step, Wisdom-modifier times a long rest.
Glamour.wants: Damage and a crowd answer. This body pays for its skill coverage with its damage line, which is being outrun from Act II, and it has no area damage at all.
uncertain: This is the one chassis in the assignment whose `skl` rises across the acts rather than falling, and the reason is Glamour: the Wisdom modifier it adds to Charisma checks scales with the same stat the pinned proficiency bonus does, so Persuasion keeps pace with the town-dialogue band while everyone else's falls behind it. The rung is authored 3/3/4 to agree with the map.

Beguiling Twist grants advantage on saves against charm and fear and a reaction to turn a successful one back onto another creature. There is no booster id that fits a two-condition advantage, so it contributes nothing to the derived saves rung of 4.
Dreadful Strikes is +1d4 once a turn, rising to 1d6 at Ranger 11 — a flat rider on four attacks, which is exactly the shape the rubric says must decay, and the ratio does: 1.12 / 0.87 / 0.75.
Fey Reinforcements at 11 is a free Summon Fey with a non-concentration toggle, which is what carries `act` from 2 to 4 alongside Conjure Animals.

Ambusher.note: Ranger 1 first, Gloom Stalker at 3, Ranger to 17, Rogue 3 (Assassin) last. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Hunter's Mark up, Iron Mind at 7, Stalker's Flurry at 11 and Shadowy Dodge at 15; Lone Wolf's +4 on Wisdom and Constitution. Everything it buys after character 8 is a refinement of a plan that was already complete.
Ambusher.strength: Iron Mind hands this body Wisdom and Intelligence save proficiency without spending Resilient, which in a two-save class covers the hole a duo dies to — and it stacks with Lone Wolf's own two picks to reach five disjoint saves. Dread Ambusher's +3 initiative plus Assassin's Alacrity restoring an Action and a Bonus Action at the top of combat is close to a free extra round in a party where there are only two initiative rolls to win.
Ambusher.wants: A crowd answer and sustained damage. This body's whole advantage is spent in round one, its area damage is zero, and its single-target line barely holds par once the opener is amortised across four rounds.
uncertain: The front-loading does not show on `st` and that is the arithmetic, not an oversight. Dread Ambusher's extra attack and Assassin's opener are once-a-fight effects amortised across four rounds, so they contribute a quarter of their headline in every act equally. The ratios do slide (1.15 / 1.09 / 1.01) but stay inside one band. The fall this body is supposed to show lands on `ctrl_s` and `ctrl_a` instead, where its Act I Fear and Ensnaring Strike are rung 2 material in Act I and background by Act III.
Stalker's Flurry is priced as one extra attack a round from character 11. If the free re-attack fires on every miss rather than once a turn it is closer to 1.4 a round and Act II reaches 1.19.

Assassinate: Ambush needs a Surprised target, and `Sensible Ambushing` makes surprise a flat DC 15 Wisdom save that applies to both sides — so the guaranteed-crit half of Assassin is not scored as reliable. Assassinate: Initiative's advantage against creatures that have not acted is scored on the opening round only, inside the amortised Dread Ambusher term.
Sneak Attack works off the bow (ranged), once a turn at 2d6; Rogue 5's off-turn reaction Sneak Attack is out of reach on a three-level dip.

Planeshift.note: Ranger 1 first, Horizon Walker at 3, Ranger to 17 for Spectral Defense, Rogue 3 (Thief) last. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Hunter's Mark up, and Planar Warrior applied twice a round on Lone Wolf's two Bonus Actions — which is also what forces the Thief dip, since Planar Warrior and Mark Quarry both want the same bonus action.
Planeshift.strength: Planar Warrior converts all of an attack's damage to Force, and Force is the least-resisted type in the run — so against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances this body simply does not have the problem the docs tell you to carry four weapons for. Distant Strike then adds a third attack whenever there are three enemies, which describes most of the fights a duo is losing.
Planeshift.wants: An area answer and a second concentration slot. This body has zero area damage, and Hunter's Mark already occupies the only concentration it will ever hold.
uncertain: The bonus budget is fully spent on Planar Warrior, which leaves no room to record Mark Quarry's re-targeting — and Thief's Fast Hands, which would be a third Planar Warrior a round, cannot be represented at all because the format caps bonus actions at 8. A third application would add roughly 9 raw a round in Act III. This is the second split in the assignment where the Thief dip's whole point is invisible to the schema.

Distant Strike's third attack only exists against three or more separate creatures; it is priced at 0.6 a round blended across crowd and boss. Its damage is carried on `st` and not on `aoe`, per the convention below — the total damage does not change with target count, only the number of bodies it lands on.
Planar Warrior is priced as a rider on an existing damage roll, so it adds no instance; the +1d8 rises to 2d8 at Ranger 11.

Ethereal Step is a whole turn of immunity once per short rest and is folded into the `dur` mitigation as roughly one round in four; it is scored as unusable outside turn-based mode, per the class file.

Volley.note: Ranger 1 first for the Strength and Dexterity saves, Hunter at 3 with Colossus Slayer, Ranger to 17, Fighter 3 last. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Hunter's Mark up and re-targeted free (Listo's rework), Colossus Slayer, Multiattack Defence at 7 and Uncanny Dodge at 15; Lone Wolf's +4 on Wisdom and Constitution rather than Dexterity, which buys a disjoint four-save set and pushes Dexterity 20 out to character 6 on both Act I feats.
Volley.strength: Volley is the only genuine area engine in the class list and it arrives at 11, which is the middle of the run rather than the end — and it is at-will, so it costs nothing against a long rest the party cannot afford. In a duo there is no third body to peel adds, so a repeatable four-target answer that spends no slot is worth more than the single-target line it does not have.
Volley.wants: Single-target damage and a concentration holder. This body is being outrun on `st` by Act III, and its own Hunter's Mark already occupies the one concentration slot it has.
uncertain: Volley is priced at the rubric's own anchor — 4 instances a round — rather than at my reading of the game, which would be 2 Volleys × 4 targets = 8 attack rolls and would put this body at `aoe` 3 in both acts. The published anchor row (69 → 1.06 → 2 at Act II, 87 → 1.06 → 2 at Act III) reproduces exactly on my per-hit figures, so I followed the authority rather than my own count. If Volley really does deliver 8 instances a round with two Actions, this row is a rung low.

Hunter's Mark is Concentration in this build — Listo pulled `20688` v1.0.0, before the non-concentration variant — so `concentration` is true and the body cannot hold anything else. Its +1d6 is scored on every hit on the marked target, not once a turn.
Ranger 17 does not reach Foe Slayer (20), so the Wisdom-modifier rider never lands.

`act` 4 in Act II is Conjure Animals at Ranger 9, which `13458` makes non-concentration until long rest — the rubric's own named rung-5 example on a Druid. It costs the levelled slots, which is why `to_damage` is 0.1 and `end` is 4 rather than 5.

Preymark.split: Ranger 17 (Monster Slayer) / Bloodhunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer)
Preymark.note: Ranger 1 first, Monster Slayer at 3, Ranger to 17 for Hold Monster and Slayer's Counter, Blood Hunter 3 (Ghostslayer) last. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Hunter's Mark and Slayer's Prey running together — the prey mark costs no concentration, which is the whole reason this conclave is here — plus Rite of the Dawn from Act III, paid in hit points.
Preymark.strength: Magic-User's Nemesis is a counterspell that costs a Reaction and no slot, on a short-rest clock, and Lone Wolf hands the body a spare Reaction to spend on it; Slayer's Counter makes a save against the boss's control spell succeed automatically. Those are the two effects that stop a two-body party being wiped by one enemy turn, and no other conclave carries either. Hunter's Sense then bypasses all resistances and immunities on the next hit, which is the direct answer to Absolute Wrath.
Preymark.wants: Crowd damage and area control. This body is built entirely around one designated target and has nothing at all for a room full of them.
uncertain: Hunter's Sense bypassing all resistances and immunities is not priced on the damage axes. Rule 4's ×0.5 penalty only applies to a body locked to one commonly resisted type, and this one carries Piercing and Radiant, so there is nothing for the strip to recover — but against a specifically resistant boss it is worth substantially more than the record shows. Recorded rather than rounded away.

Slayer's Counter (Ranger 15) makes a saving throw against the prey succeed automatically on a hit. There is no booster id for an auto-success and `supernatural-defense` covers only the +1d6, so the derived saves rung sits at 4 and under-reads this body against a boss.
Slayer's Counter's reaction attack is priced at 0.3 a round — it only fires when the prey forces a save on this body.

Rite of the Dawn is hemocraft 1d4 at Blood Hunter 3 and costs hit points to run; the drain is netted into the pool on `dur` rather than shown separately. `dark-augmentation` is Blood Hunter 10 and is not carried by this three-level dip.
