Rootbound.note: Ranger 1 first for the Strength and Dexterity saves, Primeval Guardian at 3, Ranger to 11 for Rooted Defense, Cleric 1–6 next, Barbarian 3 last. Configuration scored: longbow in Guardian form permanently — the form's 5 ft movement is free to an archer that never moves — with Spirit Guardians rather than Hunter's Mark holding the concentration slot from Act III, and Rage never entered. No class reaches 13, so it pays six feats.
Rootbound.strength: Guardian Soul pays temporary hit points every turn and Ancient Fortitude adds two maximum hit points per Ranger level, both for free and both forever — a mitigation stream on no clock at all, which is what a party that cannot afford 120-supply long rests actually needs. Rooted Defense then makes 30 ft of ground difficult terrain for enemies with no concentration and no resource, so the pair's one real concentration slot stays free for Spirit Guardians.
Rootbound.wants: Single-target damage. This body is a rooted archer with a healing pool and an area-denial field; it holds ground it cannot threaten, and it never kills a boss.
uncertain: Barbarian 3 is mostly dead weight on this split, but not entirely, and the reason is worth stating precisely. Rage forbids spellcasting and breaks concentration, so entering it would kill Spirit Guardians and the whole Cleric block — the chassis is scored with Rage never used. What survives is real: a d12 hit die, Danger Sense (recorded as a booster from Act III) and one feat. Reckless Attack survives too but is useless here, because `5e Reckless Attack` v2 gates its advantage on a Strength melee attack roll and this body shoots a bow.

Spirit Guardians is priced off the rubric's own anchor row — 42 raw over 4 instances at Act III, 74 with gear, 0.90 → rung 2 — and it takes the concentration slot from Hunter's Mark at Act III, which is why the Act III single-target line drops the Mark rider and still rises.

The Cleric domain is unnamed in the split. I scored a domain contributing Spirit Guardians and Spiritual Weapon and no heavy armour, because Cleric is not the level-1 class here and a multiclass Cleric grants none.

`dur` falls to 3 in Act III on the act table: the temporary hit points are half Ranger level and Ancient Fortitude is +2 per Ranger level, and Ranger stops at 11, so both froze at character 11 while enemy hits went from 10–29 to 13–40.
Guardian Soul's Piercing Thorns is turn-based-mode only per the class file, and the form is VFX-based and misbehaves in cutscenes.

Whiteout.note: Ranger 1 first, Snowlight at 3 for Glaring Frost, Ranger to 11 for Snow Blindness, Cleric 1–6 (Light) next, Paladin 3 last. Configuration scored: rapier and shield on Dexterity, Armour of Agathys as the per-fight opener, Word of Radiance and Radiance of the Dawn as the proactive Glaring Frost triggers, and Divine Smite spent as Radiant. No class reaches 13, so it pays six feats.
Whiteout.strength: Glaring Frost turns every Cold or Radiant damage instance into a Constitution save against Blindness, and this split exists to manufacture instances: Radiance of the Dawn is a short-rest four-target Radiant burst, Word of Radiance is an at-will one, Divine Smite is Radiant on demand and Armour of Agathys is Cold on every melee attacker. Blinding a room on a short-rest clock is worth more to two characters than any damage rider, and Snow Blindness then taxes 1d6 off every action a blinded enemy spends.
Whiteout.wants: A boss answer. Everything this body does scales with enemy count, and Blind is a Constitution save that brutes and undead shrug off — it needs a partner that can delete a single big target.
uncertain: Ranger 11 does not reach Snowborn Anthelion (15), which is what makes the blind engine an area effect. Without it, Glaring Frost blinds one creature per damage instance — so this body's mass blind comes entirely from multi-target Radiant sources (Word of Radiance, Radiance of the Dawn) supplying four instances at once, not from the conclave. That is why `ctrl_a` is 4 rather than 5 and why the hand-built Snowlight body outreads this one on area control despite four fewer Cleric levels.
Scored on Dexterity with a rapier, so `5e Reckless Attack` from the Paladin/Cleric side is irrelevant and no advantage multiplier is applied anywhere in this record.

Paladin 3 taken after level 1 grants no heavy armour and no saving throws, and Aura of Protection needs Paladin 6 — so `aura-of-protection` is deliberately absent. What the dip buys is Divine Smite on any class's slot, Channel Oath on a short rest, and Lay on Hands aimed outward.
The Cleric domain is scored as Light for Word of Radiance and Radiance of the Dawn; the split does not name it, and any other domain removes the proactive half of the engine and drops `ctrl_a` to 3.
Word of Radiance's save behaviour in Listo is `(unverified)` — save-negates rather than save-for-half would cut both the Act III AoE line and the number of Glaring Frost procs by about a fifth.

Lectern.split: Ranger 15 (Snowlight Conclave) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar) / Cleric 2 (Light)
Lectern.note: A hand-built control chassis, not a searched split — the worked sheet is `plugins/listo-build/lectern_v2.md`. Ranger 1 first, Snowlight at 3, Monk 1–3 at characters 4–6 for Friar's Bond, Ranger to 11, Cleric 1–2 at 15–16, Ranger to 15 for Snowborn Anthelion. Configuration scored: Shillelagh morningstar and shield over Unarmoured Defence, Friar's Retribution as the bond variant, Armour of Agathys as the per-fight opener, Lone Wolf's +4 on Wisdom and Constitution (the sheet's Line B).
Lectern.strength: It converts being attacked into mass Blindness. Friar's Retribution reflects 2×Wisdom Radiant on every hit that lands with no ki, no reaction and no cooldown; Glaring Frost turns each of those instances into a Constitution save; Snowborn Anthelion detonates each save into a 3 m blind; and Snow Blindness then taxes 1d6 Radiant off every Action, Bonus Action and Reaction a blinded enemy spends. The whole loop costs no slot, no ki and no action, which is exactly what a party facing 120-supply long rests wants — and Lone Wolf's second Reaction doubles the Kin-side Retribution proc.
Lectern.wants: Single-target damage against a boss, and a body that does not need this one's concentration — Friar's Bond holds the pair's only slot on this side, permanently.
uncertain: Acts I and II were derived here; the sheet's `2 ?` rows were never derived and are not carried forward. I rebuilt both on the sheet's own Act III method — 7 action-slots × 2 attacks ÷ 4 rounds, ki 4 as a short-rest pool spent in full (1 to Bond, 3 Flurries), 4 free Martial Arts strikes, Retribution at one proc a round, Armour of Agathys upcast to the act's tier. Act I is Ranger 5 / Monk 3 at Wisdom 20; Act II is Ranger 11 / Monk 3 / Cleric 1 at Wisdom 22 with Snow Blindness live. Both land at rung 3, not the sheet's provisional 2.

I removed Favored Foe from the sheet's Act III total (−4.5 raw). `ranger.md` says plainly that Favored Foe uses your concentration, and Friar's Bond holds the only slot — the sheet lists it under "free control that costs no concentration", which contradicts the class file. Act III still reads 1.17 → rung 3, so nothing moved, but the two sources disagree and the class file wins here.

The sheet contradicts itself on AoE. Its score table says 1 / 2 / 4 with worked arithmetic; its "Known weaknesses" bullet says 1 / 1 / 3. I took the worked arithmetic, because it shows the re-based par and the per-instance gear constant and the bullet does not.

Word of Radiance's Action is counted on both axes, per rule 3 as amended — the `actions` block records 7 attacking slots and one spell (Armour of Agathys), and the Word of Radiance line in `aoe_raw` is one of those attacking slots redirected. Whether Word of Radiance is save-negates or save-for-half in Listo is `(unverified)` per the sheet; save-negates would cut the Act III AoE line by roughly a fifth and still leave rung 4.

`war-caster` is recorded for Guardian of Light's advantage on Concentration checks — the schema keys that id to the effect, not the feat. It buys no rung, which is correct, but on a body whose entire engine rides one concentration ability it is the most load-bearing thing the saves block cannot score.
Friar's Retribution is the bond variant, not Friar's Blessing, so `friars-blessing` is deliberately absent and the derived saves rung is 4 rather than 5. That is the sheet's Line B trade.

Retribution is priced at one proc a round. The pak clause has no cooldown and Lone Wolf adds two Kin-side reaction procs, so three a round is defensible against a crowd — the sheet's own "the loop partly suppresses itself" caveat (blinded enemies attack at disadvantage) is why I held it at one. At three procs Act III `st` reaches 1.37 and `aoe` 2.9, both still inside their bands.
`skl` is authored 2 rather than the sheet's 3: Persuasion sits at +0 untrained on Charisma 10, and the routine town-dialogue check is a third of the axis.

Swarmlock.note: Ranger 1 first, Swarmkeeper at 3, Ranger to 11 for Mighty Swarm, Wizard 1–6 next, Barbarian 3 last. Configuration scored: longbow with Archery, Flurry of Moths as the gathered swarm for Psychic and Blind, Hunter's Mark up to feed Prey's Scent, and Lone Wolf's +4 on Intelligence and Constitution so the Wizard block has a save DC worth casting at. Rage is never entered. No class reaches 13, so it pays six feats.
Swarmlock.strength: The swarm fires once every round after any attack, with no resource and no concentration, and the Moths option is a Blind — a full attack shutdown in BG3 — on a body that also holds Web, Faerie Fire and Hypnotic Pattern off the Wizard block. In a party of two the free per-round reposition is also the only answer to being focused, since there is no third body to peel.
Swarmlock.wants: Damage and durability. This body bought two spell lists and paid for them with its save set and its hit points; it needs a partner that can absorb attention and finish targets.
uncertain: This split is at war with itself and the saves block is where it shows. Ranger wants Dexterity and Wisdom, Wizard wants Intelligence, Barbarian wants Strength and Constitution, and only two of those get Lone Wolf's +4. I spent it on Intelligence and Constitution so the Wizard's save DC reaches 18 by Act III, which costs the Wisdom proficiency and leaves a four-save set covering only two of the three key abilities — derived rung 3, not the 4 every other Ranger in this assignment reaches. Spending it on Wisdom instead buys rung 4 and a spell save DC of 15, which is not worth casting Hypnotic Pattern at.

Barbarian 3's Rage is dead here — it would switch off both spell lists — but the dip is not entirely dead: Danger Sense is a real booster and Reckless Attack works without raging. Reckless is nonetheless worth nothing to this body, because `5e Reckless Attack` v2 gates the advantage on a Strength melee attack roll and this one shoots a bow on Dexterity. No ×1.35 anywhere in this record.

Wizard 6 gives 3rd-tier slots, so Fireball is the whole area line: about 1.2 casts a fight out of `to_damage` 0.4 of a nine-slot pool, amortised at 4 targets ÷ 4 rounds. It lands at 0.43 → rung 1, which is the rubric's own "one Fireball per fight" anchor almost exactly.
The swarm fires once per round, so it is one extra damage instance a round, not one per attack; Mighty Swarm at 11 takes it from 1d6 to 1d8.

`ctrl_a` 3 rather than 4: Web, Faerie Fire and Hypnotic Pattern are all concentration, and Hunter's Mark already holds the slot — the pair cannot run two of them, which is exactly the constraint the rung-4 clause is about.

riders.single_axis_reason: Two of the eight action-slots are given to Fireball, which has no single-target mode; the weapon routine on the other six is what carries st.

Sleightweave.note: Rogue to 11, then Sorcerer 6 for third-level slots and Metamagic, then Warlock 3 for short-rest pact slots. Build-time picks: Quickened Spell and Twinned Spell as the Metamagic pair, Haste held on the partner from Act III, and two of the eight action-slots given over to levelled casting once Fireball is online. The Sorcerer multiclass node grants nothing at all — no saves, no armour, no skills — so the dip is bought purely for the slots.
Sleightweave.strength: Haste on the other body is the rubric's own example of handing an Action to your partner, and in a party of two that is a 50% increase in the party's action count from one concentration slot. The invisible permanent Mage Hand adds a third pair of hands on top, for no per-rest cost, which matters more at two characters than at four.
Sleightweave.wants: A partner worth Hasting — a body with multiattack or a bonus-action engine that converts the extra Action into real output — and a front line, since this one holds the pair's concentration and cannot afford to be hit.
uncertain: Haste is scored on `act` and nowhere else. It is a third Action for the partner, not for this body, so it never enters this record's damage block — and axis-rubrics.md rule 2 would exclude it there anyway.
act 4 in Act III rather than 5: the ladder's rung-5 Act III row wants uncapped undead or 9th-tier summons on top, and this body has Haste plus a Mage Hand and no summon set.
Twinned Spell is authored as buying nothing on rsc. The rubric notes Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Greater Restoration, but both are 4th and 5th tier and Sorcerer 6 stops at third-level slots.

Reliable Talent (Rogue 11) floors a proficient d20 at 10, which is not a modifier. It is entered as a flat +2 from Act II — exact expectation lift 12.75 - 10.50 = +2.25 — because the `skills` map carries modifiers only.

Handspun.note: Rogue to 11 for Reliable Talent, the sixth Sneak Attack die and the fourth feat, then Bard 6 for two more Expertises and a real spell list, then Warlock 3. Six expertised skills and a permanent invisible Mage Hand. Build-time picks: a rapier main-hand with a shortsword off-hand and no Two-Weapon Fighting style, and every levelled slot spent on control and rescue rather than damage.
Handspun.strength: Two characters must cover every check in the campaign, and this body clears the untelegraphed half of it alone — Expertise on four Rogue skills plus two Bard ones, under a Reliable Talent floor that makes a proficient roll of 1 impossible. The invisible permanent Mage Hand is a third pair of hands for levers and pulls that costs nothing per rest, which is worth more at a party size of two than at four.
Handspun.wants: Area damage and a front line: this body is 0 on aoe in every act, sits at 2 on `act`, and its Sneak Attack dice stop at 6d6 so it falls to par on single-target by Act III.

The skills map computes to a mean clear probability of about 0.75 in Act II and 0.77 in Act III, which sits exactly on the rung-5 boundary. Index 7 is authored at 4 rather than 5 because the per-check probabilities are coarse; the pair score recomputes from the map regardless.

Weavecutter.note: Rogue to 11, then Wizard 6, then Warlock 3. Every Seeker feature requires a free off-hand and at most light armour, so this body gives up the off-hand weapon attack that every other Rogue here takes twice a round — roughly a third of its instances — and fills the bonus action with Arcane Bolts instead. Build-time picks: the free off-hand kept open, and the Sorcery Point pool spent on Auspicious Parry before anything else.
Weavecutter.strength: Auspicious Parry turns an incoming hit into 1 damage for one point, and losing either character usually ends the fight — a flat 'no' button is worth more in a duo than its cost suggests. Spell Siphon and the Conduit reaction then give a two-person party the enemy-caster answer it otherwise has no room for, and Arcane Strike deals Force, the least-resisted type in the game.
Weavecutter.wants: Damage. This body falls to being outrun on single-target by Act III and has no rescue at all; it wants a partner who kills things while it says no to the fight-ending save.

Quickfingers.strength: Fast Hands stacks on top of Lone Wolf's two bonus actions for a third every round, and a Beast Master companion is a whole extra body in a party that only has two — between them this is the only Rogue here that answers the class's real weakness, which is that it has one attack per Action and nothing to do with the surplus.
