Farthought.note: Sorcerer 1-14 → Bard 6 (Valour). The Psionic Spells line — Mind Sliver through Evard's Black Tentacles, Summon Beholderkin and Dominate Person — is granted free and does not count against a Sorcerer's tiny known list, which is the class's real constraint. Psionic Sorcery casts any of it off sorcery points instead of slots, and with no verbal or somatic components. Sorcerer 14 stops one level short of Warping Implosion.
Farthought.strength: A duo has no third body to break a Dominate or a Fear, and Psionic Defenses at 6 hands this one psychic resistance and advantage on Charmed and Frightened saves for free — it patches the two conditions most likely to remove half the party. Casting the whole psionic list while Silenced, without spending a Metamagic pick on Subtle, leaves Twinned free for the partner.
Farthought.wants: Outward healing and revival. This body has none until the Bard tail lands at 15 — Rescue is a hard 0 through Acts I and II, which is the hole its partner exists to fill.
uncertain: Psionic Defenses grants advantage on saves against Charmed and Frightened. The registry declines two-named-condition effects on purpose, so it has no booster id and contributes nothing to index 8.

Area control reaches 4 on Evard's Black Tentacles being genuinely repeatable through Psionic Sorcery's second pool. Sorcery points are a long-rest resource, so that is about one psionic cast a fight on top of slots, not a short-rest clock.
Summon Beholderkin is a real third body from Sorcerer 7 but is excluded from the damage block by rule 2 and priced on Actions instead.

Amethyst.split: Sorcerer 11 (Draconic Bloodline (vanilla) + Draconic Bloodline Expanded) / Bard 6 / Warlock 3
Amethyst.note: Sorcerer 1-11 → Warlock 3 at 12-14 → Bard 6 (Lore) at 15-20, on the Amethyst ancestry. Draconic Bloodline Expanded gives Amethyst a Force damage type, so Elemental Affinity at 6 adds Charisma to every Magic Missile dart and to every Eldritch Blast beam the Warlock dip brings. The Bard college is not named in the split; Lore is chosen for Magical Secrets at 6, which is where Haste enters. Sorcerer 11 never reaches Draconic Presence.
Amethyst.strength: Twinned Haste covers 100% of a two-person party for one Metamagic pick, and the damage that funds the rest is Force — the least-resisted type in the list, which is what Absolute Wrath's layered resistances are for. Beams and darts are separate damage rolls, so this body collects the act's gear rider six to eight times a round where par's greatsword collects it four.
Amethyst.wants: Rescue and durability. It is a d6 chassis in a robe with nothing outward until the Bard tail lands at 15, and its concentration is committed to Haste, so it holds no control either.
uncertain: The load-bearing claim is that Agonizing Blast and Elemental Affinity both apply to the same Eldritch Blast beam. Each adds the Charisma modifier and neither excludes the other in the text available here, so a beam is scored at 1d8 + 2×Cha. If they do not stack, Act II and III single-target both fall a rung.

Elemental Affinity is scored as applying per Magic Missile dart, which is what sorcerer.md asserts ("adding Cha mod to every Magic Missile dart"). Per-cast instead of per-dart would cost roughly a third of the single-target line.

Magic Missile is carried auto-hit at 1/0.65 relative to par and at one instance per dart. That is two compounding advantages on the same spell; it is what the rubric's instance rule says, but it is the softest arithmetic in this record.
The split names no Bard college. Lore is the configuration scored, for Magical Secrets at 6; a Valour or Swords tail would trade Haste and Counterspell for Extra Attack and drop Actions from 4 to 2.
Only two damage types, both of which the body genuinely deals. Force is nearly unresisted, so the narrow set is a deliberate strength here rather than the exposure it usually is.

Bulwarksong.note: Sorcerer 1-14 → Bard 6 (Stormcalling), with Peace taken as the Chosen of the Gods domain. That fixes the class's two structural faults at level 1 — medium armour and shields on a no-armour d6 chassis — and puts Sanctuary, Aid, Beacon of Hope and Greater Restoration on the sheet as Sorcerer spells, so Metamagic applies to them. Extra Attack arrives at 6. Sorcerer 14 misses Unearthly Recovery at 15.
Bulwarksong.strength: Twinned covers 100% of a two-person party for one Metamagic pick, which is a niche pick in a party of four and the best one in the list here — Twinned Cure Wounds and Twinned Greater Restoration reach everyone. The armour and shield proficiency saves a feat and roughly four points of AC on the joint-lowest hit die in the game.
Bulwarksong.wants: A tougher partner. This body carries Warding Bond and should not: a d6 chassis is usually the softer half, and a bond running that way lowers the floor it was meant to raise.
uncertain: Favored Soul (Peace) at Sorcerer 3 is the class's only Warding Bond, confirmed by pak sweep against LHB_FavoredSoul_Domain_Peace. Twinned does nothing for it: Target_WardingBond_UCL gates on not Self() and refuses a second cast while the caster holds WARDING_BOND_CASTER.

The redirect is recorded because the body genuinely has it, but the schema counts only the tougher body's bond and this is a d6 chassis. On most pairings it will be inert or harmful, and no axis shows that.
Peace is chosen over Life as the domain. Life would trade Warding Bond and Sanctuary for Revivify, Death Ward and Raise Dead, which is a different Rescue profile at the same rungs.

Scholarblade.note: Sorcerer 1-8 → Paragon 3 (Spellblade) at 9-11 → Sorcerer 9-17, with Life as the Chosen of the Gods domain. Favored Soul supplies medium armour, shields and Extra Attack at 6; Spellblade's Scholar's Armament then makes the main-hand weapon roll Charisma for both attack and damage, so one stat does the spell DC, the swing and the Spell Sword riders. Dueling is the fighting style taken.
Scholarblade.strength: It is the rare genuinely single-stat body in a run where the primary must reach 20 by character 6 and 22 by 18 — every point of Charisma pays four times. Willpower Dice are a short-rest pool in an economy where a long rest costs 120-plus supplies, and Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Revivify off the Life list cover a two-person party completely.
Scholarblade.wants: Area control. Its own crowd answer is a Fireball off a shrinking share of the slot pool, and it has nothing that removes several enemies' turns.
uncertain: Scholar's Armament moves the attack roll onto Charisma, and anything keyed on the ability that actually rolled stops firing. The 5e Reckless Attack pak was read this run and keys on the rolling ability; the same shape applies to Strength-gated heavy armour, Athletics and any Strength-keyed rider. No Barbarian levels here, so Reckless Attack itself is not in play, but the class of interaction is and it is why no Strength-keyed effect is scored.

Paragon taken at 9 rather than 1 loses heavy armour, the Con+Cha saves and the two starting skills; it keeps shields, martial weapons, medium armour, Willpower Dice, the Fighting Style and the subclass. Saves are unaffected because Sorcerer grants the same two at level 1.

Act I has no Paragon and therefore no Scholar's Armament, so the weapon line swings off a secondary Strength or Dexterity at 14. That is why single-target sits at 2 despite Extra Attack landing at Sorcerer 6.

Spell Sword attacks are "treated as cantrips" but cast as level 1 until Arcane Surge at Paragon 6, which this split never reaches. They are not credited in the damage block; if they scale on character level like ordinary cantrips, Act III single-target rises.
The Favored Soul Life list is taken from the mod page summary in sorcerer.md; the War and Tempest alternatives are named there but not enumerated, so a different domain pick is not costed here.
Skills falls to 1 by Act III: Sorcerer grants two Charisma skills, a late Paragon grants none, and Arcane Knowhow's Expertise lands on Arcana, which the axis does not score.

Gravebreath.note: Sorcerer 1-8 → Cleric 3 (Twilight) at 9-11 → Sorcerer 9-17. Strength of the Grave turns the first drop to 0 HP into 1 HP instead, on the joint-lowest hit die in the game, and the Twilight dip buys heavy armour, martial weapons and Twilight Sanctuary's per-round temporary hit points. Hound of Ill Omen recharges on a short rest.
Gravebreath.strength: The two things that kill a duo are a body going down and a save being failed, and this chassis answers the first twice over — Strength of the Grave from level 1 and a sanctuary that re-lays temporary hit points on both bodies every round for a charge a short rest refunds. Hound of Ill Omen then hands one enemy disadvantage on saves without spending concentration, so the partner's control lands.
Gravebreath.wants: Someone to carry Act I. Rescue is 0 and armour is a robe until character 9; everything defensive on this sheet arrives with the Cleric dip.
uncertain: The split is Sorcerer 17, so Umbral Form never arrives — it is an 18th-level feature in both the Expanded mod and Expansion. The seed is filed under the subclass's headline durability feature and the build cannot reach it; durability here is Twilight Sanctuary and Strength of the Grave instead.

Durability rises to 4 in Act II and falls to 3 in Act III: Twilight Sanctuary at Cleric 3 is a flat 1d6+3 a round and does not upcast, so it is outrun by the act's hit sizes exactly as the rubric predicts of a fixed feature.
Goon's Cleric Overhaul removes the skill proficiencies a Cleric multiclass used to grant, so the Twilight dip adds none. That is why Skills falls to 1 by Act III.
True Darkness is not installed, so the published Shadow Sorcerer darkness builds do not work here; Darkness is scored as an ordinary area control spell.
Gravebreath.address: sorcerer/Shadow Magic (vanilla) + Shadow Magic Expanded - Umbral Form:durability

riders.name: Heart of the Storm
riders.single_axis_reason: It fires on every enemy within 6m of the caster whenever a lightning or thunder spell is cast, regardless of that spell's target, so it cannot be focused onto a single creature.

riders.name: Heart of the Storm
riders.single_axis_reason: It fires on every enemy within 6m of the caster whenever a lightning or thunder spell is cast, regardless of that spell's target, so it cannot be focused onto a single creature.

riders.name: Heart of the Storm
riders.single_axis_reason: It fires on every enemy within 6m of the caster whenever a lightning or thunder spell is cast, regardless of that spell's target, so it cannot be focused onto a single creature.

Galewrack.note: Sorcerer 1-14 → Bard 6 (Valour). Tempestuous Magic flies this body 9m as a bonus action after every levelled cast, Heart of the Storm adds free damage around it on every lightning or thunder spell, and Storm's Fury at 11 punishes each melee attacker as a reaction. Sorcerer 14 never reaches Wind Soul, and the Valour tail is taken for medium armour and shields rather than for Extra Attack.
Galewrack.strength: Lone Wolf hands out two Reactions and a two-person party has no front line, so a caster that both punishes melee attackers twice a round and disengage-flies out of reach for free every turn is solving its own worst problem. The MCM note that Sorcerer11thSubclass is set non-default is what puts Storm's Fury in Act II rather than Act III.
Galewrack.wants: Rescue and a damage type outside the storm. Rescue is 0 until the Bard tail lands, and lightning and thunder are the whole offence.
uncertain: Heart of the Storm is credited at two enemies within 6m, not the rubric's four, because a d6 Sorcerer standing in the middle of four enemies is not the configuration this chassis is played in. At four targets it would take Act III area damage to rung 5.

Whether Storm's Fury lands at Sorcerer 11 or 14 is unsettled: the installed profile sets misc.Sorcerer11thSubclass to a non-default true and sorcerer.md flags the key name as ambiguous. Scored at 11, which puts it in Act II; at 14 the control-single rise moves an act later.

Lightning and thunder are the entire offence apart from Fireball. Under Absolute Wrath a partner sharing either type leaves the pair badly exposed; no multiplier is applied because Fireball is a third type on the same list.

Tidesong.split: Sorcerer 11 (Wild Magic (vanilla) + Wild Magic Subclass - Additional Spells) / Bard 6 / Warlock 3
Tidesong.note: Sorcerer 1-11 → Warlock 3 at 12-14 → Bard 6 (Lore) at 15-20. Bend Luck at 6 spends two sorcery points on a reaction to add or subtract 1d4 from any visible creature's attack, check or save; the `14228` subclass list adds Hypnotic Pattern, Confusion, Polymorph and Dominate Person, castable off sorcery points via Arcane Chaos. The college is not named in the split; Lore is chosen so Cutting Words sits beside Bend Luck. Wild Magic is the one vanilla bloodline Expansion never extends past 11.
Tidesong.strength: Lone Wolf hands out two Reactions and this chassis has two different single-roll interventions to spend them on — Bend Luck on the enemy's save against the partner's Hold Monster, Cutting Words on the attack that would drop a d6 body. In a party of two the fight usually turns on one roll, which is exactly the granularity both features operate at.
Tidesong.wants: A partner that can survive this body's own surges. A Banish, a Confusion or a self-inflicted Fireball removes half the party here, and the other half has to finish the fight alone.
uncertain: Bend Luck, Arcane Chaos and Quickened Spell all draw on the same eleven sorcery points, so the reaction is pool-bound at roughly 1.7 uses a fight rather than reaction-bound at two a round. The rungs are scored against the pool, not the reaction count.

Wild Magic surges are scored as neutral. In a duo they are not: sorcerer.md is explicit that a bad surge removes half the party, and durability at 2 does not carry that risk. Nothing in the model can express a variance cost.

Rescue sits at 1 through Acts I and II on Bend Luck aimed at the partner's saving throw. That is prevention on a resource clock rather than the damage redirection the rung-1 text describes, so the placement is a judgement.
The split names no Bard college; Lore is the configuration scored, for Cutting Words as a second reaction and Magical Secrets at 6.
Mirror Image and Blink are on the free subclass list and are real mitigation layers, but each costs a slot and an Action; durability is scored without them.
Tidesong.address: sorcerer/Wild Magic (vanilla) + Wild Magic Subclass - Additional Spells:reaction

Feylock.note: A cone-and-control Archfey opened at Warlock 1 for Wisdom and Charisma saves, with a Stormcalling Bard block for Conductor, bonus-action Staccato Lightning and Concussion. Three of its eight action-slots a fight go to pact-slot control rather than to blasting, which is what holds its single-target down.
Feylock.strength: Fey Presence is an area charm-or-fear on a short-rest clock from level 1 and Repelling Blast lands every turn without concentration, so this body can remove several enemies' turns while the pair's one concentration slot is still free - the exact bind a duo hits when Listo's encounter mods add bodies.
Feylock.wants: A durable partner that can hold a front line, because this chassis sits at durability 2 in every act and dies to anything that reaches it.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.

Eldritch Cone is frozen at 3d10 from character 10 (Zone_EldritchCone reads LevelMapValue(EldritchZoneDamage), which ends at 3d10) and its SpellSuccess never checks AgonizingBlast, so it does not scale with beams, Charisma or gear riders. Its decay from Act II to Act III is the par rising underneath it.
Eldritch Cone is taken from Act II; at Warlock 9 that is the fifth of five invocations, alongside Agonizing Blast, Repelling Blast, Devil's Sight and Eldritch Mind, and there is no room for a sixth.
Staccato Lightning's +Charisma needs an electrical or concussive status on the target and needs concentration held on Conductor, which is the pair's one slot.
Archfey gets no 14th-level feature from Expansion; the class file flags whether another mod fills the gap as unverified.

Celestial.note: A Paladin-opened melee Celestial: heavy armour and Wisdom/Charisma saves at level 1, Extra Attack at Paladin 5, then fourteen Warlock levels feeding Eldritch Smite off short-rest pact slots. Healing Light is its rescue engine and it never blasts.
Celestial.strength: Healing Light is a bonus-action heal that spends no spell slot at all, so it stacks with an Action and with Lone Wolf's second Action in the same turn - and Revivify sits on a pact slot that comes back on a short rest, which is the only cheap revival in the list when a long rest costs 120+ supplies.
Celestial.wants: A crowd answer and a second concentration slot, because this chassis is 0-1 on AoE in every act and spends its own on nothing.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.
Sword-and-shield with the Duelling style, NOT Great Weapon Master: the pak puts a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty against +5/+9/+11 damage, which is a net loss from Act II against par AC.
Eldritch Smite off a 5th-level pact slot is 6d8 and refreshes on a short rest, so the whole pool is spent every fight; half of it is booked to damage and half to control and rescue.
No Heavy Armour Master: the six feats go to Charisma 22, War Caster, Tough and Alert, which is what holds durability at 3 rather than 5.
Searing Vengeance triggers on being downed and heals to half maximum hit points; scored as durability, not rescue.

Dawnpact.note: The cone-blasting Celestial. Every offensive thing it does is at-will and slot-free, so all three pact slots stay free for Revivify, Greater Restoration and Chains of Carceri, and the Cleric 3 tail adds Preserve Life on the same short-rest clock. Its Mystic Arcanum 9th is committed to Power Word Kill, which is why rescue stops at 4.
Dawnpact.strength: Nothing that keeps the pair alive here is on a long-rest clock: Revivify off a pact slot, Preserve Life off Channel Divinity and Celestial Resistance's temporary hit points all return on a short rest, which is exactly the resource profile a 120-supply long rest rewards.
Dawnpact.wants: A body that can take a hit, because this chassis is a robe caster at durability 2-3 and has no way to stop something reaching it.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.

Eldritch Cone is frozen at 3d10 from character 10 (Zone_EldritchCone reads LevelMapValue(EldritchZoneDamage), which ends at 3d10) and its SpellSuccess never checks AgonizingBlast, so it does not scale with beams, Charisma or gear riders. Its decay from Act II to Act III is the par rising underneath it.
Mystic Arcanum picks are build-time choices under rule 3, so the 9th is scored as Power Word Kill for control-single 5 and CANNOT also be Mass Heal; that is what caps rescue at 4 rather than 5.
Whether a Cleric multiclass node carries the Life domain's heavy armour is not resolved in the class file; scored as light armour with the Moderately Armoured feat.
Healing Light is a long-rest pool of 1 + Warlock level d6, split half to self (durability) and half outward (rescue).

Hellward.split: Warlock 14 (The Fiend) / Paladin 6 (Oath of the Ancients)
Hellward.note: Sword-and-shield Fiend opened at Paladin 1, reaching Aura of Protection at character 6 and then spending fourteen levels on pact slots and Dark One's Blessing. It stops one level short of Ancients' Aura of Warding, which is the defensive feature the oath is actually known for.
Hellward.strength: Aura of Protection covers the entire party because the party is two, and Dark One's Blessing hands back Charisma plus Warlock level in temporary hit points on every kill - a body that is hard to remove and hands its partner a save bonus is worth more here than one that kills faster, because losing either half ends the fight.
Hellward.wants: Both tempo axes: this chassis is 2/2/2 on single-target and 0-1 on AoE, and buys the pair's floor instead.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.
Paladin 6 does NOT reach Aura of Warding (Paladin 7), so the oath's spell-damage resistance is not scored; if the split is meant to be Paladin 7 the durability and pair-save case both improve.
Heavy Armour Master taken from Act I because this is the durability-niche seed; AC 20 plus flat reduction against Act I's 5.4 crowd hit is what puts the row at the act's ceiling.
Hurl Through Hell (Warlock 14, Expansion) counted once a fight at 10d10; whether Listo's copy is short-rest or long-rest is not stated in the class file.
Fiendish Resilience priced as a proportional layer worth about x1.4 blended in Act III.

Farsight.note: The control patron played as control: Evard's Black Tentacles off a short-rest pact slot, Chains of Carceri, and a Mystic Arcanum ladder ending at a 9th-level Power Word Kill. Mesmerist 3 arrives only at character 18, which is why its rescue is 0 until Act III and then jumps.
Farsight.strength: Its hard control runs off pact slots that come back twice a long rest, so a duo gets Dominate Person or Evard's in every fight rather than once a day - and Hypnotic Stare is a permanent minus one to an enemy's saves for a bonus action and no resource at all, which stacks under everything else.
Farsight.wants: A front-line body: this chassis falls to durability 1 by Act III and has no melee answer of any kind.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.

Eldritch Cone is frozen at 3d10 from character 10 (Zone_EldritchCone reads LevelMapValue(EldritchZoneDamage), which ends at 3d10) and its SpellSuccess never checks AgonizingBlast, so it does not scale with beams, Charisma or gear riders. Its decay from Act II to Act III is the par rising underneath it.

Only a quarter of the pact pool is booked to damage: Evard's Black Tentacles, Dominate Person and the Arcanum ladder are this body's whole point, and the rubric's one-pool-one-axis rule means the slots cannot be claimed twice.

Level order assumed Warlock 1-17 then Mesmerist 3, so Trickster's tricks and Towering Ego arrive only at character 18. Opening Mesmerist 1-3 instead would move rescue to 4 in all three acts and cost the Wisdom save proficiency.
Mesmeric Mirror is a Tier-1 trick learnable at Mesmerist 3 and is what carries rescue 4 in Act III; Gift of Will is Tier 2 and needs Mesmerist 7, which this split never reaches.

Cursebrand.split: Warlock 12 (The Hexblade) / Paladin 6 (Oath of the Ancients) / Fighter 2 (none)
Cursebrand.note: Opened at Warlock 1 so Hex Warrior puts Charisma on a weapon from level one, then Paladin 6 for Aura of Protection and Fighter 2 for Action Surge. Hexblade's Curse and Great Weapon Master both add the proficiency bonus, and it spends no feat on Heavy Armour Master.
Cursebrand.strength: Aura of Protection at character 6 covers both bodies for the whole run, and Armour of Hexes makes the cursed target miss half the time - against the one boss a duo cannot out-tempo, that is a defensive layer no amount of AC buys.
Cursebrand.wants: Area damage and area control: this chassis is 1-2 on AoE and falls to control-area 1 by Act III, and 5+0 is worse than 3+3.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.

Sword-and-shield with Duelling and no Great Weapon Master; Hexblade's Curse supplies the proficiency-bonus damage rider on its own. A Barbarian dip would not help either: 5e Reckless Attack keys on AttackRollAbility(Strength), and Hex Warrior rolls the attack off Charisma.
Hunger of Hadar is claimed as area DAMAGE here, so under the rubric's one-pool-one-axis rule control-area cannot also claim it and rests on Turn the Faithless alone.
No Heavy Armour Master: the six feats go to Charisma 22, War Caster, Alert, Tough and Resilient, which is what keeps durability at 3 rather than 5.
Paladin 6 again stops short of Aura of Warding at Paladin 7.

Bladepact.note: A pure short-rest Hexblade: Extra Attack from Deepened Pact rather than from a martial class, Eldritch Smite off three 5th-level pact slots every fight, and a Favored Soul 6 tail taken with the Life domain for Charisma-based healing and, incidentally, medium armour and shields on a class that has neither.
Bladepact.strength: Three 5th-level slots that come back twice per long rest is more real casting per adventuring day than a full caster gets, and Favored Soul puts Cure Wounds and Lesser Restoration on the same Charisma the weapon already uses - one stat pays for the attack, the smite, the save DC and the healing.
Bladepact.wants: Area damage and a durable front line, because this chassis is 1/1/1 on AoE and only 3 on durability despite being a melee body.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.

Favored Soul domain taken as LIFE, not Peace. Peace at Sorcerer 3 is this build's only route to Warding Bond, but the rubric counts only the TOUGHER body's bond and this body sits at durability 3, so the bond would lower the pair's floor rather than raise it. No redirect block is authored.
There is no Paladin level here, so Divine Smite is NOT available; every smite is Eldritch Smite off a pact slot.
Sword-and-shield rather than a greatsword, which costs about a rung of single-target and is what keeps durability at 3.

Warpline.note: The only Warlock in the batch whose area damage does not come from Eldritch Cone: Warp Wielder is gated on three specific Eldritch Blast spell ids and the Cone is not one of them, so a Psyker that takes the Cone loses its patron. It blasts beams instead and detonates them, and it pays for every beam in maximum hit points.
Warpline.strength: Three beams on one target run the Warp clock to zero inside a single Action, so a focused Eldritch Blast ends in a detonation that takes no attack roll and allows no save, in Force, which almost nothing in the list resists - and the same beams spread over a crowd put a 3m explosion on each of them, so one at-will resource covers both tempo axes.
Warpline.wants: A body that can carry the pair's durability outright, because Perils of the Warp makes this the softest chassis in the roster and there is no configuration where the damage is bought without the bleed.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is 1d8 a beam in Listo, not 1d10, with beams at character 5/10/17, so this body fires 2/3/4 a cast by act and Agonizing Blast adds Charisma to each.

Read from Cahoots Feats Overhaul: Heavy Armour Master is DamageReduction(All,Flat,LevelMapValue(CHT_HeavyArmourMaster)) = 3/5/5 by act, all damage, confirmed. Great Weapon Master is +5/+9/+11 damage against a -3/-5/-6 attack penalty (CHT_GWM_SS_Damage / _AttackPenalty), so it is NOT toggled on for any body here.

The Warp detonation level map is keyed to WARLOCK level, not character level, and this split stops at Warlock 14, so the die is frozen at 3d10 rather than reaching 4d10 at 15. That freeze is worth roughly 15 damage a round in Act III.

Load-bearing and unresolved: whether a Warp duration driven to 0 expires and detonates in-turn or at the start of the next turn. In-turn gives two detonations a round, which is what is scored; otherwise it is one and single-target drops a rung.

Durability is the biggest open question in this record. Taken literally, Perils of the Warp's IncreaseMaxHP(-die) with MultiplyEffectsByDuration and 8 applications a round against a tick-down of 1 drives maximum hit points to zero during round 2, which would make the patron unplayable rather than costly. Scored at 1 as a body that is alive but the softest in the roster; the honest range is 0 to 2 and one combat log settles it.
Endurance is 3, not the Warlock default of 4: axis-rubrics.md names The Psyker specifically as a body that pays hit points to run its output.
The random Perils table is a liability until Warlock 14 - Repulsor and Silence do not exclude the partner, and in a two-body party the partner is half the roster.

Wardkeep.note: Arcane Ward taken all the way to Spell Resistance at 14, with a late Bard 5 for the short-rest Inspiration heal and a single Barbarian level for Unarmoured Defence on a body that will never wear armour. It is the only school that fixes the Wizard's own fragility, and it pays for that by adding nothing at all to damage.
Wardkeep.strength: Projected Ward is the rarest thing in the class — a way to spend Lone Wolf's second Reaction on keeping the *other* character alive — and with two bodies the ward covers half the party rather than a quarter. Improved Abjuration refills it on the free rest rather than the 120-supply one, so it is a defensive pool the run can actually afford to use.
Wardkeep.wants: A body that removes enemy action points fast. This one is rung 1-2 on single-target throughout and its whole contribution is keeping the pair upright.
uncertain: The split names no Bard College; Lore is assumed for the three bonus proficiencies and Expertise, which is what carries skl from 1 to 3 in Act III. Named in the note.

Arcane Ward is scored into the durability pool at roughly 20/35/35 absorbed per fight (cap 2x wizard level, refilling on short rests from 10). The recharge rate depends on how many Abjuration spells the body actually casts, which the damage plan does not favour.
Barbarian 1 is taken after level 1, so it grants no saves; it is here for Unarmoured Defence and the d12 die. Raging would switch off the whole chassis and is not part of the configuration.

Interpose.note: Four different things to do with a reaction — Projected Ward, Counterspell, Shield and Cutting Words — on a run that hands every body two of them. Bard 6 adds Lore's skills, Font of Inspiration and two Magical Secrets, and there is no armour anywhere in the build.
Interpose.strength: Lone Wolf's second Reaction is normally wasted on a caster that only owns Counterspell; this body has four claims on it and can spend both every round. Projected Ward in particular spends a reaction on the *other* character, which is the only durability transfer a Wizard has, and in a two-body party the partner is half the action economy.
Interpose.wants: A front line. This body is a robe with a ward, and its single-target damage never clears par.
uncertain: This body and wizard/Abjuration:durability differ only in the dip: Bard 6 (Lore) here against Bard 5 plus Barbarian 1 there. The damage arithmetic is nearly identical and so are the rungs; the separation is one point of Act III AC and two Magical Secrets, and it is genuinely small.
Arcane Ward is scored into the durability pool at roughly 20/35/35 absorbed per fight.
Act III rsc 4 assumes a Magical Secrets pick at Lore 6 reaches Death Ward; the Extender pulls from every installed list but the exact level-6 pool was not read.

Bladesong.note: Extra Attack at Wizard 6, Bladesong for +4 AC and +4 Constitution saves, and Song of Victory adding Intelligence to weapon damage from 14, with a late Fighter 3 for Action Surge and Second Wind. It spends five of its eight action-slots swinging, so its area damage never reaches what a robe caster of the same level manages.
Bladesong.strength: +4 AC and +4 to Constitution saves off a class feature is the largest concentration-protection package a full caster can field, and it needs no armour proficiency and no gold at 4x prices. One ability score also drives both halves — Song of Victory puts Intelligence on the weapon — so the point buy funds Constitution instead of a second attack stat.
Bladesong.wants: A body that carries the crowd. This one is rung 2-3 on AoE because it attacks rather than casts, and it has no rescue in any act.
uncertain: Lone Wolf's +4 goes on Intelligence and Dexterity here rather than Intelligence and Constitution, because the body swings; Constitution proficiency is bought with Resilient. That is the opposite of every other Wizard in this batch and it is why the save set reads the same while the stat line does not.

MCM resolved from the install: Expansion's Bladesinger and WizardBladesinger are both OFF, so Bladesong is Larian's flat +2/+3/+4 rather than Expansion's Intelligence-scaled version, and Song of Victory stays at 14.
Bladesong is 3-4 uses per LONG rest, which is the resource this run taxes hardest; three uses exactly covers the three hard fights in a cycle, with nothing spare.
Fighter 3 is taken after level 1, so no heavy armour and no saves; Eldritch Knight contributes one third-caster level, which is why Act III caster level is 18 rather than 20.

Transpose.note: Two off-list Conjuration picks at 6 reach into the druid and cleric summon pools, and Focused Conjuration at 10 means damage cannot break concentration on any of them. Sorcerer 3 adds Font of Magic and Metamagic; the school itself adds almost nothing to this body's own damage.
Transpose.strength: With two players against five-body encounters, the thing that loses a fight is a concentration break dropping your third and fourth combatants — Focused Conjuration removes that failure mode outright, which is worth more here than in a party that still has two bodies left. Ultimate Transposition is also a free extract-the-other-player button at 18m.
Transpose.wants: Anything that can take a hit or heal. This is a robe with summons in front of it: rung 2 on durability in every act and effectively nothing aimed at the partner.
uncertain: Summon damage is excluded from both damage axes per rule 2 and scored on Actions only, which is why this chassis reads identically to a plain caster on st and aoe. That is the rule working, not an omission.
The mod places its features at 3 and 6 while vanilla places them at 2 and 6; whether the level-2 slot is replaced or supplemented is unverified and would move the Act I Actions rung.

act 5 in Acts II and III rests on the rubric's own rung-5 clause for a maintained summon set with Automated Summons handing turns to the AI. Act I is 4 because at 4th-level slots the set is three or four bodies and Focused Conjuration is not yet online.

The bonus-action conjured items (Alchemist's Fire, acid vial and the rest) are not counted in the raws: conjuring costs a bonus action and throwing costs an Action, and the Action is worth more as a spell.

Portent.note: Three Portent dice that replace an attack roll or saving throw made nearby, refunded by Prophecies on a short rest, plus a Stormcalling Bard dip for Chorus of Thunder and a bonus-action lightning cantrip. Its control costs no concentration and no slot, which is the whole argument for it.
Portent.strength: Portent is a reaction and Lone Wolf hands out two of them, so the dice are a pool of forced enemy rolls that never competes with the pair's one concentration slot — and with only two characters, turning a single boss save is often the entire fight. Prophecies put that pool on the free rest rather than the 120-supply one.
Portent.wants: A front line and a healer. This body is rung 2 on durability throughout and everything it does is spent on other people's dice rather than on removing enemies.
uncertain: Portent is a pre-rolled die forced onto a roll, so it guarantees a KNOWN value rather than a failure — average 10.5. It is scored as no-concentration single-target control on a short-rest clock, not as a save-or-die, and that is why ctrl_s is 4 rather than 5 before Act III.
Act III ctrl_s 5 stacks two independent no-concentration levers: Portent plus Chorus of Thunder's Concussion off the Bardic Inspiration pool, under 9th-tier control from caster level 20.

Portent aimed at the PARTNER's failed save is scored as Rescue 3 (repeatable outward prevention on a short-rest clock). It is not healing and it does not reach the Death Ward rung; the doubt is recorded here.
Otherworldly Archetypes entered Listo on a playtesting footing and Stormcalling's numbers come from the author's documentation site, not a pak read.
Expansion's changelog adds Greater Portent at 14; the class file lists it as unverified and nothing is scored for it.

Gaze.note: Hypnotic Gaze holds one creature without concentration and, with the installed patch, breaks the target's own concentration when it lands; Split Enchantment at 10 makes every single-target enchantment hit two. Sorcerer 3 buys Heightened Spell. It spends only 40% of its pool on damage and reads rung 1 on single-target in every act because of it.
Gaze.strength: Split Enchantment arrives exactly when encounters start fielding pairs of dangerous bodies, and holding two of them off one concentration slot is the only way a two-character party covers both. Hypnotic Gaze costs no concentration at all, so the partner's slot stays free — and stripping an enemy caster's concentration is a two-for-one a duo cannot otherwise buy.
Gaze.wants: A body that converts a held enemy into a dead one; this chassis is rung 1 on single-target damage in all three acts and has nothing aimed at the partner.
uncertain: Hypnotic Gaze is a LONG-rest recharge, so it is one hold per fight across the cycle rather than a repeatable engine; that is what keeps ctrl_s at 4 rather than 5 before the 9th-tier slots arrive.
Hypnotic Gaze Breaks Concentration (22655) is explicit that it does not break the caster's own; the concentration strip is scored on the enemy side only.

Listo enemies are far more save-capable than vanilla and bosses carry magic resistance, which cuts against an enchantment plan specifically. Heightened Spell's disadvantage is the answer and it does not decay, but it costs sorcery points from a long-rest pool.
to_damage is 0.4 rather than 0.5 because the lockdown plan spends the pool on control; the ctrl rungs are priced against the other 0.6.

Sculptor.note: The safe default school, with a late Fighter level bought purely for medium armour and a shield on a d6 body. Empowered Evocation adds the Intelligence modifier to every Evocation damage roll from 10, which on a four-target spell is four times over.
Sculptor.strength: Sculpt Spells matters more with two characters than with four, because in a two-body party the partner is *always* inside your own Fireball — it converts the pair's biggest friendly-fire constraint into nothing. Adding Intelligence per damage roll also scales with instance count rather than with slot level, which is the direction the run's inflated HP rewards.
Sculptor.wants: A body that holds a second concentration slot and answers bosses; this one's single-target stays at par and its control is ordinary Wizard control.
uncertain: Empowered Evocation is applied as +Int to each damage ROLL, so four times on a four-target spell. If the install applies it once per cast instead, Act II and Act III aoe_raw fall by about 45 and 60 and Act III drops from rung 4 to 3.
Overchannel (14) is an interrupt maximising a 1st-5th Evocation spell with necrotic backlash; no use limit was recoverable, so it is not counted in the raws at all.

Fighter is taken after level 1, so it grants medium armour and shields but no heavy armour and no saves. Taking Fighter first would buy heavy armour at the cost of the Int/Wis save pair, which is the worse trade on a concentration body.
The split names no Bard College; Lore is assumed.

Hexbook.note: A Wizard that reads off the Warlock list: Eldritch Blast and four Eldritch Invocations on an Intelligence chassis, ritual casting turned into temporary hit points, and Heart of Darkness recovering a slot on every kill. Its defence is temp HP and charm immunity rather than armour or a ward.
Hexbook.strength: Slot economy is what actually limits a Wizard when a long rest costs 120+ supplies, and this is the only school that manufactures slots mid-fight. Eldritch Blast also gives it four separate damage rolls a turn instead of one, which is what the per-instance gear constant pays on — and level-10 immunity to the charm and fear line matters far more with two bodies than four, because losing either ends the run.
Hexbook.wants: A body that can take a hit and one that heals — this chassis has no rescue at all before Act III and no armour in any act.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is scored WITHOUT Agonizing Blast. The invocation adds the Charisma modifier and this chassis dumps Charisma; whether Hexcraft rescales it to Intelligence is not stated anywhere I could read. If it does rescale, Act III st rises by about 18 raw and the rung goes from 2 to 3.
Beam count follows the class-level cantrip rule: 2 beams at character 8, 3 at 15, 4 at 20 with Expansion's fourth. Eldritch Blast is 1d8 per beam in this install, not 1d10.

Level-10 immunity to emotion-altering conditions is a charm/fear immunity, not a save-category effect, so it takes no booster id — the same reasoning that keeps Bard Countercharm unregistered. It is real and unscored.
The split names no Bard College; Lore is assumed.

Scribe.note: The Wizard that carries the Cleric list: Sacred Flame and Word of Radiance as cantrips, Spirit Guardians as its area engine, Erudite Remedy as a bonus-action outward heal, and Warding Rejuvenation to pick a downed partner back up. Concentration goes to Spirit Guardians, so it never holds the pair's area control spell.
Scribe.strength: In a two-person run the fight-ending event is one character going down, and this is the only Wizard that both raises a downed ally on a short-rest clock and hands out on-demand elemental resistance as a bonus action — resistance the partner can be given before a known damage type lands. Spirit Guardians on an Intelligence caster is a damage floor that costs no further actions once it is up.
Scribe.wants: A body that holds the pair's area control, because this one's single concentration slot is permanently committed to Spirit Guardians.
uncertain: Spirit Guardians is one of the levelled casts, not an addition to them, and it holds this body's concentration for the fight — which is why ctrl_a is 3 rather than the 4 every other Wizard here reaches. Scoring it on both would be the double-claim the rubric forbids.
Erudite Remedy aimed at the partner is Rescue and aimed at self is Durability; it is counted once, in Rescue, with only the self-usable share entering the durability pool.
to_damage is 0.4 rather than 0.5 because the rescue plan spends the pool; the rsc rungs are priced against the other 0.6.
The split names no Bard College; Lore is assumed.

Mirage.note: The thinnest of the base schools: a bonus-action Minor Illusion, See Invisibility on a short rest, and one attack made to miss per rest at 10. The Swords Bard dip buys medium armour and Extra Attack, but the body's Dexterity is an afterthought, so it keeps casting.
Mirage.strength: Illusory Self is a genuine do-not-die button on a d6 chassis in a run where losing either character usually ends the fight, and See Invisibility on a short-rest clock costs no slot. Beyond that it is a plain Wizard, and the Wizard list is the deepest control pool in the game.
Mirage.wants: A body with a real lockdown tool, because this one's school does not supply one — its control is whatever the Wizard list offers and nothing above it.
uncertain: This chassis is filed under the lockdown niche but the school contributes nothing to either control axis; its ctrl rungs are the bare Wizard list. Scored at to_damage 0.5 rather than the 0.4 the other two lockdown wizards use, precisely because it has no deeper control pool to spend on.
The class file records that Listo's enemy overhaul makes Minor Illusion's pull far less reliable than in vanilla; nothing is scored for it.
College of Swords rather than Lore costs this body Persuasion proficiency, and the worst-check cap holds skl at 2 in Act III rather than 3. That is the dip choice showing up, not a scoring artefact.
The Swords Bard's Extra Attack is not used: two attacks at Dexterity 16 are worth less than one Fire Bolt, so all eight action-slots stay on casting.

Thrall.note: Animate Dead++ removes the cap on how many undead this body can hold, moves the free Animate Dead to 5, and extends Undead Thralls' hit points and damage bonus to every undead it owns; Shepherd totems buff the resulting crowd. Its own damage is an ordinary caster's — the bodies are the build.
Thrall.strength: Two players against encounters tuned for five is solved most directly by fielding four to eight extra bodies, and this is the one chassis in the list built to do exactly that at 9th-tier slots. The undead also benefit from short rests and can be healed normally, so the set persists across fights instead of being re-bought every long rest.
Thrall.wants: A body that can hold a front line while the undead arrive, and one that heals — this chassis is rung 2-3 on durability and has almost nothing aimed at its partner.
uncertain: Undead damage is excluded from both damage axes per rule 2 and scored on Actions only. A reader comparing this row to Conjuration's will find them identical on st and aoe; the two chassis differ on Actions, Durability and Endurance, not on damage.

Rule 4's 0.5 resistance multiplier is NOT applied despite necrotic being the lead type, because the body also deals fire and force — the rule's own second-damage-type exemption. Unlike School of Death it has no resistance strip, so a necrotic-locked variant would be worse.

Inured to Undeath's necrotic resistance and the hit-point-maximum floor are folded into the durability ratio at about a 1.15x blended multiplier; the max-HP clause is binary and cannot be expressed as a ratio at all.
Circle of the Shepherd's Spirit Totem is scored only in Act III and only as an outward temp-HP source; the modded implementation's uptime was not read.

Quill.note: A Spectral Mind to cast through, Formulaic Attunement making the attuned damage type ignore resistance, and a three-level Hexblade dip for the only short-rest spell slots a Wizard can hold. Attunement cannot be changed during combat, so the type is a build-time pick.
Quill.strength: Every other Wizard's slots come back only on a rest that costs 120+ supplies; two pact slots refilling on the free rest are spent three times a cycle instead of once, and Eldritch Blast underneath them means the filler actions still deliver four separate damage rolls apiece. Ignoring resistance to one chosen type is the direct answer to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances.
Quill.wants: A front line and a healer — this is a robe with a spectral duplicate, rung 2 on durability throughout and nothing aimed at the partner.
uncertain: Eldritch Blast is scored WITHOUT Agonizing Blast — the invocation adds Charisma and this chassis dumps it. Beam count follows character level: four beams at 20, at 1d8 each in this install.
Formulaic Attunement's resistance-ignoring is credited but its 'a little extra damage' is not, because the exact bonus is images-only on the mod page and unrecoverable.
Levels for Wizardly Quill and Awakened Spellbook are unverified; the Spectral Mind is scored as one permanent extra body on Actions and nothing more.
The Warlock dip is worth two pact slots at 2nd level, not a caster tier — Act III caster level is 17, the lowest in the wizard batch, which is why its levelled-cast count is below its neighbours'.

Ordnance.note: Arcane Ordnance throws a slot-free bomb every round that lays its own surface, and from 14 the bomb rides a bonus action alongside a levelled cast. Salvo and Barrage do not work on the installed pak, so the school is judged on the three features that do.
Ordnance.strength: A persistent hazard laid every single turn, for no slot and no concentration, is area denial a duo cannot otherwise buy — and Saturating Fire at 14 moves it to the bonus action so both Actions stay free for control. Against encounters built for five bodies, terrain that keeps working while you cast is worth more than a second blast.
Ordnance.wants: A body that can absorb hits. This chassis has the thinnest defensive layer of any Wizard here — no ward, no stone, no armour — and no rescue before Act III.
uncertain: DEFECT CONFIRMED FROM THE PAK, not inherited. In DaelensTestament...pak Passive.txt, ArcaneOrdnance grants `ActionResource(Bombs,1,0)` and that is the only grant anywhere in the file; Salvo requires `HasActionResource('Bombs',2,...)` and adds `ModifyUseCosts(Add,Bombs,1,0)` on top of the bomb's own `Bombs:1`, so it costs 2; Salvo2/Barrage requires 3 and adds 2, so it costs 3. The ActionResourceDefinition for Bombs carries MaxLevel 0 and ReplenishType Rest. Both toggles are unreachable and neither is scored. Still unverified: whether any other pak in the 747-mod load grants Bombs.

Bombs are placed in `filler` in Acts I and II because they are at-will — ArcaneOrdnance restores the charge on any spell cast while empty, so one Action casting a spell refills the charge the other Action spends. Whether a bomb itself counts as a spell for that refill is unverified and does not change the result under two Actions.
The Big One is once per long rest, so a third of a fight's worth, and is not counted in the raws; it would add roughly 15 to Act III aoe_raw.
The 3m bomb radius is scored at 2 targets, against the 4 the AoE par assumes for a spell.
The split names no Bard College; Lore is assumed.

Reaper.note: Reaper doubles every single-target necromancy cantrip, and Improved Reaper at 14 does the same for 1st-to-5th-level necromancy spells, so this body's filler actions deliver twice the damage rolls anyone else's do. It has no defensive layer at all and it spends its Arcane Recovery on damage.
Reaper.strength: Inescapable Destruction makes its damage ignore necrotic resistance, which is the answer to Absolute Wrath for the one type that would otherwise be its worst liability — a single-type body that cannot be resisted is a genuinely different object from a single-type body that can. Doubling cantrips also doubles the instances the act's gear constant pays on.
Reaper.wants: Armour, healing, or both. This chassis is rung 2 on durability until Act III, has no rescue before it, and burns the recovery charges that would otherwise be its endurance.
uncertain: Rule 4's 0.5 resistance multiplier is NOT applied to this body despite necrotic being its dominant type, because Inescapable Destruction (6) states the damage ignores necrotic resistance. That exemption is the school's main claim and it comes from the mod page, not a pak read.
Negative Energy Infusion is counted once per round (once per turn, and the body takes one turn), at +1d8 to 10 and +2d8 from 14.
Touch of Death converts two Arcane Recovery charges into damage; it is not counted in the raws, and the endurance cost of doing so is why end stays at 2 in every act.
Artificer 1 is taken after level 1 and contributes light armour, shields and one half-caster level; the Act III caster level is 20 rather than 19 as a result.
The split names no Bard College; Lore is assumed.

Stonecut.note: The thinnest of the base schools, carried almost entirely by the Transmuter's Stone — one damage resistance, or Constitution save proficiency, held by whoever is wearing it. Bard 6 does more for this chassis than the school does.
Stonecut.strength: The stone is one of very few cross-character buffs a Wizard can simply hand over and leave equipped, which in a party of two means it covers half the party permanently for no action and no concentration. Against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances, a resistance you can re-choose after a long rest is a real answer.
Stonecut.wants: Almost anything with a damage engine or a front line — this is a support caster whose own school contributes one item.
uncertain: The Transmuter's Stone's Constitution save proficiency is NOT entered in `prof`: the schema's grant list is the level-1 class, Lone Wolf, Resilient, Slippery Mind and Diamond Soul, and there is no booster id for a transferable stone. On this body Con is already proficient, so nothing is lost here — but a pair sheet handing the stone to a partner without Con is scoring something the format cannot see.

rsc 2 in Acts I and II is the stone handed outward. It is a permanent buff rather than healing, which is what the rung-2 row describes, so it is scored a rung below where a heal of the same value would sit and the doubt is recorded here.
Experimental Alchemy does not stack with the Artificer's or any feat source, and the feat version was removed in v9.0.3; nothing is scored for it.
The damage block is identical to wizard/Abjuration:reaction because the school contributes nothing to damage. That is the finding, not an oversight.

Deflect.note: The gish-flavoured caster that is not Bladesinging: a reaction-based AC and save spike plus initiative, with a Stormcalling Bard dip for Chorus of Thunder and a bonus-action lightning cantrip. The per-level numbers behind Arcane Deflection, Tactical Wit, Power Surge and Durable Magic are images-only on the mod page and remain unverified.
Deflect.strength: Lone Wolf hands every body two Reactions and a caster normally owns one thing to spend them on; Arcane Deflection gives this one a second claim that fires on the turn it is attacked rather than on the turn it acts. Deflecting Shroud at 14 was rewritten to hit everything in the radius rather than three chosen targets, which is strictly better against the larger enemy counts a duo faces.
Deflect.wants: A front line, a healer, or both — this body defends itself with reactions and has nothing to spend on the partner until the Bard levels land.
uncertain: The whole subclass is scored from an images-only feature table. Arcane Deflection is credited with roughly +2 AC of effective value on a reaction and Durable Magic with nothing; if the real numbers are larger this chassis is under-scored on Durability by up to a rung, and if smaller its Act III dur 3 is wrong.

Arcane Deflection also spikes saving throws, which would deserve a booster id. None exists in the registry and I have not read a number to justify proposing one, so it contributes nothing to the saves axis.
Dispel Magic does not exist in BG3, so War Magic's dispel-flavoured feature uses Remove Curse instead; nothing is scored for it.

This body and wizard/Divination:reaction share a dip and a damage block. Divination's Portent is a readable, countable resource and War Magic's features are not, which is the only honest reason their reaction rungs differ.

title: Listo Pairing Ledger
lede: Which two bodies are worth building together. Every subclass in the modlist was swept, every split it can express was searched, and every promoted body was scored on ten axes across three acts — then paired with every other and ranked. The damage axes are not judgements: each carries the arithmetic it was derived from, so a re-based ladder re-derives the roster instead of stranding it.
footer: Listonomicon 10.2. Scores derived against axis-rubrics.md, scoring-model.md and gates.md; damage from stated per-act arithmetic. Claims marked settled were read from the installed paks.

Lectern.verdict: Two bodies that both want to be hit, standing next to each other. Lectern turns every landed attack into reflected radiant, every instance of that into a Constitution save, and every failed save into a spreading blind that then taxes whatever the blinded enemy tries to spend — an engine that costs no slot, no ki and no action, so it runs entirely on the turns the enemy takes. Silverward is what makes taking those turns survivable: flat damage reduction on every hit either character receives, a Channel Oath that halves everything landing on the other body, and temporary hit points topped up every round off a charge the short rest refunds. Resilience is the block carrying this pair, and it is the block that makes the engine sound rather than reckless.
Lectern.cost: Tempo is the thin half. Area damage is a genuine hole and Silverward is close to idle when the fight is a crowd, so the spreading blind is doing all the work a fireball would otherwise do. Both bodies hold concentration — and Lectern's is permanently spoken for by Friar's Bond, so the partner it asks for, one that does not need the slot, is not the partner it got; both also lean radiant, and both draw from the same weapon-and-armour pool.

vars.note: Trades the mitigation stack for at-will cone damage and a short-rest rescue kit, which answers the area hole at the cost of the pair's durability floor.
A second slot-free control engine beside this one, removing turns by a different mechanism and sharing no damage type — but the pair's floor then sits on a robe rather than on plate.

Dawnpact.verdict: Everything offensive Dawnpact does is at-will and slot-free, which leaves all three pact slots and the Cleric channel reserved for Revivify, Preserve Life and hard control — and every one of those refills on the free rest rather than the expensive one. Lectern is free in the same way, running its blind engine off being attacked instead of off any resource at all. Duration is what carries the pair: two bodies whose entire routines reload on a short rest is the most direct answer this ledger has to a long rest costing a fortune in supplies. Lectern also supplies the thing Dawnpact asks for and cannot buy — something standing between it and whatever is coming — while Dawnpact's cones cover Lectern's weak side.
Dawnpact.cost: The pair's durability floor is a robe caster, and the floor is the number that counts, so most of what Lectern's shield and morningstar buy is discarded. Both bodies hold concentration, and Lectern's is committed permanently, which parks the pair's only usable slot on its most fragile half. Both also deal radiant as their principal magical type, so one resistance blunts a large share of the pair's output at once.

Sleightweave.verdict: Sleightweave's real output is not its own. Haste on a partner with Extra Attack converts one concentration slot into an extra Action for the pair, and at two characters that is a far larger share of the party's economy than the same spell buys in four. Silverward is the right body to receive it: it asks for a partner that ends fights, and being Hasted is how it becomes the one ending them, while it repays the slot with three separate mitigation layers both characters stand inside. Utility is unusually strong here — Rogue expertise, a permanent invisible Mage Hand and two Charisma bodies leave very little out of combat closed to them.
Sleightweave.cost: Tempo is the weak block and the pair cannot hide it: area damage is a hole, Silverward is close to idle in a crowd, and Fireball has to be bought out of the same action slots Sleightweave would rather spend on Haste and Sneak Attack. The Haste is also a single point of failure — both bodies hold concentration, this one wears light armour, and a broken slot costs the partner a turn on top of the Action it was giving. The two draw from one weapon pool as well.

vars.text: Without the Metamagic: the Sorcerer block grants no saves, no armour and no skills — it is bought purely for third-level slots and the Quickened/Twinned pair. Drop those two picks and there is nothing left to justify the levels.

Vowbreaker.verdict: Two bodies built to delete one target, one of which is also the party's face. Vowbreaker is the rare genuinely single-stat paladin — Hex Warrior puts Charisma on the blade — and Vow of Enmity makes advantage a routine condition off a charge the short rest refunds rather than a once-a-fight opener, stacked on Hexblade's Curse and superiority dice. Duelbrand's Rakish Audacity lands Sneak Attack without the flanking body a duo does not have, and adds Dirty Tricks and a second Charisma voice on top. The concentration question resolves cleanly for once: Vowbreaker holds none at all, which is exactly the partner Duelbrand asks for from the moment Spirit Guardians goes up.
Vowbreaker.cost: Area damage is the hole, and Vowbreaker names it itself — Duelbrand's answer is one concentration spell that also asks a light-armour body to stand in the middle of the enemies. Tempo is the thin block overall: this pair is excellent at removing one enemy and slow at removing several, which is the wrong shape for the encounters the modlist inflates. Duelbrand's subclass also stops growing well short of the cap, and the two compete for the same blades and the same Charisma items.

Galvanic.verdict: Tempo is the block carrying this pair, and both halves of it are pure offence. Galvanic is the one Barbarian whose damage keys off the stat it was already maxing for hit points and Unarmoured Defence, so the second Bonus Action Lone Wolf hands out turns straight into output instead of queueing behind Rage — and it brings a real second damage type on every swing plus an area burst. Spitegrave adds Aura of Protection over both bodies' saves and Spiteful Suffering, advantage against the marked target for everyone, off a short-rest charge. Only one of them holds concentration, which matters more than it sounds in a set where most pairs hold two.
Galvanic.cost: Two of the three things Spitegrave offers a partner land badly on this one: Galvanic already generates its own advantage through Reckless Attack, and Aura of Hate adds nothing to a body that is neither undead nor a fiend. The damage types overlap twice — both swing slashing, both carry lightning — and Spitegrave's stated want, a radiant or force type for the Act II matchup, goes unmet. Utility is the thin block; nobody here is scouting or talking their way past anything, and Galvanic spent Lone Wolf's proficiencies on Constitution, so its save coverage leans on the partner's aura.

vars.text: The Dexterity line: taking Lone Wolf's proficiencies on the usual Dexterity pair instead widens the save set, but every number this subclass produces keys off the Constitution modifier, so the trade buys coverage with output.

Portent.verdict: Portent does not remove enemies, it decides which rolls happen: dice that replace an attack roll or a saving throw made nearby, spent as reactions on a run that hands every body two of them, and refunded on the free rest rather than the expensive one. Against two characters and one boss, turning the save that decides the fight frequently is the fight, and the pool never argues with the pair's concentration. Silverward is both halves of what Portent asks for — a front line and a healer — and resilience is what carries the pairing as a result.
Portent.cost: Duration is the weak block: Portent runs on a Wizard's levelled slots, and a pair that wants to rest is a pair spending supplies it cannot afford. Silverward is close to idle when the fight is a crowd, so the crowd side rests on a Bard-dip cantrip and whatever slots Portent can spare from turning dice. Both bodies hold concentration.

Feylock.verdict: Two control engines that never touch a concentration slot, which is the exact bind a duo hits once the encounter mods start adding bodies. Fey Presence is an area charm-or-fear on a short-rest clock, Repelling Blast lands every turn for nothing, and Lectern's blind propagates off attacks the enemy chose to make. Duration is the block carrying the pair, because almost nothing either body does is drawn from the long-rest pool. Their damage types are also entirely disjoint, which under layered resistances is worth more than the raw output suggests.
Feylock.cost: Resilience is the thin block, and the pair's floor is its weaker body: Feylock is a robe that dies to anything that reaches it, so Lectern's shield and armour raise nothing but Lectern. Lectern asks for single-target damage against a boss and does not really get it — Feylock spends a large share of its action slots on pact-slot control, which is precisely what holds its boss damage down. Both bodies hold concentration on top of that.

Wardkeep.verdict: Wardkeep exists to spend reactions on the other character, and at two characters the other character is half of everything. Projected Ward moves the wizard's ward in front of the body actually taking hits, Improved Abjuration refills that pool on the free rest, and a Barbarian level gives the wizard a floor it would otherwise never wear. Spitegrave is the offence the wizard asks for, and the wizard is — unusually — the answer to Spitegrave's own stated want: its smites are wholly necrotic and it needs a force or radiant type beside it, which this body carries. Tempo is the block carrying the pair, and all of it comes from one half.
Wardkeep.cost: Duration is the weak block and it is structural: a Wizard's slots and a Paladin's smites both draw on the long-rest pool, and this run charges a fortune for that rest. Wardkeep adds nothing at all to damage by its own admission, so a fight going badly for Spitegrave has no second engine behind it. Both bodies hold concentration.

vars.note: Swaps the necrotic smiter for a paladin that already brings concentration-free crowd control and an aura over both save sets, at the price of the single-target damage this wizard cannot supply itself.

Interpose.verdict: A caster with four separate claims on a reaction — Projected Ward, Counterspell, Shield and Cutting Words — on a run that hands every body two of them every round. The second reaction is normally dead weight on a wizard that owns only Counterspell; here both are spent every round, two of the four point at the partner rather than at itself, and Counterspell is the answer a duo has no other way to buy when the modlist adds an enemy caster. Spitegrave supplies the entire boss side of the pairing and hands out advantage against its marked target to both bodies off a charge the short rest refunds.
Interpose.cost: Duration is the weak block: two long-rest pools, slots and smites, against a rest priced in supplies the run cannot spare. There is no armour anywhere in this build, so the reaction menu is only worth what the front line is worth, and its own single-target damage never clears par — every fight has to be ended by the other half. Both bodies hold concentration.

vars.text: Armour instead of reactions: the same Abjuration core can spend a level and a feat on Unarmoured Defence and a short-rest Inspiration heal rather than on Lore's Cutting Words and Magical Secrets. The ward survives longer; the enemy caster gets one more turn.

Crownguard.verdict: BG3 has no aggro table, so enemy AI walks past the plate and goes for the softer body — and a Lone Wolf duo has exactly one softer body. Crown's Channel Oath is the only taunt in the roster: it forces the attack onto the character in heavy armour carrying Aura of Protection, and Riposte converts every forced miss into a free reaction attack, with two reactions a round to spend them from. Duelbrand is what that protection is for — Rakish Audacity lands Sneak Attack with no flanking partner available — and Crownguard holds no concentration at all, which is precisely the partner Duelbrand asks for once Spirit Guardians goes up. Utility is maxed between two Charisma voices and a Rogue's expertise.
Crownguard.cost: Area damage is the hole and Crownguard is close to idle in a crowd — its area game is cleave and nothing else, which is the want it names and does not get here. The pair's only crowd answer is Duelbrand's concentration spell, which asks a light-armour body to stand inside the enemies its partner has just pulled onto itself. Both lean radiant, and both want the same blades.

Dreadchoir.verdict: Dreadchoir stacks two crowd answers that cost no concentration — Conquering Presence off a short-rest Channel Oath, and Concussion, which drops a target prone and strips its reactions and all but one of its actions — then hands the partner its Charisma modifier on every saving throw through an aura that, at two characters, covers the entire party. Wardkeep layers rather than duplicates: Projected Ward moves the wizard's ward onto whichever body is being hit, Spell Resistance covers what the aura does not, and the ward reloads on the free rest. Resilience is where this pairing lives, and it lives there comfortably.
Dreadchoir.cost: Nothing here ends a fight. Dreadchoir asks for real single-target damage and Wardkeep is the wrong body to ask, so the boss side of this pair rests on a rapier and a shield — and against inflated hit points, a fight that will not end is a fight in which the mitigation eventually runs out. Duration is the weak block on top of that, both bodies hold concentration, and Dreadchoir's Bard block arrives late enough that Concussion is an Act III addition only.

Thrall.verdict: The most direct answer to two players facing encounters tuned for five is to stop being two. Animate Dead++ removes the cap on how many undead this body holds and extends Undead Thralls' hit points and damage to all of them, Shepherd totems buff the result, and the set survives short rests and ordinary healing instead of being re-bought every long rest. Aria is the multiplier on the other side: one Action buys a whole fight of area lightning that degrades every caught enemy's Constitution save while sharpening the partner's crits, then cashes out as a mass stun, with Chorus of Thunder's Concussion as slot-free hard control underneath. Tempo carries the pairing, and this is the one entry here where the crowded side of the field is yours.
Thrall.cost: Durability is a genuine hole — two robe casters, nothing that can interpose, and a wall of undead does not stop what simply walks through it. Neither body brings much aimed at the other: Thrall asks for a front line and a healer and gets neither, and both hold concentration, which is uncomfortable when one of them is holding a fight-long aria. They also draw on the same caster gear pool, though their damage types at least stay disjoint, which is the one thing Aria explicitly needed.

cards.title: The unit is the subclass
cards.body: The work-list is derived from the class files, not from a list anyone maintains — 150 subclasses cleared as candidates, seven excluded and named below. A subclass is not one chassis: where a body has two honest expressions, both are scored.

cards.title: The split is searched, not guessed
cards.body: A sweep agent's split is a hypothesis written while looking at one class. Every split each subclass can express was enumerated and ranked, then a judgement pass decided which variants are genuinely different bodies. Sixty-nine of the roster's splits kept the sweep's guess — the search minimises the primary class, which cuts below the level-14 capstones that are the subclass for a Beast Barbarian or a Rune Knight, and it cannot see that Rage switches off the casting it buys.

cards.title: Damage is computed, not judged
cards.body: Each chassis states its per-act arithmetic: eight action-slots that must add up, pools with their refresh clock, the fraction of levelled slots spent on damage, and how many separate damage rolls a round it makes. The rung is the ratio to a fixed par. A round can no longer be scored at zero, a short-rest pool can no longer be priced as a long-rest one, and a many-roll engine is no longer priced as if gear were worth the same to it as to a one-lump spell.

cards.title: Saves and skills are evidence, not rungs
cards.body: The saves axis is derived from the resulting proficiency set plus a closed booster registry; the pair's Skills is recomputed from a per-act modifier map. Both fail closed: an unrecognised booster raises rather than scoring as nothing.

cards.title: Verified against the installed paks
cards.body: Where a claim was load-bearing it was read from the archive rather than a mod page. That overturned one convention outright — Great Weapon Master pairs its damage rider with an accuracy penalty and is a net loss from Act II, which had been over-crediting every melee body in the roster.

items: cleric/Heavy armour / martial weapon table (the dip-planning summary) — The heading is the domain-by-domain proficiency table used for dip planning, not a playable domain.
inquisitor/Tactics Inquisition — The subclass lands at level 3, where the shipped install has a dangling subclass GUID; the mod needs updating to 2.2.1.
inquisitor/Vengeance Inquisition — Unreachable: Inquisitor is unusable past level 2 on the shipped install because of the dangling level-3 subclass GUID; needs the mod updated to 2.2.1.
inquisitor/Zeal Inquisition — Every feature sits at Inquisitor 3 or later, and the shipped install breaks at level 3 on a dangling GUID; needs updating to 2.2.1.

monk/Way of the Four Elements (vanilla) — Its best expression is the elemental Monk body, which Warrior of the Elements does strictly better; the class file says it is superseded in almost every respect.
paladin/Supporting library — A note about Oath Framework, a developer-facing API mod with no player-facing features and no selectable oath of its own.
sorcerer/Wretched Soul — The mod ships no feature list: levels, progression and Vile Affliction's effect are all unverified, and Listo added the pack for testing only.
excluded.lead: Three of these are the Inquisitor's, which the shipped install cannot take past level 2 because of a dangling subclass GUID at level 3.

settled.summary: Settled by reading the installed paks
items: Great Weapon Master and Sharpshooter pair +3/+5/+7/+9/+11 damage with a −2/−3/−4/−5/−6 attack penalty on the same passive. The penalty does not cancel against par, which carries no damage feat: the feat is a wash in Act I and a loss from Act II. It defaults on, so every melee body is scored with it toggled off.

5e Reckless Attack restores the RAW Strength gate — a Dexterity body gets no advantage at all, and a Hex Warrior or Shillelagh body loses it too, because the clause keys on the ability that actually rolled.
Heavy Armour Master reduces all damage in this install, not just physical, on a level map reaching −5 at character 13.

School of Bombardment's Salvo and Barrage are unreachable. The only grant of Bombs anywhere in the pak gives one charge; Salvo requires and spends two, Barrage three. Requirement and cost agree, so it is a coherent design dropped onto the wrong pool and no configuration rescues it.

Warrior of the Elements — Elemental Burst is a real four-target save-for-half area spell, but it consumes the whole Action where Ascendant Dragon's Breath replaces one attack of the Attack action. It buys an area rung by spending a single-target one.

assumptions.summary: Assumptions that would still move numbers
items: Both top damage bands are mis-set and are shipping as scored. Area rung 5 asks for three times par, which is between one and two four-target Fireballs per round — no chassis in the roster reaches it in any act. Single-target rung 2 holds half the field. Because every chassis stores the arithmetic rather than the rung, re-basing either ladder re-derives the whole roster without re-scoring anything, and that is the next change due.
The illithid pool is split evenly between the two bodies. A pair sheet may deviate; concentrating it lifts one body and lowers the other.
Act III proficiency bonus is pinned at +5 in every skills map, rather than derived from character level.

Reliable Talent enters the skills map as +2 and advantage on a named skill as +3 — rounded down from exact expectation lifts of +2.25 and +3.325, since the map holds modifiers and neither effect is one.
Where the split search chose a generic dip, the scoring pass picked the subclass. A body reading Cleric 6 carries no domain in its split; the domain chosen is named in that chassis's note.

Four seeds are mis-filed rather than mis-scored and are scored as their split actually reads: Knowledge's Expertise lands on checks the Skills axis does not score, Life's Barbarian dip is unusable on any round it casts, Trickery's duplicates and Spirit Guardians both need concentration, and Shadow Magic stops one level short of Umbral Form.
